description:
## Context

Phase 3.1 of the bounded-memory filesystem connector epic (gossip-8936). The previous phases establish:
- **Phase 1.1** (gossip-8936.3): Per-directory sorted readdir so the DFS walk produces globally sorted output
- **Phase 1.2** (gossip-8936.1): Spill-to-disk when the walk buffer exceeds memory limits — produces a merged run file of sorted `FileEntry` records
- **Phase 1.3** (gossip-8936.2): `SortedIndex` abstraction that lets the serving layer operate identically over `InMemory` and `OnDisk` representations

This task implements the **`OnDisk` variant** of `SortedIndex`: a compact binary index format that replaces the mmap'd merged run file from Phase 1.2 with a properly structured on-disk index supporting O(log N) binary search by key, zero-copy page iteration via `memmap2`, and a prefix-sum section for O(log N) split-point selection.

**Why a dedicated index format rather than just mmap'ing the merged run file?**

The Phase 1.2 merged run file stores variable-length records sequentially. Binary search requires O(1) access to the key at any position, which variable-length records cannot provide without an auxiliary structure. A dedicated index format separates fixed-stride metadata (offsets, sizes, IDs) from variable-length keys, enabling random access into sorted data via a single mmap.

## Current State

### SortedIndex enum (after Phase 1.3 — gossip-8936.2)

Phase 1.3 defines the `SortedIndex` enum with `InMemory` fully functional and `OnDisk` as a placeholder:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs (after Phase 1.3)
pub(crate) enum SortedIndex {
    InMemory {
        files: Vec<FileEntry>,
        prefix_sums: Vec<u64>,
    },
    OnDisk {
        // Phase 3 placeholder — this task fills it in.
        // todo!("Phase 3: on-disk index format")
    },
}
```

### FileEntry fields that must be queryable from the on-disk index (`filesystem.rs:248-266`)

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:248-266
struct FileEntry {
    key: ItemKey,                   // variable-length, up to 4096 bytes
    stable_item_id: StableItemId,   // 32 bytes (define_id_32! macro)
    version: VersionId,             // 1 byte tag (Strong=0, Weak=1) + 32 bytes ObjectVersionId
    size: u64,                      // 8 bytes
}
```

### Consumers of the SortedIndex (all must work transparently with OnDisk)

| Consumer | File:Line | What it needs |
|----------|-----------|---------------|
| `enumerate_page_bounds` | `filesystem.rs:484-543` | `lower_bound(key)`, `upper_bound(key)`, `key_bytes(idx)`, `stable_item_id(idx)`, `version(idx)`, `size(idx)` |
| `choose_split_point_bounds` | `filesystem.rs:578-605` | `lower_bound(key)`, `upper_bound(key)`, `key_bytes(idx)`, prefix-sum `partition_point` |
| `byte_weighted_split_idx` | `filesystem.rs:612-639` | `prefix_sums[idx]`, `prefix_sums[start..end].partition_point()` |
| `verify_membership` | `filesystem.rs:645-657` | `binary_search_by_key(key)` |

### Git pack-index v2 format (reference pattern — `scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs:104-139`)

```text
+----------------+
| Magic (4B)     |  0xff 't' 'O' 'c'
| Version (4B)   |  Big-endian 2
+----------------+
| Fanout (1024B) |  256 * u32 BE cumulative counts
+----------------+
| OID Table      |  N * oid_len bytes (sorted)
+----------------+
| CRC Table      |  N * 4 bytes
+----------------+
| Offset Table   |  N * 4 bytes (MSB=1 → large offset)
+----------------+
| Large Offsets  |  M * 8 bytes (optional)
+----------------+
| Pack Checksum  |  oid_len bytes
| Idx Checksum   |  oid_len bytes
+----------------+
```

### MIDX builder pattern (reference — `scanner-git/src/midx_build.rs:1-48`)

The `midx_build.rs` module already demonstrates the full pattern for building a binary index format:
- Magic bytes + version header
- Chunk table with offsets to each section
- Fanout array (256 * u32, cumulative prefix-sum for first-byte buckets)
- Fixed-stride entry tables
- Validates output by re-parsing it via `MidxView::parse`
- Returns `BytesView` (mmap or owned) via `scanner-git/src/bytes.rs`

### BytesView abstraction (`scanner-git/src/bytes.rs:15-78`)

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/bytes.rs:15-78
pub struct BytesView {
    inner: BytesInner,
}

enum BytesInner {
    Mmap(Arc<Mmap>),    // Production: zero-copy via mmap
    Owned(Arc<[u8]>),   // Simulation/test: owned bytes
}

impl BytesView {
    pub fn from_mmap(mmap: Mmap) -> Self { ... }
    pub fn from_vec(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self { ... }
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] { ... }
}
```

### StableItemId — 32-byte fixed-width (`gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs:414-432`)

Pure function of `(ConnectorTag, key_bytes)` via BLAKE3. Can be re-derived from key bytes without storing in the index, BUT re-derivation has a per-entry cost (one BLAKE3 hash per entry during page assembly). Storing it avoids this cost at the expense of 32 bytes per entry in the index.

### VersionId — 1 byte tag + 32 bytes payload (`gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:711-738`)

```rust
pub enum VersionId {
    Strong(ObjectVersionId),   // tag = 0
    Weak(ObjectVersionId),     // tag = 1
}
```

For filesystem connector, always `Weak`. `ObjectVersionId` is derived from `(mtime, mtime_nsec, len, ino, dev)` — 40 bytes of metadata hashed to 32 bytes via BLAKE3 (`filesystem.rs:1373-1381`). This CANNOT be re-derived without re-stat'ing the file, so it MUST be stored in the index.

## Desired State

### On-disk binary index format

Design a compact binary format with these sections:

```text
+================================+
| HEADER (48 bytes)              |
|   magic: [u8; 4] = b"FSIX"    |  Filesystem IndeX
|   version: u16 BE              |  = 1
|   flags: u16 BE                |  Reserved (0)
|   entry_count: u64 BE          |
|   total_bytes: u64 BE          |  Sum of all entry sizes (for split-point validation)
|   entries_offset: u64 BE       |  Byte offset of fixed-stride entries section
|   keys_offset: u64 BE          |  Byte offset of variable-length keys section
|   prefix_sums_offset: u64 BE   |  Byte offset of prefix-sum section
+================================+
| FIXED-STRIDE ENTRIES (N * 78B) |
|   Per entry:                   |
|     key_offset: u32 BE         |  Offset into keys section
|     key_len: u16 BE            |  Length of key bytes
|     stable_item_id: [u8; 32]   |  StableItemId (pre-derived)
|     version_tag: u8            |  0=Strong, 1=Weak
|     version_id: [u8; 32]       |  ObjectVersionId bytes
|     size: u64 BE               |  File size
+================================+
| VARIABLE-LENGTH KEYS           |
|   Concatenated key bytes       |
|   (no separators — offsets     |
|    from entry table)           |
+================================+
| PREFIX-SUM SECTION (N * 8B)    |
|   prefix_sums[i]: u64 BE      |  = sum(size[0..=i])
+================================+
| CHECKSUM (32B)                 |
|   BLAKE3(all preceding bytes)  |
+================================+
```

**Fixed-stride entry size = 4 + 2 + 32 + 1 + 32 + 8 = 79 bytes per entry.**

**Why store StableItemId instead of re-deriving?** The enumerate hot path (page assembly at `filesystem.rs:524-528`) reads `file.stable_item_id` per entry. Re-deriving requires one BLAKE3 hash per entry per page. At 1000 items/page, that is 1000 BLAKE3 invocations per `enumerate` call. Storing 32 bytes per entry in the index eliminates this cost. The 32 bytes is a small fraction of the ~79-byte fixed stride.

**Why store VersionId?** Version is derived from file metadata (`mtime`, `ino`, `dev`, `len`). Re-deriving would require re-stat'ing every file during page assembly — O(page_size) syscalls in the hot path. Unacceptable.

**Why prefix-sum section?** `byte_weighted_split_idx` (`filesystem.rs:612-639`) does `partition_point` over a contiguous `u64` slice. The prefix-sum section provides this as a contiguous mmap'd region, enabling O(log N) split-point selection with zero memory beyond the mmap.

### `FsIndexView` — zero-copy view over the on-disk index

```rust
/// Zero-copy view over an on-disk filesystem sorted index.
///
/// Analogous to `IdxView` (pack_idx.rs) and `MidxView` (midx.rs) —
/// all slices reference the underlying `BytesView` which may be mmap'd.
pub(crate) struct FsIndexView {
    data: BytesView,         // Owns the mmap/owned bytes
    entry_count: u64,
    total_bytes: u64,
    entries: Range<usize>,   // Byte range of fixed-stride entries section
    keys: Range<usize>,      // Byte range of variable-length keys section
    prefix_sums: Range<usize>, // Byte range of prefix-sum section
}
```

### Operations on `FsIndexView`

| Method | Implementation | Complexity |
|--------|---------------|------------|
| `len() -> u64` | Return `self.entry_count` | O(1) |
| `key_bytes(idx) -> &[u8]` | Read `key_offset`/`key_len` from entry[idx], slice into keys section | O(1) |
| `stable_item_id(idx) -> StableItemId` | Read 32 bytes from entry[idx] offset 6 | O(1) |
| `version(idx) -> VersionId` | Read tag byte + 32 bytes from entry[idx] offset 38 | O(1) |
| `size(idx) -> u64` | Read u64 from entry[idx] offset 71 | O(1) |
| `prefix_sum(idx) -> u64` | Read u64 from prefix_sums[idx * 8] | O(1) |
| `lower_bound(key) -> usize` | Binary search over entries by key_bytes | O(log N) |
| `upper_bound(key) -> usize` | Binary search over entries by key_bytes | O(log N) |
| `binary_search_by_key(key) -> Result<usize, usize>` | Binary search over entries by key_bytes | O(log N) |
| `prefix_sums_partition_point(range, pred) -> usize` | Binary search over prefix-sum slice | O(log N) |

### `FsIndexBuilder` — builds the on-disk index from sorted entries

Consumes a sorted iterator of `(key_bytes, stable_item_id, version, size)` tuples and writes the binary format to a `Vec<u8>` (or file via `BufWriter`). Two construction paths:

1. **In-memory build** (`build_to_vec`): For moderate datasets that fit in RAM after the merge. Returns `BytesView::from_vec(bytes)`.
2. **Streaming build** (`build_to_file`): For large datasets. Writes to a temp file, then mmap's the result. Returns `BytesView::from_mmap(mmap)`.

Both paths validate the output by parsing it with `FsIndexView::parse()` before returning (same as `midx_build.rs:254-257`).

### Integration with `SortedIndex::OnDisk`

```rust
pub(crate) enum SortedIndex {
    InMemory { files: Vec<FileEntry>, prefix_sums: Vec<u64> },
    OnDisk(FsIndexView),
}
```

### Integration with Phase 1.2 spill-to-disk

After the k-way merge of spill runs (Phase 1.2), instead of materializing the merged output into `Vec<FileEntry>` (which defeats the bounded-memory goal), the merge output is streamed directly into `FsIndexBuilder`:

```
walk → spill buffer → sorted runs → k-way merge → FsIndexBuilder → FsIndexView → SortedIndex::OnDisk
```

For small datasets that fit in the in-memory buffer (no spilling), the existing `SortedIndex::InMemory` path is used unchanged.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create/Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/fs_index.rs` (NEW) | `FsIndexView`, `FsIndexBuilder`, `FsIndexError`, format constants, parse/build logic | Core on-disk index format — separate module for clarity (follows `pack_idx.rs`, `midx.rs` pattern) |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs` | Fill in `SortedIndex::OnDisk(FsIndexView)` variant; implement all `SortedIndex` methods for `OnDisk` | Integration with serving layer |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs` | Import `BytesView` from `scanner-git/src/bytes.rs` OR create a local copy in `gossip-connectors` | BytesView is needed for mmap abstraction |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/Cargo.toml` | Add `memmap2` dependency | Required for mmap |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/mod.rs` or `lib.rs` | Add `mod fs_index;` | Module registration |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem_tests.rs` | Add tests for `FsIndexView`, `FsIndexBuilder`, round-trip property tests | Validation |

### Decision: BytesView reuse vs local copy

`BytesView` lives in `scanner-git/src/bytes.rs`. Options:

**Option A (recommended): Move BytesView to `gossip-stdx`** — It is a general-purpose mmap/owned byte abstraction with no git-specific dependencies. Moving it to `gossip-stdx` makes it available to all crates. This is a small, low-risk refactor (move 90 lines, update imports in `scanner-git`).

**Option B: Copy BytesView into gossip-connectors** — Violates duplication-prevention policy. Avoid.

**Option C: Add gossip-connectors dependency on scanner-git** — Wrong dependency direction (connectors should not depend on git scanner internals).

Recommend Option A. If that is too much scope for this task, use Option B as a temporary measure with a TODO to deduplicate.

### Patterns to Follow

| Pattern | Reference | Apply to |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Zero-copy view struct with section slices | `IdxView` (`pack_idx.rs:131-139`) | `FsIndexView` |
| Magic + version + section offset header | `midx_build.rs:136-154` | FSIX header |
| Fixed-stride entry table with big-endian fields | `pack_idx.rs:107-125` (OID table + offset table) | Entry table |
| Fanout/prefix-sum for O(log N) bucket search | `midx_build.rs:419-506` | Prefix-sum section |
| Build-then-validate pattern | `midx_build.rs:254-257` | `FsIndexBuilder` validates via `FsIndexView::parse()` |
| `BytesView` return type | `midx_build.rs:258` | `FsIndexBuilder` returns `BytesView` |
| Section range validation during parse | `pack_idx.rs:151-250` | `FsIndexView::parse()` validates all section bounds |

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `BytesView` | `scanner-git/src/bytes.rs` | Move to `gossip-stdx` or copy temporarily |
| `memmap2::Mmap` | `scanner-git/Cargo.toml` | Add to `gossip-connectors/Cargo.toml` |

```rust
Ok(BytesView::from_vec(midx_bytes))
```

```rust
out.push(
    ScanItem::new(item_key, item_ref, file.stable_item_id, file.version)
        .with_size_hint(file.size),

```


```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/bytes.rs:28-36 — BytesView mmap construction

    Self { inner: BytesInner::Mmap(Arc::new(mmap)) }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:1373-1381 — VersionId derivation (must store, not re-derive)
fn derive_fs_version_id(metadata: &fs::Metadata) -> ObjectVersionId {
    let mut encoded = [0u8; 40];
    encoded[0..8].copy_from_slice(&metadata.mtime().to_be_bytes());
    encoded[8..16].copy_from_slice(&metadata.mtime_nsec().to_be_bytes());
    encoded[16..24].copy_from_slice(&metadata.len().to_be_bytes());
    encoded[24..32].copy_from_slice(&metadata.ino().to_be_bytes());
    encoded[32..40].copy_from_slice(&metadata.dev().to_be_bytes());
    ObjectVersionId::from_version_bytes(&encoded)

```

## Design Notes

### Entry stride: 79 bytes (not power-of-2)

79 bytes is compact but not cache-line-aligned (64B). For binary search, only ~17 entries are touched for 1B files (log₂(10⁹) ≈ 30 comparisons, but each touches one entry). Cache-line splits are acceptable for the search path. If profiling shows cache-line misses are significant, padding to 80 bytes (1 byte reserved) is a trivial future change.

### Key section layout: concatenated, no alignment

Keys are variable-length path bytes. Concatenating them without padding minimizes total size. Each key is accessed via `(key_offset, key_len)` from the entry table. No alignment requirements since key comparison is byte-by-byte.

### Prefix-sum section: contiguous u64 array

The `partition_point` call in `byte_weighted_split_idx` requires a contiguous slice of `u64`. The prefix-sum section provides exactly this. In the mmap case, the slice is `&[u8]` and must be read as big-endian u64 values. Two options:

**Option A (recommended): Binary search with per-element BE decode.** Each `partition_point` comparison reads 8 bytes and calls `u64::from_be_bytes`. The total number of comparisons is O(log N), so the decode cost is negligible.

**Option B: Load entire prefix-sum range into a temp Vec.** Unnecessary allocation; contradicts zero-copy goal.

### Checksum section

BLAKE3 over all preceding bytes. Verified on `parse()`. This catches corruption from disk errors or truncation. If checksum verification is too expensive for the hot path (parse is called once on construction, not per-page), it can be gated behind a flag. Follow the MIDX builder pattern of zeroing checksums in tests for simplicity.

### File size estimation

For 1B files with average 80-byte keys:
- Header: 48 bytes
- Entries: 1B × 79B = 79 GB
- Keys: 1B × 80B = 80 GB
- Prefix sums: 1B × 8B = 8 GB
- Total: ~167 GB

This is large but the entire point is that it is on disk, not in memory. The mmap'd view pages in only what is needed. Binary search touches ~30 × 79B ≈ 2.4 KB of entries and ~30 × (variable key len) of keys per lookup — comfortably within L1 cache working set.

### Why not a fanout table like Git pack-index?

Git's fanout (256 × u32) works because OIDs have uniform first-byte distribution. Filesystem path keys do NOT have uniform first-byte distribution (most start with lowercase ASCII letters). A fanout table would provide minimal speedup and waste 1 KB. Binary search over the full entry table is O(log N) and sufficient.

**Future optimization:** If profiling shows binary search is too slow for very large indexes (>1B entries), add an optional sampling-based interpolation search or a 256-entry fanout on the first key byte. This is out of scope for v1.

## Risk Analysis

- **Endianness**: All fields are big-endian, matching the Git pack-index convention and the existing codebase (`midx_build.rs`, `pack_idx.rs`). No endianness issues on any platform.
- **Index file corruption**: BLAKE3 checksum detects corruption. Parse validates all section bounds before returning a view.
- **Concurrent modification**: The index file is written once and never modified. The mmap is read-only (`Mmap::map`, not `MmapMut`). No concurrency issues.
- **Temp file cleanup**: Same `Drop`-based cleanup as Phase 1.2 spill files. The `FsIndexView` owns the `BytesView` which owns the `Arc<Mmap>` which keeps the mapping alive.
- **Address space exhaustion**: On 64-bit systems, mmap'ing 167 GB is fine (virtual address space is 256 TB). On 32-bit systems, this would fail — but 32-bit is not a target platform (confirmed by existing mmap usage in `midx_build.rs`).

## Performance Considerations

- **Binary search over mmap**: ~30 page faults for a cold search over 1B entries. After warmup, frequently-accessed pages stay in the page cache. This is the standard database index access pattern.
- **Page assembly**: Each page touches ~1000 contiguous entries (sequential access pattern). The OS read-ahead will prefetch subsequent pages, making this effectively sequential I/O.
- **Prefix-sum search**: O(log N) with per-comparison 8-byte BE decode. Negligible overhead.
- **Allocation tier**: `FsIndexView::parse()` is COLD (called once on construction). `key_bytes(idx)`, `stable_item_id(idx)`, `lower_bound(key)`, etc. are HOT (called per-page/per-split). HOT methods must be allocation-free — they return slices into the mmap.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Unit tests for `FsIndexBuilder`**: Build from known entries, verify byte layout matches expected format
2. **Unit tests for `FsIndexView::parse`**: Parse known-good bytes, verify all field accessors
3. **Round-trip test**: Build → parse → verify all entries match input
4. **Property test (proptest)**: Arbitrary sorted `Vec<(key, stable_id, version, size)>`, build → parse → verify:
   - `len()` matches input count
   - `key_bytes(i)` matches input key for all i
   - `lower_bound(key)` matches `partition_point` on input vec
   - `upper_bound(key)` matches `partition_point` on input vec
   - `prefix_sum(i)` matches cumulative sum of input sizes
   - `prefix_sums_partition_point` matches `partition_point` on cumulative sums
5. **Corruption tests**: Truncated file, bad magic, bad version, section overlap → verify parse error
6. **Checksum test**: Flip one byte → verify parse rejects
7. **Integration test**: Wire `SortedIndex::OnDisk` through `enumerate_page_bounds` and `choose_split_point_bounds` with a small dataset → verify identical results to `InMemory`
8. **Large-scale test**: Build index with 100K entries, verify O(log N) binary search correctness
9. **All existing 108+ filesystem tests pass unchanged** (they use small datasets → `InMemory` path)

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8936 | Bounded-memory filesystem connector for TB-PB scale enumeration | **Parent epic** |
| gossip-8936.2 | SortedIndex abstraction for in-memory and on-disk filesystem index | **Direct dependency** — defines the `SortedIndex` enum and `OnDisk` placeholder this task fills |
| gossip-8936.1 | Bounded-memory spill-to-disk for filesystem index | **Dependency** — produces the sorted run file that this task's `FsIndexBuilder` consumes |
| gossip-8936.3 | Per-directory sorted readdir in filesystem walker | **Indirect dependency** — ensures walk output is sorted, enabling streaming build |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `FsIndexView` struct provides zero-copy read access to all index fields via mmap'd `BytesView`
- [ ] `FsIndexBuilder` constructs valid index bytes from a sorted entry iterator (both `build_to_vec` and `build_to_file` paths)
- [ ] Binary format: FSIX header (48B) + fixed-stride entries (79B each) + variable-length keys + prefix-sum section (8B each) + BLAKE3 checksum (32B)
- [ ] `FsIndexView::parse()` validates magic, version, section bounds, entry count, and checksum
- [ ] O(log N) `lower_bound`, `upper_bound`, `binary_search_by_key` via binary search over fixed-stride entries
- [ ] O(1) `key_bytes(idx)`, `stable_item_id(idx)`, `version(idx)`, `size(idx)`, `prefix_sum(idx)` access
- [ ] O(log N) `prefix_sums_partition_point` for split-point selection
- [ ] `SortedIndex::OnDisk(FsIndexView)` variant fully functional (no more `todo!()`)
- [ ] All `SortedIndex` methods produce identical results for `InMemory` and `OnDisk` given the same data (property test)

title: Streaming split-point estimation via weighted quantile sketch
Token-based walk state checkpointing for cursor resume
description:
## Context

Phase 1C of bounded-memory filesystem connector epic (gossip-8936). Once the per-directory sorted readdir (gossip-8936.3) produces a streaming DFS walk, cursor resume can no longer use the current u64 index-based token (common.rs:199-239) — there is no flat sorted array to index into. Without a walk-state token, every resume requires restarting the DFS from root and skipping entries ≤ last_key (O(N) in the worst case — every file before the resume point must be re-walked and discarded).

With walk-state tokens, the DFS stack is serialized into the cursor token and reconstructed on resume: reopen directories along the saved stack, re-list + sort entries per directory, and fast-forward each level to the saved child index. This gives O(depth × max_dir_size) resume instead of O(N).

**Safety invariant**: tokens are advisory-only optimizations. Token corruption, decode failure, or filesystem mutation between sessions must NEVER produce incorrect results — only slower resume via key-only fallback. This matches the existing trust model documented at filesystem.rs:50-69.

## Current State

### Token encoding (common.rs:199-239)
The current token format is a big-endian u64 encoding the next absolute index position in a flat sorted array:

```rust
// common.rs:225-238
pub(crate) fn build_next_cursor(
    last_key: ItemKey,
    next_idx: usize,
    emit_tokens: bool,
) -> Result<Cursor, EnumerateError> {
    if !emit_tokens {
        return Ok(Cursor::with_last_key(last_key));
    }
    let next_idx_u64 = u64::try_from(next_idx)
        .map_err(|_| EnumerateError::permanent("next index exceeds capacity"))?;
    let token = TokenBytes::try_from_slice(&next_idx_u64.to_be_bytes())
        .map_err(|err| EnumerateError::permanent(format!("invalid token: {err}")))?;
    Ok(Cursor::with_token(last_key, token))
}
```

### Token decoding (common.rs:199-212)
```rust
// common.rs:207-212
pub(crate) fn cursor_token_index(cursor: &Cursor) -> Option<usize> {
    cursor
        .token()
        .and_then(|token| parse_u64_be(token.as_bytes()))
        .and_then(|idx| usize::try_from(idx).ok())
}
```

### Advisory debug_assert pattern (filesystem.rs:496-507)
```rust
// filesystem.rs:498-507
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
if self.emit_tokens
    && cursor.last_key().is_some()
    && let Some(token_idx) = common::cursor_token_index(cursor)
{
    debug_assert_eq!(
        token_idx, key_resume,
        "token index {token_idx} disagrees with key-derived resume position {key_resume}"
    );
}
```

### Walk stack structure (filesystem.rs:926-936)
The DFS walk uses a stack of WalkFrames, each holding a directory component and its entry iterator:
```rust
// filesystem.rs:926-936
struct WalkFrame {
    component: Option<std::ffi::OsString>,
    depth: usize,
    entries_since_check: usize,
    entries: DirList,
}
```

### Cursor contract (types.rs:578-651)
Owned Cursor holds optional ItemKey (last_key) and optional TokenBytes (token). TokenBytes max size is 16 KiB (types.rs:74-81). Token is connector-opaque — coordination layer passes it through without interpretation.

### Key size limits
- MAX_TOKEN_SIZE: 16,384 bytes (types.rs:81)
- MAX_ITEM_KEY_SIZE: 4,096 bytes (types.rs:64)

## Desired State

### New token format: serialized walk stack
The token encodes the DFS stack as an array of `(relative_dir_path, next_child_index)` tuples. On resume:
1. Decode the token into a list of stack frames
2. Walk down from root, reopening each directory in the saved path
3. At each level, re-list entries, sort them (per gossip-8936.3), and fast-forward to `next_child_index`
4. Resume iteration from that position

### Token wire format (compact binary)
```
[version: u8 = 0x01]
[frame_count: u16-LE]
for each frame:
    [path_component_len: u16-LE]
    [path_component_bytes: [u8; path_component_len]]
    [next_child_index: u32-LE]
```

Design choices:
- Version byte allows future format changes without breaking decode
- u16-LE for frame count: max 65535 frames (far beyond DEFAULT_MAX_WALK_DEPTH=512)
- u16-LE for path component length: max 65535 bytes per component (NAME_MAX is 255 on Linux/macOS)
- u32-LE for child index: max ~4B children per directory (practical readdir limit)
- Total token size for typical case (depth 10, avg component 20 bytes): ~1 + 2 + 10*(2+20+4) = 263 bytes (well within 16 KiB)
- Worst case (depth 512, component 255 bytes): ~1 + 2 + 512*(2+255+4) = 133,635 bytes — exceeds MAX_TOKEN_SIZE. Must handle: truncate stack to fit or fall back to key-only.

### Fallback behavior
- Token missing → key-only resume (restart walk + skip ≤ last_key)
- Token decode fails (wrong version, truncated, malformed) → key-only resume
- Token decodes but directory does not exist or child index out of range → key-only resume
- Token decodes and agrees with walk position → O(depth × max_dir_size) resume

### debug_assert cross-check
In debug builds, when both token-based and key-based resume are available, assert they agree — matching the existing pattern at filesystem.rs:498-507. In release builds, silently prefer key-authoritative position.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs` | Add `WalkToken` struct + encode/decode methods | New token format definition |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs` | Modify streaming enumerate to emit walk-state tokens | Token production on page emit |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs` | Add token-based resume path in streaming enumerate | Token consumption on page resume |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs` | Keep existing u64 token functions for in-memory connector (no change needed) | In-memory connector still uses flat index tokens |

### New types (in filesystem.rs)
```rust
/// Serialized DFS walk position for O(depth) cursor resume.
///
/// Each frame records a directory path component and the index of the next
/// child to process after resume. Token corruption falls back to key-only
/// resume — tokens are advisory.
struct WalkToken {
    frames: Vec<WalkTokenFrame>,
}

struct WalkTokenFrame {
    /// Directory component relative to parent (empty for root frame).
    component: Vec<u8>,
    /// Index of the next child entry to process in this directory's
    /// sorted entry list.
    next_child_index: u32,
}
```

### Patterns to Follow
- Existing advisory-token pattern (filesystem.rs:496-507): debug_assert on mismatch, key-authoritative in release
- Existing `with_tokens(bool)` builder (filesystem.rs:321-325): toggle token emission
- Existing `cursor_token_index` (common.rs:207-212) returns `Option` — new decode should similarly return `Option<WalkToken>`
- Existing `build_next_cursor` (common.rs:225-238): new builder should follow same error-handling pattern
- TokenBytes::try_from_slice (types.rs:565-576): enforces MAX_TOKEN_SIZE at construction

### Size budget enforcement
Before encoding, compute the encoded size. If it exceeds MAX_TOKEN_SIZE (16,384 bytes), either:
1. Truncate the stack (drop deepest frames, keeping root-ward frames) — still helps, just resumes from a shallower point
2. Fall back to no token — key-only resume

Option 1 is preferred: partial tokens still save work proportional to the saved depth.

### Relationship to gossip-8936.3
This task depends on gossip-8936.3 (per-directory sorted readdir) because the token's `next_child_index` is an index into the sorted entry list for that directory. Without deterministic per-directory sort order, the index has no meaning across sessions.

## Code References

- Token encoding: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:225-238` (`build_next_cursor`)
- Token decoding: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:207-212` (`cursor_token_index`)
- Advisory debug_assert: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:496-507`
- Walk stack structure: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:926-936` (`WalkFrame`)
- DFS walk main loop: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:1128-1316`
- Resume semantics doc: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:50-61`
- Trust model doc: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:64-69`
- TokenBytes type: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:565-576`
- MAX_TOKEN_SIZE: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:74-81` (16,384 bytes)
- Cursor type: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:578-651`
- In-memory connector O(1) token resume: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs:334-357`
- Page assembly with token staging: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:361-396`
- FilesystemConnector struct: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:276-294`
- `with_tokens` builder: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:321-325`

## Related Work

- **gossip-8936** (parent epic): Bounded-memory filesystem connector for TB-PB scale enumeration
- **gossip-8936.3**: Per-directory sorted readdir — PREREQUISITE (token's child index requires deterministic sort order)
- **gossip-8936.1** (closed): Bounded-memory spill-to-disk — established the sorted index abstraction
- **gossip-8936.5**: Key-range subtree pruning — complementary optimization (prune during walk)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WalkToken` struct with encode/decode round-trips correctly (unit test)
- [ ] Token decode gracefully returns `None` on: wrong version byte, truncated data, zero-length component in non-root frame
- [ ] Token-based resume produces identical enumeration output as key-only resume (property test: for random trees and random resume points, both paths emit same items)
- [ ] Token size stays within MAX_TOKEN_SIZE (16,384 bytes); if walk depth × avg component exceeds budget, stack is truncated root-ward and partial token is still usable
- [ ] debug_assert fires when token-derived position disagrees with key-derived position (test in debug mode)
- [ ] Token corruption (random byte flip) never causes incorrect enumeration — only falls back to key-only resume
- [ ] In-memory connector token behavior is completely unaffected (u64 index token path unchanged)
- [ ] All existing filesystem_tests pass without modification
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- Streaming walk serving layer task (not yet created — this task depends on it being designed first) will define how the walk state is held across `enumerate_page` calls
- The current `walk_dir_collect_files` (filesystem.rs:876-1319) is a one-shot function; streaming enumerate will need an incremental walk that yields pages. Token checkpointing snapshots the incremental walk's position.
- `MAX_TOKEN_SIZE` enforcement happens at `TokenBytes::try_from_slice` — the encode path must pre-check size before calling this
- For directories that changed between sessions (entries added/removed), the saved `next_child_index` may land on a different entry. The key-authoritative fallback handles this: if the entry at the saved index has a key ≤ last_key, the token is stale and key-based skip takes over.

title: Git OID-based streaming enumeration — replace path-based with content-addressed
description:
## Context

The Git connector currently enumerates files by shelling out to `git ls-files -z`, collecting ALL tracked paths into a sorted in-memory `Vec<GitEntry>`, then paginating over that snapshot. This has the same fundamental scaling problem as the filesystem connector (gossip-8936): O(N) memory and O(N log N) startup latency for sorting, where N = total tracked files.

Git repositories have a better option: **object IDs (OIDs)** are already stored in sorted order in pack `.idx` files and the multi-pack-index (MIDX). The `scanner-git` crate already has complete infrastructure for building MIDX in-memory from pack index files, performing O(log N) fanout-based binary search, and iterating OIDs in sorted order. This epic replaces the path-based enumeration model with OID-based content-addressed enumeration, leveraging these existing sorted index structures.

This is architecturally distinct from the filesystem connector work (gossip-8936) because:
- Git OIDs are **content-addressed** (same content = same OID), enabling `VersionId::Strong`
- The sorted OID keyspace is **uniformly distributed** (SHA-1/SHA-256), making shard splitting trivially balanced
- Pack index files provide **on-disk sorted order** with O(log N) seek via fanout tables -- no in-memory sort needed
- Location enrichment (path/commit mapping) can be deferred to findings only, not all objects

## Current State

The `GitConnector` (`crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:144-157`) builds a sorted `Vec<GitEntry>` from `git ls-files -z` output:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:144-157 -- connector struct with in-memory entries
pub struct GitConnector {
    repo: PathBuf,
    emit_tokens: bool,
    max_tracked_files: Option<usize>,
    index_state: IndexState,
    entries: Vec<GitEntry>,  // <-- O(N) memory
}
```

The `ensure_indexed` method (`git.rs:251-353`) shells out to `git ls-files -z`, stats every file, builds entries, and sorts:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:283-302 -- collecting all paths into memory
let tracked = match list_git_tracked_paths(&self.repo) { ... };
let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(tracked.len());
for key_bytes in tracked {
    // ... stat each file, build entry ...
}
entries.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| left.key.cmp(&right.key));
```

The `list_git_tracked_paths` function (`git.rs:656-683`) spawns `git ls-files -z` as a subprocess:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:656-683 -- shelling out to git
fn list_git_tracked_paths(repo: &Path) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, EnumerateError> {
    let output = Command::new("git")
        .arg("-C").arg(repo)
        .arg("ls-files").arg("-z").arg("--")
        .output() ...;
    // ... split on NUL, collect into Vec<Vec<u8>> ...
}
```

Meanwhile, the `scanner-git` crate already has:

1. **MIDX building** (`scanner-git/src/midx_build.rs:400-436`) -- k-way merge of sorted OID streams from pack `.idx` files, producing a unified sorted index
2. **Fanout-based OID lookup** (`scanner-git/src/midx.rs:326-361`) -- O(log N) binary search using 256-entry fanout table
3. **Sorted cursor seek** (`scanner-git/src/midx.rs:371-397`) -- monotonic cursor for merge-join style OID lookups
4. **Pack index iteration** (`scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs:319-331`) -- `iter_oids()` yielding (OID, index) pairs in sorted order
5. **OID hash index** (`scanner-git/src/oid_index.rs:50-57`) -- fixed-capacity open-addressing OID->index map
6. **Object store** (`scanner-git/src/object_store.rs:1-50`) -- pack/loose-backed object loader with MIDX lookup, delta resolution, and caching
7. **Pack decode** (`scanner-git/src/pack_decode.rs:1-13`) -- bounded zlib inflation of pack objects

## Desired State

A new `OidGitConnector` (or refactored `GitConnector`) that:

1. **Enumerates by OID, not by path.** ItemKey = raw OID bytes (20 bytes SHA-1 or 32 bytes SHA-256). Enumeration walks pack `.idx` / MIDX in sorted OID order.
2. **Uses O(1) memory relative to repo size.** The index is on-disk (mmap'd pack index / MIDX files). Only the current page of items is in memory.
3. **Provides O(log N) seek for cursor resume.** Binary search to first OID > last_key using fanout + binary search within the bucket.
4. **Produces `VersionId::Strong`.** OID bytes ARE the content hash -- immutable, content-addressed. No weak mtime-based versioning.
5. **Filters to blobs only during enumeration.** Trees, commits, and tags are not scannable; skip them without reading object bytes (type byte in pack header is cheap to decode).
6. **Defers location enrichment.** Path/commit mapping is done ONLY for findings (O(findings) not O(objects)). During enumeration, items carry only their OID.
7. **Splits shards uniformly.** The OID keyspace is uniformly distributed by construction (SHA-1/SHA-256). Hash-based shard splitting is trivially balanced.
8. **Latches pack list at scan start.** View/snapshot semantics: the set of pack files is captured once at the start of a scan. New packs arriving mid-scan are invisible.

## Implementation Guidance

### Architecture Overview

```
                    Pack .idx files
                         |
                    [MIDX builder]  (scanner-git/src/midx_build.rs)
                         |
                    MidxView (mmap)  (scanner-git/src/midx.rs)
                         |
              [OID-range enumeration]
                    /          \
           [blob filter]    [shard bounds]
                    \          /
              [EnumerationPage]
                         |
              [pack read for content]  (scanner-git/src/object_store.rs)
                         |
              [lazy location enrichment]  (only for findings)
```

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs` | Major refactor or new parallel impl | Replace path-based enumeration with OID-based |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs` | Possibly extend `ItemKey` / `VersionId` | Support OID bytes as keys |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/midx.rs` | Add range iteration API | `oids_in_range(start, end) -> OidRangeIter` |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/midx_build.rs` | Potentially expose builder for connector use | May need public API surface |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs` | Add range iteration on individual pack index | For repos without MIDX |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/object_store.rs` | Add blob-only type check API | Cheap type header decode without full inflation |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs` | Shared helpers for OID-based pagination | Reuse binary search patterns |

### Patterns to Follow

- The `MidxView::find_oid` method at `scanner-git/src/midx.rs:326-361` demonstrates fanout-based O(log N) binary search. OID range enumeration should use the same fanout structure.
- The `IdxView::iter_oids` method at `scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs:319-331` shows sorted iteration over a single pack index.
- The k-way merge in `midx_build.rs:421-436` shows how to merge sorted OID streams from multiple packs.
- The `ObjectStore` at `scanner-git/src/object_store.rs:16-17` already handles MIDX-based pack lookup and object inflation.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `MidxView` | `scanner-git/src/midx.rs` | Zero-copy MIDX parser with fanout, OID table, offset table |
| `IdxView` | `scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs` | Zero-copy pack index parser with OID iteration |
| `MidxBuildError` / builder | `scanner-git/src/midx_build.rs` | Build MIDX from pack `.idx` files |
| `OidBytes` | `scanner-git/src/object_id.rs` | Fixed-size OID representation (20 or 32 bytes) |
| `OidIndex` | `scanner-git/src/oid_index.rs` | Fast OID->index hash map |
| `ObjectStore` | `scanner-git/src/object_store.rs` | Pack/loose object loading with delta resolution |
| `PackDecodeLimits` | `scanner-git/src/pack_decode.rs` | Bounded inflation for reading blob content |
| `EntryKind` | `scanner-git/src/pack_inflate.rs` | Object type discrimination (blob/tree/commit/tag) |
| `BytesView` | `scanner-git/src/bytes.rs` | Owned or mmap'd byte buffers |

### Blast Radius

- **Enumeration consumers**: Anything that consumes `EnumerationPage` and interprets `ItemKey` as a path will need updating. ItemKey becomes opaque OID bytes.
- **Read path**: `ReadConnector::open` currently returns a file handle for a path. OID-based read must decode the object from pack/loose storage.
- **StableItemId derivation**: Currently `derive_stable_item_id(tag, key_bytes)` where key_bytes is a path. Changes to `derive_stable_item_id(tag, oid_bytes)`.
- **Version model**: Moves from `VersionId::Weak` (mtime+size) to `VersionId::Strong` (OID = content hash). This changes dedup and change-detection semantics.
- **Location enrichment**: Finding reporters that expect a file path will need the lazy enrichment layer to resolve OID -> (path, commit).
- **Scanner runtime**: `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` wires connectors. The OID connector will need runtime integration.

## Code References

```rust
    let mut iter = view.iter_oids();
    if let Some((oid, idx)) = iter.next() {
        heap.push(MergeEntry {
            oid,
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/midx.rs:326-361 -- fanout-based OID binary search
pub fn find_oid(&self, oid: &OidBytes) -> Result<Option<u32>, MidxError> {
    let bytes = oid.as_slice();
    let first = bytes[0];
    let bucket_end = self.fanout(first);
    let bucket_start = if first == 0 { 0 } else { self.fanout(first - 1) };

    let mut lo = bucket_start;
    let mut hi = bucket_end;
    while lo < hi {
        let mid = lo + ((hi - lo) / 2);
        let mid_oid = self.oid_at(mid);
        match bytes.cmp(mid_oid) {
            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => hi = mid,
            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => lo = mid + 1,
            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => return Ok(Some(mid)),
        }
    }
    Ok(None)
}
```

```rust
    IdxOidIter {
        oid_table: self.oid_table,
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:719-725 -- VersionId
pub enum VersionId {
    Strong(ObjectVersionId),
    Weak(ObjectVersionId),
}
```

## Design Notes

### Key Design Decisions

1. **ItemKey = raw OID bytes, not hex.** Using the raw 20/32-byte OID as the key avoids 2x expansion from hex encoding and preserves the natural sort order of the index. The OID keyspace is uniformly distributed, so shard splitting via prefix ranges (e.g., `[0x00..., 0x80...)` and `[0x80..., 0xff...]`) is trivially balanced.

2. **StableId = `repo_id:oid`.** Content-addressed identity. The same blob in two repos gets different StableIds (via repo_id prefix), but the same blob at two paths in one repo is deduplicated.

3. **VersionId::Strong always.** OID bytes ARE the content hash. There is no mtime or size ambiguity. The scanner can trust that same-OID = same-content without re-reading.

4. **Blob-only filtering is cheap.** Pack entry headers encode the object type in the first few bits. Decoding the type requires reading a few bytes of the pack header, not inflating the full object. Non-blob objects (trees, commits, tags) are skipped during enumeration with negligible cost.

5. **Location enrichment is lazy.** During enumeration, items carry only their OID. Path and commit information is resolved ONLY for items that produce findings. This changes the cost model from O(objects) to O(findings), which is typically 3-5 orders of magnitude smaller.

6. **View/snapshot semantics.** The set of pack files (and thus the MIDX) is captured once at the start of a scan. Concurrent `git gc` or `git repack` operations that create/remove packs do not affect the in-progress scan. This is similar to MVCC -- the scan sees a consistent snapshot.

### Trade-offs

- **Dedup across paths:** OID-based enumeration naturally deduplicates blobs that appear at multiple paths. This is generally desirable (why scan the same content twice?) but changes the enumeration count relative to path-based enumeration.
- **No working-tree changes:** OID enumeration sees only committed/packed objects, not uncommitted working-tree changes. This is a deliberate scope decision -- uncommitted work is handled by separate mechanisms.
- **Location enrichment latency:** Finding reports will have slightly higher latency for the first finding in a blob, since path resolution is deferred. This is acceptable because finding volume is low.

## Performance Considerations

- **Memory:** O(1) relative to repo size. MIDX/pack indexes are mmap'd. Only the current page of `ScanItem`s is in memory.
- **Startup:** No `git ls-files` subprocess. No in-memory sort. MIDX build (if needed) is O(N log P) where P = pack count, and the output is reusable across scans.
- **Seek:** O(log N) via fanout table (256 buckets) + binary search within bucket. Much faster than binary search over the full keyspace.
- **Scan throughput:** Sequential OID iteration through MIDX is cache-friendly (contiguous memory-mapped pages).
- **Shard balance:** SHA-1/SHA-256 OIDs are uniformly distributed. Any prefix-based split produces balanced shards without needing to sample the data.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8936 | Bounded-memory filesystem connector for TB-PB scale enumeration | relates-to: parallel epic for filesystem connector; different architecture but same scaling motivation |
| gossip-8936.3 | Per-directory sorted readdir in filesystem walker | relates-to: filesystem-specific approach to sorted enumeration |
| gossip-8925 | Fix TOCTOU read-path confinement in GitConnector via shared openat helper | relates-to: current git connector security fix; OID-based read bypasses the path-based TOCTOU issue entirely |
| gossip-rs-8r9.8 | Phase 4B: Implement Git connector and wire Git connector-mode runtime parity | relates-to: created the current path-based GitConnector being replaced |

## Sub-tasks (to be created as child tasks)

1. **OID-range enumeration using pack .idx / MIDX sorted order** -- Add `oids_in_range(start, end)` API to `MidxView` and `IdxView`; implement `EnumerationConnector` that pages through the sorted OID table.
2. **Blob-only filtering during OID enumeration** -- Add cheap type-header decode to skip trees/commits/tags during enumeration without inflating objects.
3. **Lazy location enrichment for findings only** -- Build path/commit mapping layer that resolves OID -> (path, commit) on demand, triggered only when a finding is reported.
4. **Pack-aware shard splitting (hash-uniform distribution)** -- Implement `choose_split_point` using OID prefix ranges; prove uniform distribution via property tests.
5. **View/snapshot semantics -- latch pack list at scan start** -- Capture pack file set at connector construction; handle stale mmaps gracefully when packs are repacked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Git enumeration works without building in-memory sorted path list
- [ ] Enumeration uses O(1) memory relative to repo size (pack index is mmap'd on-disk)
- [ ] OID-range queries via MIDX are O(log N) seek + O(page_size) scan
- [ ] `VersionId::Strong` is used for all enumerated items (OID = content hash)
- [ ] Non-blob objects (trees, commits, tags) are filtered during enumeration
- [ ] Location enrichment (path/commit) is deferred to finding-time only
- [ ] Shard splitting produces balanced partitions (property test: max/min ratio < 2x for 16+ shards)
- [ ] Concurrent `git repack` does not corrupt in-progress scan (snapshot semantics)
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- MIDX format spec: https://git-scm.com/docs/multi-pack-index
- `scanner-git/src/midx.rs` -- complete MIDX parser with fanout, OID lookup, pack offset resolution
- `scanner-git/src/pack_idx.rs` -- complete pack `.idx` parser with sorted OID iteration

- `scanner-git/src/blob_introducer.rs` -- existing blob processing pipeline (for understanding how blobs flow to findings)

title: Stride-based sparse sampling to fix O(N×cap) compaction and per-item heap churn in StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review of `StreamingSplitEstimator` (gossip-8936.8) identified two fatal performance issues: (1) after `sample_cap` is reached, every `observe()` triggers an O(sample_cap) compaction rebuild, and (2) every `observe()` allocates and copies key bytes regardless of whether the sample is retained. At PB scale with hundreds of millions of files, this makes the estimator unusable.

The `observe()` call sits inside the core page enumeration loop (`filesystem.rs:779`), running once per file in the walk. Under the allocation policy this is a WARM-to-HOT path at scale.

## Current State

### Pathological compaction — O(N × sample_cap) total work

After the first fill, the steady state is: push (cap+1) → compact back to cap → repeat for every item:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:247-255
fn push_rank_sample(&mut self, position: f64, key: &[u8]) {
    self.rank_samples.push(KeySample {
        position,
        key: key.to_vec(),
    });
    if self.rank_samples.len() > self.sample_cap {
        self.compact_rank_samples();
    }
}
```

`compact_samples` (`:19-91`) does a full sweep through the old vector with clones at each pick. With N files past the cap and default sample_cap=1024, total compaction work is O(N × 1024).

### Per-item heap churn — 2 allocations per item

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:145-167
pub(crate) fn observe(&mut self, key: &[u8], file_size: u64) {
    if self.first_observed_key.is_none() {
        self.first_observed_key = Some(key.to_vec());  // alloc #1 (once)
    }
    let rank = self.count as f64;
    self.push_rank_sample(rank, key);    // alloc #2 — key.to_vec() always
    // ...
    self.push_byte_sample(cumulative, key); // alloc #3 — key.to_vec() when size > 0
    // ...
}
```

Most of these allocations are immediately dropped during the next compaction cycle.

### Callsite — per-file in pagination loop

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:779
self.split_estimator.observe(file.key.as_bytes(), file.size);
```

## Desired State

Replace the "sample every item, compact when full" strategy with stride-based sparse sampling:

### Rank sampling
- Maintain `rank_stride: u64` starting at 1. Only record a rank sample every `rank_stride` items.
- When sample count exceeds `sample_cap`, downsample by keeping every other sample and double `rank_stride`.
- After the first fill, compaction happens O(log N) times total, not O(N) times.

### Byte sampling
- Maintain `byte_stride: u64` and `next_byte_mark: u64`.
- Sample when `cumulative_bytes >= next_byte_mark`, then `next_byte_mark += byte_stride`.
- When sample count exceeds cap, downsample and double `byte_stride`.

### Net effect
- `observe()` becomes O(1) amortized: increment counters, occasionally (every `stride` items) push one sample.
- Key allocations become O(sample_cap) total, not O(N).
- Compaction runs O(log N) times, not O(N) times.
- Accuracy is preserved — the test suite should still pass.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Replace push-every-item + compact-on-overflow with stride-based sampling | Core fix |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Update/add tests for stride-based behavior | Verify correctness preserved |

### Patterns to Follow

- The existing `compact_samples` function's position-based nearest-neighbor selection logic can be reused for the rare downsample events.
- `InlineVec<u8, N>` from `gossip-stdx/src/inline_vec.rs` may be useful for key storage if most keys are short.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `InlineVec<T, N>` | `gossip-stdx/src/inline_vec.rs` | Stack-first key storage for retained samples |

### Blast Radius

| Consumer | File | Impact |
|----------|------|--------|
| `FilesystemConnector::enumerate_page_bounds` | `filesystem.rs:779` | No API change — observe() signature unchanged |
| `choose_split_point_bounds` | `filesystem.rs:879` | No change — estimate_split_key() signature unchanged |
| `merge()` | `split_estimator.rs:220` | Must be updated for stride-based internals |
| All existing tests | `split_estimator_tests.rs` | Must still pass (accuracy may shift slightly within bounds) |

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:19-91 — compact_samples (O(cap) per call)
fn compact_samples(samples: &mut Vec<KeySample>, cap: usize) {
    if samples.len() <= cap { return; }
    let old = mem::take(samples);
    // ... full sweep with clones at each pick ...
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:93-97 — KeySample struct
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct KeySample {
    position: f64,
    key: Vec<u8>,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:99-120 — StreamingSplitEstimator struct
pub(crate) struct StreamingSplitEstimator {
    sample_cap: usize,
    rank_samples: Vec<KeySample>,
    byte_samples: Vec<KeySample>,
    total_bytes: u64,
    count: u64,
    first_observed_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}
```

## Performance Considerations

- Under the allocation policy, this is a WARM path (per-file in pagination loop) that behaves like HOT at PB scale.
- After this fix, `observe()` should do zero heap work in the common case (counter increments only), with occasional O(1) sample insertion.
- Compaction (O(sample_cap)) happens O(log N) times total — amortized cost per item drops from O(sample_cap) to O(log(N) × sample_cap / N) ≈ O(1).
- A microbenchmark feeding 1M items should confirm observe() does not do O(sample_cap) work per call.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8936.8 | Streaming split-point estimation via weighted quantile sketch | **Predecessor** — original implementation being improved |
| gossip-8936 | Bounded-memory filesystem connector for TB-PB scale enumeration | **Parent epic** |
| gossip-6rbq | Filesystem connector performance optimizations | **Relates-to** — prior perf work on the connector |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `observe()` is O(1) amortized — only records a sample every `stride` items/bytes
- [ ] Compaction happens O(log N) times total, not O(N) times
- [ ] Key allocations are O(sample_cap), not O(N)
- [ ] All existing tests in `split_estimator_tests.rs` pass
- [ ] Zipf accuracy test still achieves ≤1% weight error
- [ ] Merge behavior preserved (merged estimator matches single-pass within tolerance)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`

- Callsite: `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:779`
- Allocation policy tiers: see `AGENTS.md` allocation policy section

title: Unify rank and byte sample vectors into single Sample struct in StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review of `StreamingSplitEstimator` identified that the same key bytes are stored twice — once in `rank_samples` and once in `byte_samples`. Unifying these into a single sample vector cuts key allocations roughly in half, reduces memory footprint, and simplifies the code (one vector, one compact path).

## Current State

### Two separate sample vectors with duplicate keys

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:99-120
pub(crate) struct StreamingSplitEstimator {
    sample_cap: usize,
    rank_samples: Vec<KeySample>,    // stores key bytes
    byte_samples: Vec<KeySample>,    // stores SAME key bytes again
    total_bytes: u64,
    count: u64,
    first_observed_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}
```

### Both push methods clone the key independently

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:247-265
fn push_rank_sample(&mut self, position: f64, key: &[u8]) {
    self.rank_samples.push(KeySample {
        position,
        key: key.to_vec(),   // clone #1
    });
    // ...
}

fn push_byte_sample(&mut self, position: f64, key: &[u8]) {
    self.byte_samples.push(KeySample {
        position,
        key: key.to_vec(),   // clone #2 of same key
    });
    // ...
}
```

### Both vectors are compacted independently

`compact_rank_samples` and `compact_byte_samples` (`:267-273`) call the same `compact_samples` function on their respective vectors.

## Desired State

A single unified sample struct and vector:

```rust
struct Sample {
    rank: u64,
    cumulative_bytes: u64,
    key: Box<[u8]>,  // or InlineVec<u8, 128>
}
```

Both `rank` and `cumulative_bytes` are monotonically non-decreasing in stream order, so a single sorted vector supports binary search on either dimension:
- Rank-based lookup: `samples.partition_point(|s| s.rank < target_rank)`
- Byte-based lookup: `samples.partition_point(|s| s.cumulative_bytes < target_bytes)`

For zero-size files: `cumulative_bytes` equals the current cumulative total (unchanged from previous sample). The byte-based search still works correctly since the position is monotonic.

### Compaction

One `compact_samples` call using the byte position dimension (which has more information than rank for weighted median estimation). When bytes are all zero, fall back to rank-based spacing.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Replace `KeySample` with unified `Sample { rank, cumulative_bytes, key }` | Single struct, single vector |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Merge `rank_samples` and `byte_samples` into `samples: Vec<Sample>` | One vector instead of two |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Remove `push_rank_sample`, `push_byte_sample`, `compact_rank_samples`, `compact_byte_samples` | Simplify to single push + compact path |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Update `estimate_split_key` to search single vector by appropriate dimension | Rank or byte search on same vector |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Update `merge` to operate on single vector | Simpler merge logic |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Update test helpers, remove `rank_sample_len`/`byte_sample_len` | Adapt to unified vector |

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `InlineVec<T, N>` | `gossip-stdx/src/inline_vec.rs` | Stack-first key storage — most filesystem keys (paths) are < 128 bytes |

### Blast Radius

| Consumer | File | Impact |
|----------|------|--------|
| `observe()` | `split_estimator.rs:145` | Simplified — one push instead of two |
| `estimate_split_key()` | `split_estimator.rs:169` | Search single vector by rank or bytes |
| `merge()` | `split_estimator.rs:220` | One vector to merge instead of two |
| Test helpers | `split_estimator_tests.rs:296-308` | `rank_sample_len`/`byte_sample_len` → `sample_len` |

No external API changes.

## Code References

```rust

    let rank = midpoint_rank.clamp(min_rank, max_rank);
    return Self::nearest_sample(&self.rank_samples, rank).map(ToOwned::to_owned);
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:191-197 — byte-based primary search
let target_weight = self.total_bytes as f64 / 2.0;
let mut candidate = Self::nearest_sample(&self.byte_samples, target_weight)
    .or_else(|| {
        let rank = midpoint_rank.clamp(min_rank, max_rank);
        Self::nearest_sample(&self.rank_samples, rank)
    })?
    .to_vec();
```

title: Implement redacted Debug for split estimator types to prevent toxic key byte leakage
description:
## Context

Code review identified that `#[derive(Debug)]` on `KeySample` and `StreamingSplitEstimator` will print raw key bytes (customer filesystem paths) in panic backtraces, debug logging, or any context that formats these types. Keys are customer-derived and should be treated as toxic by default.

A prior task (gossip-4d9) addressed similar Debug redaction issues in `error.rs`. This applies the same principle to the split estimator types.

## Current State

### Derived Debug prints raw key bytes

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:93-97
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct KeySample {
    position: f64,
    key: Vec<u8>,    // <-- raw customer paths printed by Debug
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:104
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct StreamingSplitEstimator {
    // ...
    first_observed_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,  // <-- also printed
}
```

If these types appear in a panic backtrace (e.g., from an `expect()` on a method that borrows them, or from a `debug_assert!` in a test), raw customer paths would be emitted to logs.

## Desired State

Manual `Debug` implementations that redact key bytes:

```rust
impl fmt::Debug for KeySample {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("KeySample")
            .field("position", &self.position)
            .field("key_len", &self.key.len())
            .finish()
    }
}

impl fmt::Debug for StreamingSplitEstimator {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("StreamingSplitEstimator")
            .field("sample_cap", &self.sample_cap)
            .field("rank_samples_len", &self.rank_samples.len())
            .field("byte_samples_len", &self.byte_samples.len())
            .field("total_bytes", &self.total_bytes)
            .field("count", &self.count)
            .field("has_first_key", &self.first_observed_key.is_some())
            .finish()
    }
}
```

Print structural info (lengths, counts, presence) but never raw key bytes.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Replace `#[derive(Debug)]` with manual `Debug` impls on `KeySample` and `StreamingSplitEstimator` | Redact customer key bytes |

### Patterns to Follow

- gossip-4d9 addressed identical Debug redaction in `error.rs` — follow that precedent.
- Print `key_len` instead of key contents. Optionally print a truncated hash prefix (e.g., first 4 bytes of blake3) for debugging identity without exposing content.

### Blast Radius

Minimal. These are `pub(crate)` types. The only consumers of their Debug output are panic backtraces and test failures. No external API change.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:93-97
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct KeySample {
    position: f64,
    key: Vec<u8>,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:104-120
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct StreamingSplitEstimator {
    sample_cap: usize,
    rank_samples: Vec<KeySample>,
    byte_samples: Vec<KeySample>,
    total_bytes: u64,
    count: u64,
    first_observed_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-4d9 | Address H-1 (Debug redaction) and M-3 (box large variants) in error.rs | **Precedent** — same pattern applied to error types |
| gossip-8938 | Stride-based sparse sampling | **Relates-to** — if done together, apply to the new struct shape |
| gossip-8940 | Unify rank and byte sample vectors | **Relates-to** — unified Sample struct also needs redacted Debug |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No `#[derive(Debug)]` on types containing key bytes in `split_estimator.rs`

- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

title: Fix semantic mismatch in byte-sample doc comment in StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review identified a semantic mismatch between the doc comment on the byte sampling logic and what the code actually does. The comment claims the algorithm "selects the file whose range straddles the weighted median" but the code selects the sample whose *start cumulative position* is nearest to the target — which can pick the next file when the median falls near the end of a large file's range.

## Current State

### Comment overpromises

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:159-162
// Sample the cumulative position at the *start* of this file's byte
// range so that `nearest_sample(byte_samples, total/2)` selects the
// file whose range straddles the weighted median rather than the file
// whose cumulative end is nearest.
```

### What the code actually does

`nearest_sample` (`:275-293`) uses `partition_point` to find the sample with position closest to `total/2`. This selects the sample whose *start* cumulative position is nearest to the target — a nearest-start selection, not a "straddles the median" selection.

## Desired State

Update the comment to accurately describe what the code does:

```rust
// Sample the cumulative position at the *start* of this file's byte
// range. `nearest_sample(byte_samples, total/2)` selects the sample
// whose start-of-range position is closest to the byte-weighted
// midpoint.
```

Also review the module-level doc (`split_estimator.rs:1-6`) for similar claims.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:159-162` | Fix comment to describe actual nearest-start behavior | Accuracy |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:1-6` | Review module-level doc for similar overpromising | Consistency |

### Blast Radius

None — doc-only change.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8936.8 | Streaming split-point estimation via weighted quantile sketch | **Predecessor** |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Comment at `:159-162` accurately describes the nearest-start selection algorithm
- [ ] No doc claims "straddles the median" unless the algorithm actually guarantees that
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- `nearest_sample`: `split_estimator.rs:275-293`
- Module doc: `split_estimator.rs:1-6`
close_reason: Issue resolved by code rewrite: the dual-axis stride-based sampling redesign replaced the old rank_samples/byte_samples architecture. All current doc comments accurately describe the algorithm — the original misleading 'straddles the weighted median' comment no longer exists. Module doc (lines 37-49) correctly describes dual-axis sampling, stride-doubling compaction, and nearest-position binary search estimation.

title: Rename misleading compression parameter to sample_cap in StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review identified that the `compression` parameter name in `StreamingSplitEstimator::new()` is misleading — it's actually a sample-cap scaling factor, not a compression ratio. Additionally, `MIN_SAMPLE_CAP = 64` is dead weight because `compression.max(32) * KEY_SAMPLE_FACTOR(4) = 128` always exceeds 64.

## Current State

### Misleading parameter name

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:129-133
pub(crate) fn new(compression: usize) -> Self {
    let compression = compression.max(32);
    let sample_cap = compression
        .saturating_mul(KEY_SAMPLE_FACTOR)
        .max(MIN_SAMPLE_CAP);
    // ...
}
```

The parameter `compression` suggests data compression ratio. In practice, it's `max_samples / KEY_SAMPLE_FACTOR`. The actual sample cap is `compression * 4`.

### Dead constant

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:10
const MIN_SAMPLE_CAP: usize = 64;
```

Since `compression.max(32) * 4 = 128`, `MIN_SAMPLE_CAP = 64` can never trigger. The `.max(MIN_SAMPLE_CAP)` is dead code.

### Callsite uses the misleading name

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:289-290
const SPLIT_ESTIMATOR_COMPRESSION: usize = StreamingSplitEstimator::DEFAULT_COMPRESSION;
```

## Desired State

Either:
- **Option A**: Accept `sample_cap` directly as the constructor parameter. Remove the intermediate scaling.
- **Option B**: Rename to `max_samples_hint` to communicate intent. Keep the scaling but rename the knob.

Remove the dead `MIN_SAMPLE_CAP` constant. Rename `DEFAULT_COMPRESSION` to `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_CAP`.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Rename parameter, remove dead constant | API clarity |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:289-290` | Update constant name | Match renamed API |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Update test constructors | Match renamed API |

### Blast Radius

`pub(crate)` API — only affects callers within the `gossip-connectors` crate.

| Consumer | File | Impact |
|----------|------|--------|
| `FilesystemConnector::new` | `filesystem.rs:308` | Update constructor arg name |
| All tests | `split_estimator_tests.rs` | Update `new(compression)` calls |

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8938 | Stride-based sparse sampling | **Relates-to** — renaming can be done alongside the redesign |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `compression` parameter renamed to `sample_cap` or `max_samples_hint`
- [ ] `MIN_SAMPLE_CAP` removed or replaced with meaningful minimum
- [ ] `DEFAULT_COMPRESSION` renamed to match new parameter name
- [ ] All callsites updated
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- Callsite: `filesystem.rs:289-290, 308`

title: Add proptest stability, byte-precision, and performance guard tests for StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review of `StreamingSplitEstimator` identified gaps in test coverage that should be filled to guard against regressions — particularly around the new stride-based sampling, integer precision, and performance characteristics. Some of the suggested tests already partially exist in the test suite but need extension.

## Current State

### Existing test coverage

The test suite (`split_estimator_tests.rs`) has good coverage of:
- Equal/skewed weight split selection
- Minimum entry requirements
- Front-loaded weight avoidance (first-key guard)
- Zipf accuracy (1% weight error bound)
- Merge consistency
- Compaction edge cases
- Extreme file sizes (u64::MAX / 2)
- Property tests: zero-size midpoint, observed-key invariant, memory boundedness

### Missing coverage

1. **Monotonicity/stability property**: No test verifies that appending more items doesn't cause the split estimate to jump backward wildly. The existing proptest for `prop_split_key_is_always_observed_key` checks the key is valid but not stability.

2. **Byte precision above 2^53**: The extreme file sizes test uses `u64::MAX / 2` but doesn't check for f64-precision drift. Need a test with many files whose cumulative bytes exceed 2^53 and verify determinism across runs.

3. **Allocation/performance guard**: No test or benchmark verifies that `observe()` is O(1) amortized or that allocations scale with sample count, not item count.

## Desired State

### 1. Monotonicity/stability proptest

```rust
/// Appending more items should not cause the estimated split to jump backward
/// in key order by more than a bounded amount.
#[test]
fn prop_split_estimate_stable_under_append(count in 10..500usize) {
    // Feed items, record estimate at each step past count=2
    // Assert: estimate never decreases by more than (count / sample_cap + 1) positions
}
```

### 2. Byte-precision test above 2^53

```rust
#[test]
fn deterministic_above_two_pow_53() {
    // Construct stream whose total_bytes exceeds 2^53
    // Run twice, verify identical split keys
    // With integer positions: exact match guaranteed
    // With f64: this test would catch drift
}
```

### 3. Allocation/performance guard

A microbenchmark or instrumented test that:
- Feeds 1M items to the estimator
- Asserts `observe()` average cost does not scale with `sample_cap`
- Optionally: uses a counting allocator to verify allocations are O(sample_cap), not O(N)

This can be a `#[bench]` (nightly), a Criterion benchmark, or a `#[test]` with time thresholds.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Add monotonicity proptest | Stability regression guard |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Add byte-precision test above 2^53 | Precision regression guard |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/benches/` (new or existing) | Add microbenchmark for observe() throughput | Performance regression guard |

### Patterns to Follow

- Existing proptests in `split_estimator_tests.rs:385-459` use `proptest!` macro with range parameters.
- The `key_for_index` / `index_from_key` helpers are available for constructing/decoding keys.
- `relative_weight_error` helper already exists for accuracy assertions.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `key_for_index` | `split_estimator_tests.rs:15` | Construct deterministic keys |
| `index_from_key` | `split_estimator_tests.rs:19` | Decode keys to indices |
| `relative_weight_error` | `split_estimator_tests.rs:31` | Accuracy assertions |

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs:385-427
// Existing proptests — follow this pattern
proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn prop_zero_sizes_use_count_midpoint(count in 2..500usize) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn prop_split_key_is_always_observed_key(count in 2..200usize) { ... }
}
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8938 | Stride-based sparse sampling | **Depends on** — perf guard test validates the stride-based redesign |
| gossip-8939 | Replace f64 positions with u64 | **Depends on** — precision test validates the integer math fix |
| gossip-8940 | Unify rank and byte sample vectors | **Relates-to** — tests may need updating if sample accessors change |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Proptest for monotonicity/stability of split estimate under append
- [ ] Deterministic test with `total_bytes > 2^53` verifying identical results across runs
- [ ] Benchmark or instrumented test verifying `observe()` is O(1) amortized at 1M items
- [ ] All new tests pass
