## Current State

### `DurableCommitSink` struct (`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:86-220`)

`DurableCommitSink` implements the local `CommitSink` trait. On each item lifecycle:

- `begin_item` (line 180-194): Stores `ItemMeta` in `Mutex<BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, ItemMeta>>` and records `CommitProgressRecord::Begin` via `CoordinationEventRecorder`.

title: EP2.9.3 — Add readiness gate tests to prevent old-path regression
description:
## Context

The receipt-driven commit protocol (EP2.1–EP2.8) established `ResultCommitter`, `PrefixCheckpointAggregator`, `CommitPipeline`, and the `CompletedUnit` / `CommitReceipt` vocabulary as the authoritative durability path. EP2.9.1 deletes the old `DurableCommitSink` escape hatch, and EP2.9.2 updates docs.

Without a guardrail, future code changes could silently reintroduce the old completion path — re-adding `DurableCommitSink`, leaking `checkpoint_hint` fields into the runtime surface, or removing the durability regression test suite. This task adds two layers of defense:

1. A **compile-time guardrail test** that uses `include_str!` to assert certain banned patterns do NOT appear in key runtime source files.
2. A **runtime durability regression test suite** that stitches together `ResultCommitter` + `PrefixCheckpointAggregator` primitives with real durable receipts to prove the core durability invariants.

## Current State

### Test module wiring (`lib.rs`)

The test module is wired at the end of `lib.rs`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:1642-1644
#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "lib_tests.rs"]
mod tests;
```

There is no `runtime_durability_tests` module wired anywhere in the crate. The file `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` does not exist.

### Existing test file (`lib_tests.rs`)

`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs` (909 lines) contains 28 tests covering parsing, validation, cancellation, scan dispatch, event round-tripping, and commit forwarding. No readiness gate or durability regression tests exist.

### `checkpoint_hint` still present in runtime surface

`AssignmentOutcome` exposes `checkpoint_hint`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:678-687
pub struct AssignmentOutcome {
    pub report: ScanReport,
    /// Optional checkpoint hint for distributed coordinators.
    pub checkpoint_hint: Option<ScanCheckpoint>,
    pub debug_output: Option<String>,
}
```

Both `ordered_content.rs` (lines 89, 163) and `git_repo.rs` (lines 105, 161) set `checkpoint_hint: None` in their return values.

### `DurableCommitSink` still present

`DurableCommitSink` is defined at `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:86-220`. EP2.9.1 will delete it.

### Required modules for runtime durability tests do NOT yet exist

The durability test suite imports from four modules that are not yet present in `gossip-scanner-runtime`:

- `crate::checkpoint_aggregator` — Defined in EP2.5 (`PrefixCheckpointAggregator`, `PrefixCheckpointError`, `ReceiptRecordOutcome`, `ReceiptOwner`)
- `crate::commit_model` — Defined in EP2.2 (`CompletedUnit`)
- `crate::result_committer` — Defined in EP2.4 (`ResultCommitter`, `ResultCommitError`)
- `crate::result_translation` — Defined in EP2.3 (`translate_item_result`, `ItemResult`, `PersistenceTranslation`, `ScanTiming`)

It also imports from:
- `gossip_persistence_inmemory` — **Exists** at `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/` with `InMemoryDoneLedger` (in `done_ledger.rs:131`) and `InMemoryFindingsSink` (in `findings.rs:93`)
- `scanner_scheduler::FsFindingRecord` — **Exists** in the current codebase
- `gossip_contracts` types — **Exist** (Cursor, ItemKey, WriteContext, identity types, etc.)

### Cargo.toml dev-dependencies

```toml
# crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/Cargo.toml:29-31
[dev-dependencies]
rstest.workspace = true
tempfile = "3"
```

`gossip-persistence-inmemory` is **not** currently a dev-dependency of `gossip-scanner-runtime`.

### Source files in the crate

```
crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/
├── cli.rs
├── cli_tests.rs
├── commit_sink.rs
├── coordination_sink.rs

```

## Desired State

### Part A: Compile-time readiness gate test (add to `lib_tests.rs`)

Append this test to the end of `lib_tests.rs`:

```rust
// Append to crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs
#[test]
fn epic2_readiness_gate_keeps_legacy_progress_paths_out_of_runtime() {
    let lib_src = include_str!("lib.rs");
    assert!(
        !lib_src.contains("pub checkpoint_hint"),
        "runtime surface must not expose checkpoint hints after the Epic 2 cutover"
    );
    assert!(
        lib_src.contains("mod runtime_durability_tests;"),
        "runtime durability regression suite must stay wired into crate tests"
    );

    let commit_sink_src = include_str!("commit_sink.rs");
    assert!(
        !commit_sink_src.contains("pub struct DurableCommitSink"),
        "legacy DurableCommitSink path must stay removed"
    );

    let distributed_src = include_str!("distributed.rs");
    assert!(
        !distributed_src.contains("checkpoint_hint"),
        "distributed runtime must not depend on checkpoint hints"
    );
}
```

**Prerequisites for this test to pass:**
- EP2.9.1 must have removed `DurableCommitSink` from `commit_sink.rs`
- `pub checkpoint_hint` must be removed from `AssignmentOutcome` in `lib.rs` (either by EP2.9.1 or by this task)
- `runtime_durability_tests` module must be wired into `lib.rs`
- `distributed.rs` must not contain `checkpoint_hint` (currently it does not)

### Part B: Runtime durability test suite (`runtime_durability_tests.rs`)

Create `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` (523 lines) containing 6 integration tests:

1. **`no_checkpoint_without_receipt_even_when_done_ledger_is_durable`** — Proves findings+done-ledger durability alone cannot produce a checkpoint without an explicit receipt.
2. **`crash_after_findings_before_ledger_write_does_not_checkpoint_and_retry_is_safe`** — Proves crash recovery: findings durable but ledger fails, no checkpoint; retry succeeds idempotently.
3. **`real_receipts_only_advance_the_contiguous_prefix`** — Proves out-of-order receipt arrival: only the contiguous prefix checkpoints.
4. **`repo_frontier_uses_the_same_committer_and_checkpoint_aggregator_primitives`** — Proves Git repo-frontier units use the same committer+aggregator as ordered-content.
5. **`crash_after_ledger_before_checkpoint_allows_reassignment_retry_and_rejects_stale_fence`** — Proves stale fence epochs are rejected after reassignment, and retry with current epoch succeeds.
6. **`pending_prefix_does_not_widen_until_the_previous_checkpoint_is_acked`** — Proves checkpoint preparation is atomic: pending prefix doesn't grow until acknowledged.

The full test code is in the reference artifact at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/commit-protocol/2_9/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` (523 lines).

**Prerequisites for this test file:**
- All four modules must exist: `checkpoint_aggregator`, `commit_model`, `result_committer`, `result_translation`
- `gossip-persistence-inmemory` must be added as a dev-dependency in `Cargo.toml`

### Part C: Wire the durability test module into `lib.rs`

Add a `#[cfg(test)]` module declaration for `runtime_durability_tests` in `lib.rs`:

```rust

mod runtime_durability_tests;
```

### Part D: Add dev-dependency

Add to `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
gossip-persistence-inmemory.workspace = true
rstest.workspace = true
tempfile = "3"
```

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs` | Append the readiness gate test (Part A) |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` | **Create** this file with the 6 durability tests (Part B) |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Wire `runtime_durability_tests` module (Part C); remove `pub checkpoint_hint` from `AssignmentOutcome` if EP2.9.1 has not |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/Cargo.toml` | Add `gossip-persistence-inmemory` dev-dependency (Part D) |

### Dependency chain and what can be added when

**Part A (readiness gate test):** Can only be added AFTER all its assertions can pass:
- The `!lib_src.contains("pub checkpoint_hint")` assertion requires either EP2.9.1 or this task to remove the `checkpoint_hint` field from `AssignmentOutcome`.
- The `lib_src.contains("mod runtime_durability_tests;")` assertion requires Part C.
- The `!commit_sink_src.contains("pub struct DurableCommitSink")` assertion requires EP2.9.1.
- Therefore: Part A requires EP2.9.1 + Parts B and C to all land together.

**Part B (durability tests):** Requires EP2.2 (`commit_model`), EP2.3 (`result_translation`), EP2.4 (`result_committer`), and EP2.5 (`checkpoint_aggregator`) to have landed their modules in `gossip-scanner-runtime`. Cannot be added until those modules exist.

**Part C (module wiring):** Trivial, but pointless without Part B.

**Part D (dev-dependency):** Can be added independently at any time.

**Conclusion:** All four parts must land as a single unit AFTER EP2.9.1 and the EP2.2–EP2.5 modules exist. The implementer should verify all prerequisites are met before starting.

### Patterns to follow

- The existing test file `lib_tests.rs` uses `use super::*;` to import from `lib.rs`. The readiness gate test needs no additional imports (only `include_str!` which is a built-in macro).
- The durability test file uses full qualified `crate::` imports for the four modules and `use` for external crates.
- Test functions follow the pattern: descriptive snake_case name, setup, act, assert with clear failure messages.

### Handling `checkpoint_hint` removal

The readiness gate test asserts `!lib_src.contains("pub checkpoint_hint")`. Currently `AssignmentOutcome` at `lib.rs:684` has `pub checkpoint_hint`. This field must be removed (or made non-pub) by the time Part A is added. If EP2.9.1 does not remove it, this task must do so:

2. Remove `checkpoint_hint: None` from `ordered_content.rs` (lines 89, 163) and `git_repo.rs` (lines 105, 161).
3. Remove `ScanCheckpoint` type if it becomes unused.

Check whether EP2.9.1 handles this before duplicating the work.

title: Extend differential oracle to multi-run topology
description:
## Context

The differential oracle tests a single-run, single-tenant topology
(N_WORKERS=4, N_SHARDS=8, one RunId). Real deployments have multiple
concurrent runs per tenant, which exercises run-level isolation, cross-run
claim routing, and run terminal transitions more thoroughly.

## Current State

DifferentialOracle::new() calls with_workers_and_shards(N_WORKERS, N_SHARDS)
which seeds a single run (RunId(1)). All arb_sim_op operations target this
single run.

## Desired State

Support multi-run topologies:
- Parameterize the oracle to seed N_RUNS (e.g., 2-3) runs
- Extend arb_sim_op or create a multi-run strategy that targets different runs
- Verify cross-run isolation: mutations on run A don't affect run B's state

## Implementation Guidance

- File: crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle_etcd.rs
- CoordinationSim::with_workers_and_shards seeds one run; may need a
  with_multi_run_topology builder or manual run creation via create_run
- arb_sim_op generates ShardKeys with RunId(1) hardcoded; needs extension
- comparable_state already handles multiple runs via BTreeMap iteration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Oracle supports at least 2 concurrent runs
- [ ] Operations target different runs
- [ ] No state drift between backends
- [ ] cargo test --features test-support -- --ignored passes
- [ ] cargo fmt / clippy / doc clean

title: Batch shard reads in ObservedEtcdCoordinator::refresh_run_state
description:
## Context

ObservedEtcdCoordinator::refresh_run_state issues one etcd round-trip per
known shard ID when refreshing the cache after a mutation. With N_SHARDS=8
this means 8 sequential point reads per successful step. As topology grows,
this becomes a performance bottleneck for the oracle.

## Current State

refresh_run_state (differential_oracle_etcd.rs ~line 330 after cleanup):

```rust
for shard_id in known_ids {
    let key = ShardKey::new(run, shard_id);
    match self.inner.test_load_shard_snapshot(tenant, key) { ... }
}
```

Each test_load_shard_snapshot is a separate etcd Get RPC.

## Desired State

Batch shard reads into a single etcd range query or use test_load_all_shard_snapshots
(if it exists or can be added) to fetch all shards for a (tenant, run) in one RPC.

## Implementation Guidance

- File: crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle_etcd.rs
- May need a new test helper on EtcdCoordinator: test_load_all_shard_snapshots
- EtcdCoordinator can do prefix range scans — a range query on the shard
  prefix for a run would fetch all shards in one RPC
- Backend helper: crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend/test_support.rs

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] refresh_run_state uses at most 2 etcd RPCs per call (1 run + 1 shard range)
- [ ] Oracle behavior unchanged (same state snapshots)
- [ ] cargo test --features test-support -- --ignored passes
- [ ] cargo fmt / clippy / doc clean

title: Introduce CommittedUnitCount(u64) newtype for type-safe committed-units fields
description:
## Context

Code review finding F4 on feature/shared-write-context identified that `committed_units` 
and `record_count` are raw `u64`/`NonZeroU64` throughout the commit model. A newtype 
would prevent accidental mixing with other u64-typed fields (sequence numbers, byte counts).

## Current State

Raw u64 used in:
- `CommitScope::committed_units` field (crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:193) — `NonZeroU64`
- `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt::record_count()` return type (crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs)
- Validation site in `PageCommit<FindingsDurable>::record_done_ledger` comparing `scope.committed_units().get()` vs `receipt.record_count()`
- All test helpers passing raw u64 for these fields

## Desired State

A `CommittedUnitCount(NonZeroU64)` newtype (or similar) wrapping the committed-units 
concept, used consistently across CommitScope, DoneLedgerCommitReceipt, and the 
validation site. Consider also `SequenceNo(u64)` for `CompletedUnit::sequence_no` 
if the pattern proves ergonomic.

## Implementation Guidance

- Define the newtype in `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/` or `gossip-contracts/src/identity/`
- Update CommitScope, DoneLedgerCommitReceipt, and the PageCommit validation
- Update all test helpers
- This is a breaking change across crate boundaries (gossip-contracts + gossip-scanner-runtime)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CommittedUnitCount` newtype replaces raw u64 in committed_units fields
- [ ] Validation in record_done_ledger uses the newtype for comparison
- [ ] All test helpers updated
- [ ] cargo fmt && cargo check && cargo clippy && cargo test pass

`rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` in `result_translation.rs` converts the engine-local
positional `rule_id: u32` (an array index into `rules_cold`) into a 32-byte
`RuleFingerprint` by writing LE bytes and zero-filling. Since `rule_id` is assigned
by position during engine construction, reordering or adding/removing rules between
builds causes the same numeric ID to map to a different rule. Because `RuleFingerprint`
feeds into `FindingId` derivation via `FindingIdInputs`, this silently corrupts durable
finding deduplication and done-ledger counts.

The `RuleFingerprint` type's own invariant (`finding.rs:144`) states: "The same rule
definition MUST always produce the same `RuleFingerprint`." The current code violates
this contract.

## Current State

The bug function zero-pads a positional index into 32 bytes:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_translation.rs:408-420
pub(crate) fn rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id(rule_id: u32) -> RuleFingerprint {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
    bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&rule_id.to_le_bytes());
    RuleFingerprint::from_bytes(bytes)
}
```

Called at two sites:
- `result_translation.rs:374` in `translate_findings()`
- `commit_sink.rs:156` in `DurableCommitSink::derive_identity_record()`

`FsFindingRecord` (`store.rs:42-57`) carries only `rule_id: u32`, with no stable
rule identity.

The engine already stores rule names in `RuleCold.name` (`rule_repr.rs:671`) and
exposes them via `Engine::rule_name(rule_id)` (`core.rs:2031`). The contracts crate
already defines `domain::RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1` (`domain.rs:90`) for BLAKE3 derive-key
mode, but it is currently unused.

## Desired State

`RuleFingerprint` is derived from the rule's stable name via BLAKE3 derive-key using
the existing `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1` domain constant. The fingerprint is precomputed
once per rule at engine construction time (cold path) and stored in `RuleCold`. A
public accessor `Engine::rule_fingerprint(rule_id) -> RuleFingerprint` exposes it.

The `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` function is deleted. Callers obtain the stable
fingerprint through a lookup table or engine accessor instead of deriving it from
the positional index.

## Implementation Guidance

### Approach

Precompute fingerprints at engine build time. This is preferred because:
- `RuleCold` already holds `name` and is indexed by `rule_id`
- Precomputation amortizes the BLAKE3 cost to engine construction (cold path)
- No changes to `FsFindingRecord` struct size (preserves 80-byte cache constraint)
- `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1` already exists for exactly this purpose

Use rule `name` (not `encode_policy`) as the fingerprint input. `PolicyHash` already
captures semantic changes for cache invalidation. `RuleFingerprint` serves a different
purpose: stable cross-run dedup. If a rule's regex changes, the finding should keep
the same identity (same rule name, same secret, same location = same finding).

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/finding.rs` | Add `derive_rule_fingerprint(name: &str) -> RuleFingerprint` using `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1` domain | Canonical derivation function next to the type definition |
| `crates/scanner-engine/src/engine/rule_repr.rs` | Add `fingerprint: RuleFingerprint` field to `RuleCold` | Precomputed at build time |
| `crates/scanner-engine/src/engine/core.rs` | Compute fingerprint during rule compilation; add `Engine::rule_fingerprint(rule_id) -> RuleFingerprint` | Public accessor parallel to `rule_name()` |
| `crates/scanner-engine/src/api.rs` | No changes expected | `FindingRec` keeps `rule_id: u32` for scan-loop hot path |
| `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/engine_trait.rs` | Add `rule_fingerprint(rule_id: u32) -> RuleFingerprint` to `ScanEngine` trait | Exposes stable fingerprint to callers |
| `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/engine_impl.rs` | Implement new trait method | Delegates to `Engine::rule_fingerprint()` |
| `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/engine_stub.rs` | Implement new trait method for mock | Stub can derive from mock rule names |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_translation.rs` | Delete `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id`; accept a fingerprint lookup closure or table; use it in `translate_findings` | Core fix |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs` | Replace `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` call with lookup | Second call site |

### Patterns to Follow

- Cached BLAKE3 hasher pattern: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/hashing.rs:62-91`
  uses `LazyLock<Hasher>` for amortized derive-key setup.
- `domain_hasher()` at `hashing.rs:131` creates a derive-key hasher from a domain string.
- `derive_from_cached()` at `hashing.rs:116` clones a cached hasher, updates with
  canonical bytes, and finalizes to `[u8;32]`.
- `Engine::rule_name()` at `core.rs:2031` — the new `rule_fingerprint()` should
  follow the same pattern.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1` | `identity/domain.rs:90` | Domain tag for BLAKE3 derive-key |
| `domain_hasher()` | `identity/hashing.rs:131` | Create cached hasher for rule fingerprint |
| `finalize_32()` | `identity/hashing.rs:141` | Finalize BLAKE3 hasher to `[u8;32]` |
| `RuleFingerprint::from_bytes()` | `identity/finding.rs` | Wrap derived bytes |

### Blast Radius

| Caller/Dependent | File | Relationship |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `translate_findings()` | `result_translation.rs:374` | Direct call — must change to use lookup |
| `DurableCommitSink::derive_identity_record()` | `commit_sink.rs:156` | Direct call — must change (may be deleted by gossip-9065.7.4) |
| `build_persistence_batch()` | `local_fs_owner.rs:538` | Builds `FsFindingRecord` — unaffected if struct shape preserved |
| `FindingRecord::new()` | `persistence/findings.rs:79` | Consumer of `RuleFingerprint` — unchanged |
| `derive_finding_id()` | `identity/finding.rs:361` | Consumer of `FindingIdInputs.rule` — unchanged |
| Test assertions | `result_translation.rs:869-893` | Must update to use new derivation |
| Sim mutation | `sim/mutation/family.rs:113, adapter.rs:371` | `rule_id()` usage — same fix needed |

## Code References

See Current State section for inline snippets of the bug function, call sites,
`FsFindingRecord`, `RuleCold`, `Engine::rule_name()`, `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1`,
and the `RuleFingerprint` type invariant.

## Risk Analysis

- **Low risk of regression**: the change only affects identity derivation, not
  scan correctness. All existing `FindingId`s in persistence will change on
  first run with the fix — this is acceptable since the old IDs were
  non-deterministic anyway.
- **No hot-path impact**: fingerprint is precomputed at engine build time (cold)
  and looked up by index at translation time (warm).
- **No unsafe code** in any affected path.

## Testing Strategy

- Unit tests in `result_translation.rs`: verify that two rules with the same
  name produce the same fingerprint and different names produce different ones.
- Verify that reordering rules (same names, different positions) produces the
  same `FindingId` for the same (tenant, item, rule_name, secret).
- Existing `translate_item_result` tests continue to pass with updated assertions.
- Property test: for any permutation of a rule set, fingerprints are identical
  by name.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9065.7.4 | Remove DurableCommitSink from authoritative path | relates-to (will delete one of two call sites) |
| gossip-9065.9.1 | Delete old DurableCommitSink | relates-to |
| gossip-9065.4 | Implement ResultCommitter | relates-to (consumes PersistenceTranslation) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` is deleted
- [ ] `RuleFingerprint` is derived from rule name via BLAKE3 `RULE_FINGERPRINT_V1`
- [ ] Fingerprint is precomputed at engine build time in `RuleCold`
- [ ] `Engine::rule_fingerprint(rule_id)` public accessor exists
- [ ] `ScanEngine` trait exposes `rule_fingerprint()`
- [ ] `translate_findings` and `commit_sink` use stable fingerprint lookup
- [ ] Same rule name at different positions produces identical `FindingId`
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/hashing.rs` — cached hasher patterns
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/domain.rs` — all domain constants
- `crates/scanner-engine/src/engine/compile.rs` — engine construction where `RuleCold` is populated

title: Add Stormy fault-level differential oracle runs
description:
## Context

The differential oracles on `feature/differential-oracle` validate behavioral
equivalence between coordination backends by feeding identical `SimOp` sequences
to two `CoordinationSim` harnesses and comparing events, state, and invariant
results at every step. Currently all oracle runs use `FaultLevel::SunnyDay`
(zero faults), leaving fault-tolerance code paths unexercised in cross-backend
comparison.

## Current State

Both oracle test files hardcode `FaultLevel::SunnyDay`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle.rs:75-78
let memory = CoordinationSim::with_backend(seed, FaultLevel::SunnyDay, memory_backend)
    .with_workers_and_shards(N_WORKERS, N_SHARDS);
let sim_etcd = CoordinationSim::with_backend(seed, FaultLevel::SunnyDay, sim_etcd_backend)
    .with_workers_and_shards(N_WORKERS, N_SHARDS);
```

`FaultLevel::Stormy` is already fully implemented in the harness:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs:244-251
FaultLevel::Stormy => Self {
    lease_expiry_ppm: 100_000, // 10%
    pause_ppm: 50_000,         // 5%
    pause_range: 1..=5,
    time_jump_ppm: 100_000,    // 10%
    time_jump_range: 50..=200,
},
```

Existing harness tests (`harness_tests.rs:554-588`) already exercise Stormy for
single-backend correctness and determinism, but no cross-backend oracle uses it.

## Desired State

A new test function runs the differential oracle at `FaultLevel::Stormy`,
confirming that `InMemoryCoordinator` and `SimEtcdCoordinator` remain
behaviorally equivalent under moderate fault injection (lease expiry, worker
pause, time jumps).

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle.rs` | Parameterize `build_oracle` by `FaultLevel`, add Stormy test function | Core change |

### Patterns to Follow
- `harness_tests.rs:554-569` — Stormy-level test that asserts rejections > 0
- `harness_tests.rs:581-588` — Determinism test confirming same seed → same results
- Existing `build_oracle(seed)` pattern — add `level: FaultLevel` parameter

### Utilities to Reuse
- `FaultLevel::Stormy` and `FaultConfig::for_level` (already implemented in `sim/mod.rs`)
- `arb_sim_op` strategy (unchanged — same op generation for both fault levels)
- Existing `DifferentialOracle::run_sequence` (no changes needed)

### Blast Radius
- Oracle comparison logic (`support/oracle.rs`) needs no changes — `ComparableBackendState` already normalizes all backend-specific details
- S1–S9 invariants already run at every step and handle fault-induced state transitions
- Both backends use the same seeded PRNG, so fault timing is deterministic and identical

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs:192-197 — FaultLevel enum
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FaultLevel {
    SunnyDay = 1,
    Stormy = 2,
    Radioactive = 3,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness.rs:1098 — with_backend accepts level
pub fn with_backend(seed: u64, level: FaultLevel, backend: B) -> Self
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness_tests.rs:554-560 — Stormy test pattern
#[test]
fn report_properties() {
    let report = default_sim(42, FaultLevel::Stormy).run(500, 200);
    assert!(report.event_counts.values().sum::<usize>() > 0);
    let rejected = report.event_counts.get(&SimEventKind::Rejected).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    assert!(rejected > 0, "expected rejections in Stormy mode");
}
```

## Design Notes

**Why Stormy, not Radioactive?** Stormy provides moderate fault rates (10%
lease expiry, 10% time-jump) sufficient to exercise fault-tolerance paths
without overwhelming CI with false positives. Radioactive (20% rates) can be
added later if Stormy passes cleanly.

**Non-determinism concern**: Both backends inherit from the same `CoordinationSim`
harness and consume PRNG calls in identical order for the same seed. Fault
injection timing is therefore identical across backends — the oracle's
step-by-step comparison remains valid.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9020 | Extend DST to etcd backend + cross-component | parent epic |
| gossip-9020.3 | Add progressive fault injection to SimulatedEtcdKV | predecessor (infrastructure this task uses) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Stormy-level differential oracle test passes for 50+ seed variations
- [ ] Stormy runs verify rejections > 0 (faults are actually exercised)
- [ ] No regression in SunnyDay test pass rate
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers
- `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness_tests.rs` — existing Stormy test patterns
- `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/fault_injector.rs` — fault injection mechanism
- `docs/gossip-coordination/simulation-harness.md` — simulation architecture docs

title: Move DifferentialOracle to gossip-coordination test-support
description:
## Context

The generic `DifferentialOracle<L, R>` compares two `SimulationBackend` implementations step-by-step, checking that emitted events, full shard/run state, and invariant results match after every operation. It is the primary cross-backend correctness tool for the coordination subsystem. Currently it lives inside the `gossip-coordination-etcd` test crate, but it is backend-agnostic (generic over `SimulationBackend`). Two test binaries include it via `#[path = "support/oracle.rs"]`, which is fragile and prevents other crates from reusing it.

## Current State

The oracle struct and all its helpers live in a single file:

**`crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs`** (lines 1-431)

Two test binaries include it with `#[path]`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle.rs:8-9
#[path = "support/oracle.rs"]
mod oracle;
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle_etcd.rs:10-11
#[path = "support/oracle.rs"]
mod oracle;
```

The oracle depends only on types from `gossip-contracts` and `gossip-coordination`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:8-15
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use gossip_contracts::coordination::{PooledCursor, PooledShardSpec, PooledSpawned};
use gossip_coordination::sim::{CoordinationSim, SimIntrospection, SimOp, SimulationBackend};
use gossip_coordination::{
    LogicalTime, OpId, OpKind, RunConfig, RunId, RunOpKind, RunOpResult, RunRecord, RunStatus,
    ShardId, ShardKey, ShardRecord, ShardStatus, TenantId, WorkerId,
};
```

The `gossip-coordination` crate already has a `test-support` feature and a `sim::test_util` module gated behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` (see `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs:77-78`).

## Desired State

The `DifferentialOracle<L, R>` struct and all associated types (`ComparableShardState`, `ComparableRunState`, `ComparableBackendState`, `ComparableLease`, `ComparableShardOpLogEntry`, `ComparableRunOpLogEntry`, `DriftComparison`, `comparable_state()`, `panic_drift()`) move to a new submodule inside `gossip-coordination::sim::test_util` (e.g., `sim::test_util::oracle`), gated behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`. The unit test in `oracle.rs` (`oracle_detects_deliberate_drift`) moves with it.

After the move:
- Both etcd test binaries import via `use gossip_coordination::sim::test_util::oracle::DifferentialOracle;` instead of `#[path]`.
- The `oracle.rs` file is deleted from `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/`.
- Any future crate implementing `SimulationBackend` can use the oracle by depending on `gossip-coordination` with `features = ["test-support"]`.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/test_util.rs` | Add `pub mod oracle;` submodule declaration |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/test_util/oracle.rs` (new) | Move oracle code here; change `pub(crate)` to `pub` on `DifferentialOracle` and its constructor/methods |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs` | Verify `test_util` module is already public under `test-support` feature (it is, line 78) |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/Cargo.toml` | Likely no change needed; `gossip-contracts` is already a dependency |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle.rs` | Replace `#[path = "support/oracle.rs"] mod oracle;` with `use gossip_coordination::sim::test_util::oracle::DifferentialOracle;` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/differential_oracle_etcd.rs` | Same replacement |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs` | Delete |

### Patterns to Follow

- The existing `test_util.rs` is a flat file. Converting it to a directory module (`test_util/mod.rs` + `test_util/oracle.rs`) is the cleanest approach. Move current `test_util.rs` content to `test_util/mod.rs` and add `pub mod oracle;`.
- The oracle's `pub(crate)` visibility on `DifferentialOracle::new` and `DifferentialOracle::run_sequence` must become `pub` since it will be used by external crates.
- The tripwire size assertions (`const _: () = { ... }`) should stay in the oracle module since they guard oracle correctness.

### Utilities to Reuse

- `gossip_coordination::sim::test_util` already exists and is the canonical home for sim test infrastructure.
- `gossip_contracts::test_util::selected_seeds_from_env` is already used by the oracle's callers.

### Blast Radius

- Only the two differential oracle test binaries in `gossip-coordination-etcd` import the oracle today.
- The `concurrent_cas_contention.rs` and `sim_mega_tests.rs` tests do NOT use the oracle, so they are unaffected.
- The `support/mod.rs` file (`ObservedEtcdCoordinator`) stays in place — it is etcd-specific.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:18-25
pub(crate) struct DifferentialOracle<L: SimulationBackend, R: SimulationBackend> {
```

title: Move done-ledger oracle to gossip-done-ledger-postgres
description:
## Context

The done-ledger differential oracle compares `InMemoryDoneLedger` (reference implementation) against `DoneLedgerPg` (PostgreSQL backend) by replaying randomized `batch_upsert` sequences and asserting receipt and state equality. The test currently lives in `gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/differential_oracle.rs`, but it depends on `gossip-done-ledger-postgres` as a dev-dependency. This creates an inverted dependency: the in-memory reference crate should not know about a specific storage backend. The natural direction is for the postgres crate to depend on the in-memory crate for its reference implementation, not the other way around.

## Current State

**`crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/differential_oracle.rs`** (lines 1-231) — the full test lives here.

The dev-dependency that creates the inversion:

```toml
# crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/Cargo.toml:23-24
[dev-dependencies]
gossip-done-ledger-postgres = { workspace = true, features = ["test-utils"] }
gossip-pg-common = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }
postgres = "0.19"
```

The test imports from `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/differential_oracle.rs:15-16
use gossip_done_ledger_postgres::{DoneLedgerPg, schema::DONE_LEDGER_ENTRIES_TABLE};
use gossip_persistence_inmemory::InMemoryDoneLedger;
```

Meanwhile, `gossip-done-ledger-postgres/Cargo.toml` (lines 1-29) has no dependency on `gossip-persistence-inmemory` at all today — neither in `[dependencies]` nor `[dev-dependencies]`.

## Desired State

The test file moves to `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/tests/differential_oracle.rs`. The dependency direction becomes natural:

- `gossip-done-ledger-postgres` adds `gossip-persistence-inmemory` as a `[dev-dependencies]` entry (it already has `gossip-contracts` and `gossip-pg-common` as dev-deps).
- `gossip-persistence-inmemory` removes its dev-dependencies on `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`, `gossip-pg-common`, and `postgres`.

After the move:
- `gossip-persistence-inmemory` has zero knowledge of any postgres crate.
- The test binary runs under `cargo test -p gossip-done-ledger-postgres`.
- The env var names (`GOSSIP_DONE_DIFF_SEED`, `GOSSIP_DONE_DIFF_CASES`) and repro command are updated to reference the new crate.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/tests/differential_oracle.rs` (new) | Move test file here; update `use` paths (`InMemoryDoneLedger` import path stays the same since it is a crate dependency) |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/Cargo.toml` | Add `gossip-persistence-inmemory` to `[dev-dependencies]`; add `rand`, `rand_chacha`, `postgres` dev-deps |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/differential_oracle.rs` | Delete |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/Cargo.toml` | Remove `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`, `gossip-pg-common`, and `postgres` from `[dev-dependencies]` |

### Patterns to Follow

- The test uses `#[test] #[ignore]` since it requires a live postgres instance. This pattern is already used in `gossip-done-ledger-postgres` (see its existing tests).
- The `repro_command` function (line 24-28) must be updated to reference `-p gossip-done-ledger-postgres` instead of `-p gossip-persistence-inmemory`.
- The test uses `gossip_pg_common::test_support::create_test_db()` which is already a dev-dep of `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`.

### Utilities to Reuse

- `gossip_contracts::test_util::selected_seeds_from_env` — already used by the test (line 14).
- `gossip_contracts::test_util::done_record` — test helper for constructing `DoneLedgerRecord` values.
- `gossip_pg_common::test_support::create_test_db` — already a dev-dep of `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`.

### Blast Radius

- Only this single test file references `gossip-done-ledger-postgres` from `gossip-persistence-inmemory`.
- No other test in `gossip-persistence-inmemory` depends on postgres. Removing the dev-deps is safe.
- The `gossip-persistence-inmemory` crate may have other tests (proptest, unit tests) that are unaffected.

## Code References

```rust
        "GOSSIP_DONE_DIFF_SEED={seed} cargo test -p gossip-persistence-inmemory \
         done_ledger_pg_matches_in_memory_differential_oracle -- --ignored --exact --nocapture"
    )
}
```

After move, this becomes:
```rust

    format!(
        "GOSSIP_DONE_DIFF_SEED={seed} cargo test -p gossip-done-ledger-postgres \
```

title: Add spec_metadata to SimIntrospection and oracle comparison
description:
## Context

The differential oracle's `ComparableShardState` compares shard records across backends by normalizing away storage details. It includes `spec_start` and `spec_end` (via `spec_bounds()`) but omits `spec_metadata` — the connector-opaque metadata field stored in `PooledShardSpec`. This means metadata drift between backends goes undetected. A new `spec_metadata()` accessor on `SimIntrospection` is needed, with implementations in all backends, and inclusion in the oracle's comparable state.

## Current State

The `SimIntrospection` trait defines `spec_bounds()` but has no `spec_metadata()` method:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/backend.rs:140-144
/// Return the shard range bounds `[start, end)` as borrowed slices.
///
/// Borrow is tied to `self` because pooled fields are slab-backed.
/// This keeps split and cursor-bound validation allocation-free.
fn spec_bounds<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> (&'a [u8], &'a [u8]);
```

`PooledShardSpec` stores three fields, but the oracle only reads two:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/pooled.rs:162-166
pub struct PooledShardSpec {
    key_range_start: ByteSlot,
    key_range_end: ByteSlot,
    metadata: ByteSlot,
}
```

The `metadata` accessor already exists on `PooledShardSpec`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/pooled.rs:203-206
/// Connector-opaque metadata.
#[inline]
pub fn metadata<'a>(&self, slab: &'a ByteSlab) -> &'a [u8] {
    slab.get(self.metadata)
}
```

The oracle's `ComparableShardState` lacks a metadata field:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:63-76
struct ComparableShardState {
    status: ShardStatus,
    park_reason: Option<gossip_coordination::ParkReason>,
    spec_start: Vec<u8>,
    spec_end: Vec<u8>,
    cursor_last_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    cursor_semantics: gossip_coordination::CursorSemantics,
    lease: Option<ComparableLease>,
    fence_epoch: gossip_coordination::FenceEpoch,
    parent: Option<ShardId>,
    spawned: Vec<ShardId>,
    op_log: Vec<ComparableShardOpLogEntry>,
}
```

And the `comparable_state` function reads bounds but not metadata:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:339
let (start, end) = backend.spec_bounds(record);
```

The tripwire assertion guards `PooledShardSpec` size at 48 bytes (3 `ByteSlot` fields):

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:121
assert!(std::mem::size_of::<PooledShardSpec>() == 48);
```

### Existing `SimIntrospection` implementations

1. **`InMemoryCoordinator`** — `crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs:2819-2824` — has `self.slab` directly.
2. **`SimEtcdCoordinator`** — `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs:477-492` — uses `cached.slab`.
3. **`ObservedEtcdCoordinator`** — `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/mod.rs:238-243` — uses `snapshot.slab()`.
4. **`FaultInjectingIntrospector`** — `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/fault_injector.rs:235-237` — delegates to inner.
5. **`FaultingSessionBackend`** (test-only) — `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness_tests.rs:340-342` — delegates to inner.

## Desired State

1. `SimIntrospection` gains a `spec_metadata` method:
   ```rust
   fn spec_metadata<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> &'a [u8];
   ```
2. All five implementations provide it (pattern matches `spec_bounds` exactly — same slab access, just calling `record.spec.metadata(slab)` instead of `key_range_start`/`key_range_end`).
3. `ComparableShardState` gains a `spec_metadata: Vec<u8>` field.
4. `comparable_state()` calls `backend.spec_metadata(record).to_vec()` and populates the new field.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/backend.rs` | Add `fn spec_metadata<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> &'a [u8];` to `SimIntrospection` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs` | Implement: `record.spec.metadata(&self.slab)` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/fault_injector.rs` | Delegate: `self.inner.spec_metadata(record)` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness_tests.rs` | Delegate: `self.inner.spec_metadata(record)` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs` | Implement using `cached.slab` pattern matching `spec_bounds` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/mod.rs` | Implement using `snapshot.slab()` pattern matching `spec_bounds` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs` | Add `spec_metadata: Vec<u8>` to `ComparableShardState`; populate in `comparable_state()` |

### Patterns to Follow

- Mirror the `spec_bounds` pattern exactly for each impl. The accessor is `record.spec.metadata(slab)`.
- The `SimEtcdCoordinator` impl should handle the cache-miss case the same way `spec_bounds` does (log a warning and return `&[]`).
- The `FaultInjectingIntrospector` and `FaultingSessionBackend` just delegate to inner.

### Utilities to Reuse

- `PooledShardSpec::metadata(&self, slab: &ByteSlab) -> &[u8]` already exists (`pooled.rs:203-206`).
- No new infrastructure needed.

### Blast Radius

- Adding a method to `SimIntrospection` is a breaking change to all implementors, but all five are in-tree and listed above.
- The oracle's `ComparableShardState` gains a field, which changes the tripwire assertion on `PooledShardSpec` only if the struct size changes (it won't — no new `ByteSlot` is added to `PooledShardSpec`, just a new trait method reading the existing field).

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs:2819-2824
fn spec_bounds<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> (&'a [u8], &'a [u8]) {
    (
        record.spec.key_range_start(&self.slab),
        record.spec.key_range_end(&self.slab),
    )
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs:477-492
fn spec_bounds<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> (&'a [u8], &'a [u8]) {
    let Some(cached) = self.cached_shard_for_record(record) else {
        tracing::warn!(/* ... */);
        return (&[], &[]);
    };
    (
        record.spec.key_range_start(&cached.slab),
        record.spec.key_range_end(&cached.slab),
    )
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/mod.rs:238-243
fn spec_bounds<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> (&'a [u8], &'a [u8]) {
    let snapshot = self.snapshot_for_record(record);
    (
        record.spec.key_range_start(snapshot.slab()),
        record.spec.key_range_end(snapshot.slab()),
    )
}
```

## Related Work

- `gossip-9123` (tombstone) — stub for this same task, being replaced by this fully detailed version.
- `gossip-9121` / D2 task — the oracle may move to `gossip-coordination` first; this task can be done before or after, but the file paths in the oracle module will change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `SimIntrospection` has a `spec_metadata` method.
2. All five implementations compile and return the correct metadata bytes.
3. `ComparableShardState` includes `spec_metadata: Vec<u8>`.
4. `comparable_state()` populates `spec_metadata` from `backend.spec_metadata(record)`.
5. The oracle self-test (`oracle_detects_deliberate_drift`) still passes.
6. `cargo test -p gossip-coordination` passes.
7. `cargo test -p gossip-coordination-etcd --features test-support` passes.
8. `cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.
9. `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` passes.

## Pointers

- `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/backend.rs:70-171` — `SimIntrospection` trait definition.
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/pooled.rs:203-206` — `PooledShardSpec::metadata` accessor.
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:63-76` — `ComparableShardState` struct.
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/tests/support/oracle.rs:335-374` — `comparable_state()` function.

title: Add post-dequeue cancellation check in commit pipeline worker
Add debug_assert for unreachable KindMismatch path in commit pipeline
Enforce findings-to-OVID evidence chain in ResultCommitter scanned-request validation
description:
## Context

`ResultCommitter::validate_request()` enforces referential integrity, tenant
consistency, write-context matching, and findings-count agreement — but the
chain validation is incomplete for scanned statuses. A request with FindingRecords
but zero OccurrenceRecords and zero ObservationRecords passes all checks, because:

- Referential integrity only checks *downward* (occurrences reference findings,
  observations reference occurrences) — empty layers trivially pass.
- The OVID check (done-ledger key vs observation OVID) only iterates observations,
  which are absent.
- `distinct_findings_count()` counts FindingIds regardless of whether any
  occurrence/observation evidence exists for the target item version.

This means the module can durably claim "item X was scanned with N findings"
without persisting any occurrence or observation evidence for item X, or mix
stable findings from one item with the done-ledger row for another.

## Current State

`validate_request()` at `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs:348-435`
performs these checks in order:

```rust
// result_committer.rs:368-371 — referential integrity (downward only)
let findings = request.findings();
findings.validate_observation_identity()?;
findings.validate_referential_integrity()?;
```

```rust
// result_committer.rs:393-407 — OVID check on observations ONLY
let expected_ovid = done_ledger.key().ovid_hash();
for (index, observation) in findings.observations().iter().enumerate() {
    // ...
    let actual_ovid = observation.ovid_hash();
    if actual_ovid != expected_ovid {
        return Err(ResultCommitRequestError::ObservationOvidMismatch { ... });
    }
}
```

```rust
// result_committer.rs:417-432 — count check uses findings alone
let distinct_findings = distinct_findings_count(findings)?;
if done_ledger.status().is_scanned() {
    let expected = done_ledger.findings_count();
    if expected != distinct_findings {
        return Err(ResultCommitRequestError::FindingsCountMismatch { ... });
    }
} else if !findings.is_empty() {
    return Err(...);
}
```

The `distinct_findings_count` function at line 438-448 collects FindingIds into
a HashSet, with no reference to occurrences or the target OVID:

```rust
// result_committer.rs:438-448
fn distinct_findings_count(
    findings: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>,
) -> Result<u32, ResultCommitRequestError> {
    let count = findings
        .findings()
        .iter()
        .map(|f| f.finding_id())
        .collect::<HashSet<_>>()
        .len();
    u32::try_from(count).map_err(|_| ResultCommitRequestError::DistinctFindingsOverflow { count })
}
```

Key data model facts (from `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs`):
- `FindingRecord` (layer 1): version-independent, carries `StableItemId` but no OVID/ObjectVersionId
- `OccurrenceRecord` (layer 2): carries `object_version_id: ObjectVersionId`, references a FindingId
- `ObservationRecord` (layer 3): carries `ovid_hash: OvidHash`, references an OccurrenceId
- `DoneLedgerKey`: carries `ovid_hash: OvidHash`

The chain linking findings to the target OVID is:
Finding -> Occurrence (has ObjectVersionId) -> Observation (has OvidHash) -> DoneLedger (has OvidHash)

Without occurrences and observations, findings float free of any item version binding.

## Desired State

For scanned statuses (`ScannedClean` and `ScannedWithFindings`), `validate_request()`
should enforce the complete evidence chain:

1. Every finding counted toward `findings_count` must be reachable through at
   least one occurrence in the batch.
2. Every occurrence in the batch must carry an `object_version_id` consistent
   with the done-ledger's target item version.
3. Every occurrence must have at least one observation in the batch (observations
   are what carry the OVID that is checked against the done-ledger key).

Rule 1 is the most important: it closes the gap where findings-only batches
satisfy the count. Rules 2-3 strengthen the chain but may need to be evaluated
against the data model — `OccurrenceRecord` carries `ObjectVersionId` while
`DoneLedgerKey` carries `OvidHash` (derived from `StableItemId + VersionId`),
so a direct hash comparison is not possible at the occurrence layer without
additional context. The observation layer's OVID check already covers this
when observations are present.

Minimum viable fix: For `ScannedWithFindings` status, require that the
occurrence slice is non-empty and that every FindingId in the findings slice
has at least one referencing OccurrenceRecord. This ensures findings cannot
be counted without version-scoped evidence.

Add new error variants as needed (e.g., `FindingWithoutOccurrence`,
`OccurrenceWithoutObservation`).

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Add upward-chain validation in `validate_request()` scanned branch | Core fix |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Add error variants to `ResultCommitRequestError` | Support new rejection reasons |

### Patterns to Follow
The existing downward referential integrity check in
`FindingsUpsertBatch::validate_referential_integrity()`
(`crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:736`) builds HashSets
of parent IDs and checks children against them. The upward check follows the
same pattern in reverse: build a HashSet of occurrence `finding_id` values
and verify every finding in the batch has at least one entry.

### Utilities to Reuse
- `HashSet` is already imported and used for `distinct_findings_count`
- `FindingsUpsertBatch` accessors: `.findings()`, `.occurrences()`, `.observations()`
- Existing `ResultCommitRequestError` enum for new variants

### Blast Radius
| Caller/Dependent | File | Relationship |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `ResultCommitter::commit_item` | `result_committer.rs:309` | Calls `validate_request` |
| `ResultCommitter::commit_translation` | `result_committer.rs:288` | Delegates to `commit_item` |
| `run_commit_stage` | `commit_pipeline.rs:424` | Pipeline worker calling `commit_translation` |
| Test suite | `result_committer.rs:456-1319` | Multiple tests exercise validation paths |

All existing callers go through `translate_item_result()` which produces
correctly-structured batches, so this change should not break any existing
happy paths. The fix catches misuse of the lower-level `commit_item()` API.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:168-175 — OccurrenceRecord fields
pub struct OccurrenceRecord {
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    occurrence_id: OccurrenceId,
    finding_id: FindingId,
    object_version_id: ObjectVersionId,
    byte_offset: u64,
    byte_length: NonZeroU64,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:736-761 — existing downward integrity
// validate_referential_integrity checks:
// 1. tenant consistency
// 2. occurrences -> findings (every occ references an existing finding)
// 3. observations -> occurrences (every obs references an existing occ)
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:83-114 — DoneLedgerKey with ovid_hash
pub struct DoneLedgerKey {
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    policy_hash: PolicyHash,
    ovid_hash: OvidHash,
}
```

## Testing Strategy

Add regression tests to the existing test suite in `result_committer.rs`:

1. **findings-only scanned request**: 1 FindingRecord, 0 occurrences, 0
   observations, `ScannedWithFindings` done-ledger with `findings_count=1`.
   Must be rejected before any write.

2. **occurrences-without-observations**: FindingRecords + OccurrenceRecords
   but 0 ObservationRecords for a scanned status. Evaluate whether this should
   be rejected (depends on whether observations are contractually required for
   scanned commits — check `translate_item_result` output for guidance).

3. **occurrences for wrong object version**: FindingRecords + OccurrenceRecords
   with a different `ObjectVersionId` than what the done-ledger OVID implies.
   This may require enriching the validation if feasible given the ID types.

Use the existing `assert_validation_rejects` helper at line 1028 for consistent
test structure.

## Related Work

- [ ] The findings-count check for scanned statuses verifies that each counted finding has at least one occurrence in the batch
- [ ] New error variant(s) added to `ResultCommitRequestError` with clear Display messages
- [ ] Regression test: findings-only scanned request is rejected before any write
- [ ] Regression test: valid scanned request with full chain still succeeds

title: Make CompletedUnit-to-persistence-row mismatch unrepresentable in CommitRequest
description:
## Context

`ResultCommitter::validate_request()` validates findings, done-ledger records,
and write-context consistency but never inspects the `CompletedUnit` bundled
in the `CommitRequest`. The `CommitScope` (which drives checkpoint boundary
advancement) is derived from `completed_unit.checkpoint_boundary()` without
verifying any relationship between that boundary and the persistence rows
being committed.

This means the `commit_item()` public API accepts a `CommitRequest` where a
caller can pair a `CompletedUnit` for stream position B with persistence rows
for item A. The committer would durably persist A's data but return a receipt
whose checkpoint boundary reflects B — potentially advancing the checkpoint
past items that were never committed.

The higher-level `commit_translation()` path couples them correctly from the
caller, so this is not a live bug in the current pipeline. It is a robustness
gap in the lower-level public API.

## Current State

`CommitRequest` at `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs:130-176`
bundles the four components with only debug-mode tenant sampling:

```rust
// commit_model.rs:130-135
pub struct CommitRequest<'a> {
    write_context: WriteContext,
    completed_unit: CompletedUnit,
    findings: FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>,
    done_ledger: &'a [DoneLedgerRecord],
}
```

```rust
// commit_model.rs:145-176 — constructor has debug_assert only
pub fn new(
    write_context: WriteContext,
    completed_unit: CompletedUnit,
    findings: FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>,
    done_ledger: &'a [DoneLedgerRecord],
) -> Self {
    debug_assert!(...); // tenant sampling only
    Self { write_context, completed_unit, findings, done_ledger }
}
```

`CompletedUnit` at `commit_model.rs:49` carries only stream-level identity:

```rust
// commit_model.rs:49-52
pub struct CompletedUnit {
    sequence_no: u64,
    checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary,
}
```

It does NOT carry item identity (no OVID, no StableItemId, no tenant). The
doc on `UnitCommitReceipt::new` (line 263) explicitly notes: "CompletedUnit
does not carry scope identity, so a stronger check is structurally impossible
at this layer."

`validate_request()` at `result_committer.rs:348` destructures the request
and validates everything EXCEPT the completed unit:

```rust
// result_committer.rs:348-349
fn validate_request(request: &CommitRequest<'_>) -> Result<(), ResultCommitRequestError> {
    let write_context = request.write_context();
    // ... validates done_ledger, findings, observations, write_context
    // CompletedUnit is never accessed
}
```

The receipt is then built using the unvalidated boundary:

```rust
// result_committer.rs:321-325
let scope = CommitScope::from_write_context(
    write_context,
    NonZeroU64::MIN,
    completed_unit.checkpoint_boundary().clone(),
);
```

## Desired State

The mismatch between `CompletedUnit` and persistence rows should be
structurally unrepresentable (or at minimum validated). Two approaches:

### Option A: Coupled construction type (preferred)

Introduce a type that bundles `CompletedUnit` with its `PersistenceTranslation`
at construction time, so the commit stage cannot receive them separately.
`commit_translation()` already takes both — the change is to make the coupling
first-class and remove or restrict the raw `commit_item(CommitRequest)` path.

This is the strongest option: if the only way to build a `CommitRequest` is
through a function that holds both the unit and its translation, the caller
cannot pair the wrong ones.

### Option B: Validate at CommitRequest construction

Add item-level identity to `CompletedUnit` (e.g., `OvidHash`) or pass it
alongside, and validate at `CommitRequest::new()` that the done-ledger's
OVID matches. This requires enriching `CompletedUnit` which changes several
call sites.

### Option C: Restrict commit_item visibility

Make `commit_item()` private or `pub(crate)` and require all external callers
to use `commit_translation()`, which already couples the components. This is
the lowest-effort fix but weakens the API surface for future consumers.

The implementing agent should evaluate these options against the existing
call graph and choose the one with the best complexity-to-safety ratio.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs` | Modify `CommitRequest` construction or add coupled type | Structural coupling |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Update `commit_item` / `commit_translation` accordingly | API surface change |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_pipeline.rs` | Update `run_commit_stage` if commit API changes | Consumer of commit_translation |

### Patterns to Follow
`PersistenceTranslation` at `result_translation.rs:147` already bundles the
item-level persistence rows with `ovid_hash`. The coupling pattern should
mirror how that type groups related data at construction.

### Utilities to Reuse
- `PersistenceTranslation::ovid_hash()` for extracting item identity
- `DoneLedgerKey::ovid_hash()` for cross-checking

### Blast Radius
| Caller/Dependent | File | Relationship |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `commit_translation` | `result_committer.rs:288` | Primary entry point |
| `commit_item` | `result_committer.rs:309` | Lower-level entry point |
| `run_commit_stage` | `commit_pipeline.rs:449-451` | Pipeline consumer |
| `QueuedCommit` | `commit_pipeline.rs` | Submission type (holds unit + translation) |
| Test suite | `result_committer.rs:456+` | Tests construct CommitRequest manually |

## Code References

```rust
// commit_pipeline.rs:449-451 — pipeline already couples them correctly
let (write_context, completed_unit, translation) = work.into_parts();
let expected_kind = completed_unit.checkpoint_boundary_kind();
let result = committer.commit_translation(write_context, &completed_unit, &translation);
```

```rust
// result_translation.rs:147-152 — PersistenceTranslation carries ovid_hash
pub struct PersistenceTranslation {
    ovid_hash: OvidHash,
    findings: Vec<FindingRecord>,
    occurrences: Vec<OccurrenceRecord>,
    observations: Vec<ObservationRecord>,
    done_ledger: DoneLedgerRecord,
}
```

```rust
// commit_model.rs:263-270 — UnitCommitReceipt::new acknowledges the gap
// "CompletedUnit does not carry scope identity, so a stronger check is
// structurally impossible at this layer."
```

## Design Notes

This is a robustness improvement, not a live bug fix. The current pipeline
goes through `commit_translation()` which takes both `&CompletedUnit` and
`&PersistenceTranslation` from the same caller context. The risk is future
misuse of the lower-level `commit_item()` API.

The trade-off is between API restriction (easier, lower blast radius) and
structural coupling (harder, but makes misuse impossible by construction).
If Option C (restrict visibility) is chosen, add a code comment documenting
why `commit_item` is not public and what invariant the caller must uphold.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9133 | Enforce findings-to-OVID evidence chain in ResultCommitter scanned-request validation | relates-to: fixes a different validation gap in the same function |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] It is structurally impossible (or validated-at-construction) to pair a CompletedUnit with persistence rows for a different item
- [ ] The commit pipeline (`commit_pipeline.rs`) still compiles and passes tests
- [ ] Regression test: constructing a mismatched CommitRequest either fails at construction or is rejected by validation
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-scanner-runtime`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_pipeline.rs:424-504` — the pipeline consumer that shows how the coupling works today
- `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs:250-306` — `UnitCommitReceipt` boundary check (the only existing cross-check between unit and receipt)
close_reason: Not needed for EP2 work; commit_translation() already couples CompletedUnit and persistence rows correctly, and no upcoming task uses the raw commit_item() API.

title: Defer HashSet allocation to scanned branch and include diagnostic fields in ResultCommitRequestError Display
description:
## Context

Two minor quality issues in `ResultCommitter` validation: an unnecessary
HashSet allocation on invalid requests, and error Display impls that omit
diagnostic fields useful for incident debugging.

## Current State

### HashSet allocation before is_scanned check

At `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs:417-432`,
`distinct_findings_count()` runs unconditionally — it allocates a HashSet
and collects all FindingIds — even when the done-ledger status is not scanned.
For non-scanned statuses, the only check needed is `!findings.is_empty()`,
which is O(1) with no allocation.

```rust
// result_committer.rs:417-432
let distinct_findings = distinct_findings_count(findings)?;
if done_ledger.status().is_scanned() {
    let expected = done_ledger.findings_count();
    if expected != distinct_findings {
        return Err(ResultCommitRequestError::FindingsCountMismatch {
            expected,
            actual: distinct_findings,
        });
    }
} else if !findings.is_empty() {
    return Err(
        ResultCommitRequestError::FindingsPresentForUnscannedStatus {
            status: done_ledger.status(),
        },
    );
}
```

`distinct_findings_count` at line 438-448:

```rust
fn distinct_findings_count(
    findings: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>,
) -> Result<u32, ResultCommitRequestError> {
    let count = findings
        .findings()
        .iter()
        .map(|f| f.finding_id())
        .collect::<HashSet<_>>()
        .len();
    u32::try_from(count).map_err(|_| ResultCommitRequestError::DistinctFindingsOverflow { count })
}
```

### Display impls omit diagnostic fields

At `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs:126-133`:

```rust
// result_committer.rs:126-131 — actual OVID omitted
Self::ObservationOvidMismatch {
    index, expected, ..
} => write!(
    f,
    "observation at index {index} targets a different OVID than expected ({expected:?})"
),
```

The `actual` field is present in the variant but dropped by Display. During
incident review, knowing what OVID was actually present is essential.

```rust
// result_committer.rs:132-135 — both sides omitted
Self::DoneLedgerWriteContextMismatch { .. } => write!(
    f,
    "done-ledger write context does not match the request-level write context"
),
```

Both `expected` and `actual` WriteContext values are boxed in the variant but
the Display output includes neither.

## Desired State

1. Move `distinct_findings_count()` into the `is_scanned()` branch so the
   HashSet is never allocated for non-scanned statuses.

2. Include all diagnostic fields in Display output:
   - `ObservationOvidMismatch`: show both `expected` and `actual` OVIDs
   - `DoneLedgerWriteContextMismatch`: show both `expected` and `actual`
     WriteContexts (or at minimum the differing fields)

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Reorder validation logic to defer HashSet allocation | Avoid allocation on invalid non-scanned requests |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Update Display impl for ObservationOvidMismatch and DoneLedgerWriteContextMismatch | Better diagnostics |

### Patterns to Follow
Other Display impls in the same enum (e.g., `TenantMismatch` at line 112-121)
already include both expected and actual values.

### Utilities to Reuse
None needed.

### Blast Radius
| Caller/Dependent | File | Relationship |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `validate_request` | `result_committer.rs:348` | Only caller of distinct_findings_count |
| Display consumers | logging, error formatting | Output format changes |

The HashSet reordering is a pure refactor — no behavioral change for valid
requests. The Display change alters log output format but not semantics.

## Code References

```rust
// result_committer.rs:112-121 — TenantMismatch shows both sides (pattern to follow)
Self::TenantMismatch {
    layer,
    expected,
    actual,
} => {
    write!(
        f,
        "{layer} tenant mismatch: expected {expected:?}, got {actual:?}"
    )
}
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9133 | Enforce findings-to-OVID evidence chain in ResultCommitter scanned-request validation | relates-to: touches the same validation function |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `distinct_findings_count()` is called only when `done_ledger.status().is_scanned()` is true
- [ ] `ObservationOvidMismatch` Display output includes both expected and actual OVIDs
- [ ] `DoneLedgerWriteContextMismatch` Display output includes both expected and actual WriteContext values
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-scanner-runtime`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs:101-149` — full Display impl block
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` — WriteContext Display/Debug impl for formatting reference
close_reason: Low-value cleanup not needed for EP2 work; HashSet allocation is on an error path and Display fields are nice-to-have.
