title: Reuse findings Vec across items in scan_item_chunks HOT loop
description:
## Context

`scan_item_chunks` allocates a fresh `Vec<FsFindingRecord>` per item (`Vec::new()` at line ~1134). Other scratch buffers in the same loop (`scan_buf`, `scan_scratch`, `scan_pending`, `scan_metrics`) are allocated once before the item loop and reused via `&mut` references with `clear()` semantics. The findings Vec should follow the same pattern for allocation consistency on the HOT scan-miss execution path.

## Current State

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/ordered_content.rs:1134
let mut findings = Vec::new();
```

This is inside `scan_item_chunks`, called once per scan-miss item from `execute_scan_misses_with_engine`. Every item creates a fresh empty Vec that grows via `append_findings` on each chunk producing matches.

## Desired State

Thread a `&mut Vec<FsFindingRecord>` through `scan_item_chunks` the same way `pending` and `metrics` are threaded. Clear at the top, use as scratch, `std::mem::take` at break points to move populated contents into the outcome while leaving a zero-capacity shell for reuse.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/ordered_content.rs` | Add `findings_scratch` param to `scan_item_chunks`, `execute_item_via_range_read`, `execute_item_via_open` | Buffer reuse |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/ordered_content.rs` | Allocate `findings_scratch` once in `execute_scan_misses_with_engine` before the item loop (~line 955) | Single allocation |

### Patterns to Follow
```rust
// Existing pattern at ordered_content.rs:948-952 — scan_pending is allocated once, reused
let mut scan_pending = Vec::with_capacity(
    <scanner_engine::Engine as ScanEngine>::max_findings_per_chunk(&engine),
);
```

### Blast Radius
`scan_item_chunks`, `execute_item_via_range_read`, `execute_item_via_open` all gain one parameter. These are all `fn` (private) within ordered_content.rs. No external callers.

## Performance Considerations
HOT tier (per-item in scan-miss loop). After the first item that produces findings, subsequent items reuse the backing allocation (capacity retained across `take` + `clear` cycles). Most items with few findings save one heap allocation per item.

## Code References
- `ordered_content.rs:946-952` — existing scratch buffer allocation pattern
- `ordered_content.rs:1130-1134` — current per-item findings allocation
- `ordered_content.rs:1215` — `append_findings` growth point

None found.

title: Eliminate item_ref clone in range-read HOT path
description:
## Context

`execute_item_via_range_read` clones `item.item_ref()` to give the `move` closure ownership while `item` is separately moved into `scan_item_chunks`. `ItemRef` is backed by `ToxicBytesStorage` which in the `Owned` variant performs a full `Box<[u8]>` clone — a heap allocation plus memcpy up to 16 KiB per item. The `execute_item_via_open` path avoids this by opening the reader before passing `item`.

## Current State

```rust

```

This clone exists solely to satisfy the `move` closure that captures `item_ref` for the `read_range` call, while `item` is moved into `scan_item_chunks`.

## Desired State

Eliminate the clone by restructuring so `item_ref` can be borrowed or moved without cloning. Options:
- A) Have `scan_item_chunks` take `&ScanItem` instead of `ScanItem` by value, allowing `item_ref` to be borrowed into the closure
- B) Split `ScanItem` into parts before the call: move `item_ref` into closure, pass remaining fields to `scan_item_chunks`

### Blast Radius

## Performance Considerations
HOT tier (per-item when range-read is enabled). One heap allocation eliminated per scan-miss item on the range-read path. For pages with hundreds of items this reduces allocation pressure measurably.

title: Handle deferred items and multi-page pagination in ordered filesystem shard execution
description:
## Context

PR #311 review identified two interrelated data-loss scenarios in the bounded ordered-content executor:

1. **Single-page execution**: `scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine` processes exactly one connector page per shard assignment. If the page returns `PageState::HasMore`, remaining pages are never fetched because `run_worker` calls `complete_shard` (terminal) unconditionally.

2. **Deferred items permanently lost**: The skip-ahead feature in `execute_scan_misses_with_engine` defers oversized items from the interior of the page. The caller (`scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine`, line 1467) iterates only `execution.outcomes()` and never consumes `execution.deferred()`. Since deferred items can have keys smaller than subsequently committed items, the checkpoint cursor advances past them. On shard completion, they are permanently skipped.

## Current State

- `scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine` (distributed.rs:1419-1480) calls `execute_source` once, processes one page, returns `checkpoint_hint: None`.
- `run_filesystem_lease` (distributed.rs:1511-1646) computes checkpoint from `PrefixCheckpointAggregator`, always returns to `run_worker`.
- `run_worker` (distributed.rs:1675-1750) unconditionally calls `complete_shard` (terminal Done transition).
- `execution.deferred()` is never read in any production code path.
- `execution.page_state()` is never inspected in the distributed execution path.

Reproduce scenario for deferred item loss:
- Budget: 15 bytes
- Page: `a.txt` (3B) → `b.txt` (20B, oversized) → `c.txt` (5B)
- After scanning `a.txt` (remaining=12), `b.txt` is deferred (20 > 12), `c.txt` is scanned (remaining=7).
- Checkpoint cursor → `c.txt`. On re-claim, start from after `c.txt`. `b.txt` is permanently skipped.

## Desired State

1. When `page_state == HasMore` or `deferred.is_non_empty()`, use non-terminal `checkpoint` instead of terminal `complete`, allowing the shard to be re-processed.
2. When deferred items exist, constrain the checkpoint cursor to not advance past the minimum deferred item key.
3. Add a pagination loop (either in `run_filesystem_lease` or `run_worker`) that re-processes the shard until the page is complete and no items are deferred.

## Implementation Guidance

The coordination protocol already supports `checkpoint` (non-terminal) vs `complete` (terminal). See `CoordinationBackend` trait in `crates/gossip-coordination/src/traits.rs`.

This work overlaps with and should be coordinated with:
- gossip-9273.17 (receipt-only checkpointing)
- gossip-9273.18 (explicit completion outcomes)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Deferred items are never silently lost — checkpoint does not advance past them
- [ ] Multi-page shards process all pages before terminal completion
- [ ] `execution.deferred()` and `execution.page_state()` are consumed in the distributed execution path
- [ ] Tests cover the deferred-item-with-interior-gap scenario
- [ ] `cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

title: Reduce per-page ShardSpec clone overhead in ordered filesystem page loop
description:
## Context

Review finding from feature/request-to-worker-path ce-review. The ordered filesystem
page loop clones ShardSpec (three Box<[u8]> fields: key_range_start, key_range_end,
metadata) on every page iteration because OrderedContentRuntimeInput::new takes ownership.
The spec is invariant across pages — only the resume cursor changes.

## Current State

File: crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs, inside
scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine, around line 1960.

Each page iteration calls shard_spec.clone() to construct a new RestoredShardState.
For shards with many pages (large directories with budget-bounded page sizes), this
produces N heap allocations where N is the page count.

## Desired State

OrderedContentRuntimeInput should borrow or Arc-wrap the ShardSpec so the invariant
spec is shared across pages. Only the cursor (which changes per page) should be cloned.

## Implementation Guidance

- Modify OrderedContentRuntimeInput::new in gossip-scanner-runtime/src/ordered_content.rs
  to accept &ShardSpec or Arc<ShardSpec> instead of owned ShardSpec
- Update RestoredShardState construction in the page loop accordingly
- This is a cross-crate API change affecting ordered_content module internals

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ShardSpec is no longer cloned per page iteration
- [ ] All existing tests pass: cargo test -p gossip-scanner-runtime
- [ ] cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

## Current State

File: crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs, around line 2070.

first deadline check. The narrow window between pipeline start and the third check is

A test that expires the deadline specifically in the window between CommitPipeline::start()
and pipeline.split(), exercising the pipeline.shutdown() cleanup path.

description:
## Context

Epic 3 introduces distributed Git repository scanning to gossip-rs. Before implementation spreads across multiple crates, the execution model must be locked in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR). Without this, implementation will oscillate between "Git as another ordered-content connector" and "Git as a repo-family runtime," wasting effort and introducing architectural drift.

The existing codebase already has most of the infrastructure needed for Git MVP execution:
- Shard coordination with `ShardStatus` state machine (`Active -> Done | Split | Parked`)
- Receipt-driven checkpoint advancement (`CompletedUnit -> UnitCommitReceipt -> CheckpointAggregatorInput`)
- Git family contracts (`RepoKey`, `GitSelection`, `GitRepoTarget`, `GitRunError`, three traits)
- Inner scanner-git persistence (`PersistenceStore::commit_finalize`)
- Lease-loss handling (`LeaseUncertainty` enum with `DeadlineElapsed`, `AdvanceStaleFence`, `AdvanceLeaseExpired`)

The ADR needs to formalize how these existing patterns compose for the Git repo-native family, not invent new mechanisms.

## Current State

### No ADR directory or format exists yet
The repository uses boundary-spec documents in `docs/` (e.g., `docs/gossip-coordination/boundary-2-coordination.md`) but has no ADR directory or established ADR format. This will be the first ADR.

### Existing outer state machine (coordination-level)
```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/record.rs:97-113
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum ShardStatus {
    Active = 0,   // may be acquired by a worker
    Done = 1,     // completed successfully
    Split = 2,    // replaced by children via SplitReplace
    Parked = 3,   // halted due to repeated or permanent error
}
```
All transitions originate from `Active`. Terminal states are irreversible. The repo execution state machine must be a **substate within `Active`** — the `ShardStatus` enum itself must not change.

### Existing error taxonomy (binary)
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:49-60
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ErrorClass {
    Retryable,
    Permanent,
}
```
Binary today. The `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute means adding a variant is additive/non-breaking.

**Important**: Three separate `ErrorClass` enums exist at different abstraction layers:
1. **Connector-level** — `gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:49-60` (binary, `#[non_exhaustive]`)
2. **Scheduler-level** — `scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/failure.rs:100-106` (binary with `RetryableReason`/`PermanentReason` subtypes)
3. **Remote-level** — `scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/remote.rs:68-75` (binary, simple)

The ADR addresses the connector-level enum only. Scheduler-level and remote-level mapping is deferred to the implementation ticket.

### Existing receipt chain (repo-frontier variant ready)
```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs:74-80
pub fn repo_frontier(sequence_no: u64, checkpoint_cursor: Cursor) -> Self {
    Self::new(
        sequence_no,
        CheckpointBoundary::repo_frontier(checkpoint_cursor),
    )
}
```
`CompletedUnit::repo_frontier()` already exists and is tested. The `CheckpointBoundaryKind::RepoFrontier` variant is defined. No end-to-end production callers exercise this path yet — the infrastructure is ready but the Git execution pipeline is not wired.

### Existing lease-loss handling (runtime-level only)
```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:479-506
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum LeaseUncertainty {
    DeadlineElapsed { deadline: LogicalTime, observed: LogicalTime },
    AdvanceStaleFence { presented: FenceEpoch, current: FenceEpoch },
    AdvanceLeaseExpired { deadline: LogicalTime, now: LogicalTime },
}
```
Three variants covering local deadline and coordinator-side rejection. Currently only exists at the runtime level, not the connector level.

### Existing inner persistence contract
```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/persist.rs:21-27
pub trait PersistenceStore {
    fn commit_finalize(&self, output: &FinalizeOutput) -> Result<(), PersistError>;
}
```
Inner scanner-git atomic finalize. The ADR must document how this maps to the outer `UnitCommitReceipt` chain.

### Existing Git connector error type
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:613-616
crate::define_connector_error! {
    /// Repo-native execution or mirroring failure.
    GitRunError
}
```
Generated via `define_connector_error!` macro. Gets `retryable()`, `permanent()`, `rate_limited()` constructors. Would gain a `stale_owner()` constructor when `ErrorClass` is extended.

### Existing `is_retryable()` binary branching
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:62-68
impl ErrorClass {
    pub const fn is_retryable(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Retryable)
    }
}
```
The `define_connector_error!` macro generates per-type `is_retryable()` that delegates to this. Adding a third variant (`StaleOwner`) means it falls through to `false` — matching `Permanent` behavior. Call sites using binary `if is_retryable() { ... } else { /* treat as permanent */ }` must be audited when `StaleOwner` is implemented.

## Desired State

A new ADR document at `docs/adr/0001-git-mvp-execution-model.md` that locks four architectural decisions with explicit state machines, error taxonomy, and scope constraints. The ADR must be self-contained — a developer reading it should understand the full execution model without consulting external documents.

### Decision 1: Repo execution is a substate of ShardStatus::Active

Document the repo execution lifecycle as phases within the `Active` shard state, including both the happy path and abort/interruption edges:

```text
[Coordinator view]        [Worker-internal view]
                          ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
ShardStatus::Active  ──>  │ Claimed                                  │
                          │   ├── MirrorSync ────┐                   │
                          │   ├── Executing ─────┤ (lease loss from  │
                          │   ├── InnerDurable ──┤  any inner state  │
                          │   └── OuterCheckpointed  => worker stops, │
                          │                        shard stays Active │
                          │                        for reassignment)  │
                          └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
ShardStatus::Done    ──>  (terminal: shard complete, after OuterCheckpointed)
ShardStatus::Parked  ──>  (terminal: permanent error from any inner substate)
```

**Abort/interruption edges** (must appear in ADR):
- **Lease loss** from any inner substate: worker stops immediately, shard remains `Active` for coordinator reassignment. In-flight work is discarded; idempotent replay handles the overlap on re-acquire.
- **Retryable error** from `MirrorSync` or `Executing`: retry within `Active` (worker-internal retry loop, bounded by the lease deadline).
- **Permanent error** from any inner substate: worker requests `ShardStatus::Parked` via coordination.

The coordinator only sees coarse milestones (claimed, durable receipt, done). Worker-internal states like `Executing` and `InnerDurable` are local bookkeeping invisible to coordination.

### Decision 2: Receipt-driven sequential handoff (durable-receipt seam)

Document the two-layer durability chain:

```text
scanner-git PersistenceStore::commit_finalize(FinalizeOutput)
    ↓ (inner persistence durable)
RepoExecutionReceipt (proof of inner durability)
    ↓
CompletedUnit::repo_frontier(seq, cursor)
    ↓
[shared commit pipeline: translate → commit findings → commit done-ledger]
    ↓
UnitCommitReceipt (outer durability proof)
    ↓
CheckpointAggregatorInput (kind-validated)
    ↓
PrefixCheckpointAggregator → checkpoint advancement
```

Key invariant: **Outer repo frontier MUST NOT advance before inner durable persistence completes.**

**Crash window safety**: The window between `InnerDurable` and `OuterCheckpointed` is inherent to any non-2PC system and is safe by construction. If a crash occurs after inner persistence completes but before outer checkpoint advances:
- Inner writes are durable (watermarks + data ops committed atomically by `PersistenceStore`).
- On re-acquire by a new worker, idempotent seen-blob dedup prevents double-processing.
- Watermark suppression on partial `FinalizeOutcome` prevents ref tips from advancing past unscanned content.
- The outer checkpoint replays from the last known position; dedup handles the overlap.

This matches FDB's `commit_result_unknown` precedent: treat the outcome as unknown and rely on idempotent replay.

### Decision 3: Three-class error taxonomy

Document the extension of the connector-level `ErrorClass` (at `gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs`) from binary to ternary:

| Class | Meaning | Worker Action | Example |
|-------|---------|---------------|---------|
| `Retryable` | Transient failure, same request may succeed | Retry with backoff | Network timeout, HTTP 503, `git gc` contention |
| `Permanent` | Will not succeed without external change | Park shard | Auth denied, repo not found, invalid refs |
| `StaleOwner` | Ownership revoked or uncertain | Stop immediately, release resources | Fence epoch mismatch, lease expired, deadline elapsed |

`StaleOwner` is a **control-flow event**, not an error (per Gray & Cheriton 1989). The worker stops, discards in-flight work, and the coordinator reassigns. At the connector level this maps to `ErrorClass::StaleOwner`; at the runtime level it maps to `LeaseUncertainty`.

**Migration constraint**: `ErrorClass::is_retryable()` currently returns `matches!(self, Self::Retryable)`, meaning a new `StaleOwner` variant falls through to `false` (same as `Permanent`). The ADR must specify:
- `is_retryable()` semantics are unchanged — `StaleOwner` is not retryable (correct behavior).
- All call sites using binary `if is_retryable() { ... } else { /* treat as permanent */ }` must be audited to add a third arm for `StaleOwner` (it requires immediate stop, not parking).
- The `define_connector_error!` macro must gain a `stale_owner()` constructor (no `retry_after_ms` — pointless for a revoked lease).
- An `is_stale_owner()` convenience method should be added to `ErrorClass`.

**Parallel taxonomy note**: The scheduler-level `ErrorClass` at `scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/failure.rs:100-106` uses `Retryable(RetryableReason)` / `Permanent(PermanentReason)` subtypes. The remote-level `ErrorClass` at `scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/remote.rs:68-75` is a simple binary. The ADR addresses the connector-level enum only. Mapping `StaleOwner` into the scheduler-level and remote-level taxonomies is deferred to the implementation ticket.

**Cross-reference**: The existing error taxonomy documentation at `docs/gossip-coordination/coordination-error-model.md` describes the coordination-layer error hierarchy. The ADR's Decision 3 extends the connector-layer taxonomy and should reference that document as complementary.

### Decision 4: MVP scope locks

| Lock | Decision | Rationale |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Scheduling unit | One normalized repo target = one shard | Simplest geometry; avoids multi-target packing complexity |
| Discovery | Local/static paths only, no hosted provider discovery | MVP scope boundary |
| Selection | One `GitSelection` per shard, not in `RepoKey` | Keeps ordering stable; selection is shard payload, not identity |
| Duplicates | Same-repo/different-selection submissions rejected for MVP | Avoids identity ambiguity |
| Inner progress | scanner-git watermark/seen/persistence state only | Keeps coordination state at O(shards), not O(objects) |
| Shard splitting | `ShardStatus::Split` is unreachable for repo shards in MVP (one repo = one atomic work unit, no sub-repo fan-out) | Simplest geometry; repos are not subdivisible mid-scan |
| `StaleOwner` code changes | ADR documents the decision only; `ErrorClass::StaleOwner` variant, macro update, and call-site audit are deferred to a separate implementation ticket | Keeps this ADR as documentation-only |

### Invariants (must appear in every downstream Epic 3 ticket)

The following 8 invariants from the Epic 3 plan must be listed in the ADR and referenced by every downstream implementation task:

1. A stale fence token must never be accepted again.
2. Loss of lease must stop repo execution quickly.
3. Outer repo frontier must never advance before inner durable persistence completes.
4. Control-plane state must scale with shards, not objects inside repos.
5. Same request inputs must normalize to the same ordered repo targets.
6. Same explicit commit input must lower to the same synthetic ref.
7. No raw secret bytes, repo paths, refs, or tokens in logs/metrics/traces.
8. Duplicate submission and worker replay must be idempotent.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docs/adr/0001-git-mvp-execution-model.md` | The ADR document (target ~250-300 lines; decision-focused, not tutorial-length) |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `docs/scope-map.toml` | Add `[[scopes]]` entry for `docs/adr/` | Enable design-doc-scope-check hook for ADR directory |
| `docs/README.md` | Add ADR section to documentation index | Discoverability |

### Out of Scope

This task documents architectural decisions only. No code changes are made. Specifically:
- The `ErrorClass::StaleOwner` variant, `define_connector_error!` macro update, `stale_owner()` constructor, `is_stale_owner()` method, and call-site audit are **separate implementation tasks**.
- The `RepoExecutionReceipt` type design is **deferred to the persistence adapter ticket** (Epic 3, Ticket 10).
- Partial inner progress semantics on lease expiry (whether watermarks from incomplete runs are preserved or discarded) are **deferred to the scanner-git adapter ticket** (Epic 3, Ticket 9).

### ADR Format to Follow
Use MADR (Markdown Architectural Decision Record) format adapted to the codebase style:
- **Title**: Short imperative statement
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Why this decision is needed now
- **Decision**: The chosen approach for each of the four decisions
- **Alternatives Considered**: For each decision, the rejected alternative with tradeoff
- **Consequences**: What downstream implementation tasks this enables
- **Scope Locks**: Explicit MVP boundaries
- **Invariants**: The 8 invariants listed above

### Patterns to Follow
Reference the existing `PageCommit<S>` typestate documentation in `diagrams/08-pagecommit-typestate.md` as the model for documenting state machine transitions and durability ordering. The actual typestate struct definitions are at `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:425-456` (`AwaitingFindings`, `FindingsDurable`, `ItemDurable`, `CheckpointDurable`).

Reference the existing coordination error model at `docs/gossip-coordination/coordination-error-model.md` as complementary documentation for error taxonomy.

Reference the existing 4-stage filesystem orchestration pipeline in `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/` (request normalization, geometry planning, payload encoding, run setup) as the architectural template the Git control-plane will follow.

### Blast Radius
- `ErrorClass` has ~150 references across the codebase. The ADR decision to add `StaleOwner` will (in a future ticket) affect the `define_connector_error!` macro, all three generated error types (`EnumerateError`, `ReadError`, `GitRunError`), and their test coverage.
- The durable-receipt seam decision will guide implementation of Tickets 9-11 (scanner-git adapter, persistence adapters, runtime loop).
- The scope locks will constrain Tickets 2-8 (RepoKey, request models, shard payload, planner, mirror, discovery).

### ParkReason (coordination-level error parking)


## Design Notes

### State Machine Composition: Substate vs Parallel
**Chosen**: Repo execution as substate of `Active` (Harel statechart model).
**Alternative**: Parallel state machine tracked independently.
**Tradeoff**: Parallel machine risks inner/outer desync (Kafka Streams failure mode). Substate gets inherited transitions: any inner state can transition to Parked/Split via outer coordination, ensuring lease loss always stops execution regardless of inner phase.

### Durable-Receipt Seam: Sequential Handoff vs 2PC
**Chosen**: Receipt-driven sequential handoff (outbox pattern).
**Alternative**: Two-phase commit between inner scanner-git and outer coordination.
**Tradeoff**: 2PC is more uniform but much larger refactor, higher risk of violating inner watermark semantics, and unnecessary given the existing idempotent replay guarantees (DoneLedger dedup + watermark suppression).

### Error Taxonomy: Ternary vs Binary + Runtime Signal
**Chosen**: Add `StaleOwner` to connector-level `ErrorClass`.
**Alternative**: Keep `ErrorClass` binary and handle lease-loss only at runtime level via `LeaseUncertainty`.
**Tradeoff**: Binary keeps the connector layer simpler, but means connectors cannot signal lease-loss; the runtime must detect it. With Git execution, the inner scanner-git may detect stale ownership (e.g., during persistence writes), so the connector-level signal is needed for completeness.

### Scope: One Repo per Shard vs Multi-Repo Packing
**Chosen**: One normalized repo target = one shard for MVP.
**Alternative**: Pack multiple repos per shard.
**Tradeoff**: Multi-repo packing has fewer etcd records but adds split-point, replay, and checkpoint complexity for no immediate value.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| ADR locks wrong durable-receipt seam, causing rework | Low | High | Receipt chain is already proven for ordered-content; repo-frontier uses same chain |
| `ErrorClass::StaleOwner` addition breaks existing match arms | Very Low | Medium | The implementation ticket must update the exhaustive `match` expressions in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs` and `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api_tests.rs`; `#[non_exhaustive]` only protects external consumers. |
| Inner/outer state desync during crash between InnerDurable and OuterCheckpointed | Medium | Medium | Safe by construction: idempotent replay via DoneLedger dedup + watermark suppression |
| MVP scope locks prevent future multi-repo packing | Low | Low | Explicit scope lock means the constraint is documented and can be lifted deliberately |
| `is_retryable()` binary branching misclassifies `StaleOwner` at call sites | Medium | High | ADR specifies migration constraint; implementation ticket must audit all `is_retryable()` call sites |

description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 4 is the seam where normalized Git request state becomes shard-local metadata. Ticket 3 (`gossip-9426`) defines typed Git request models and normalization, but there is still no typed payload contract for the bytes stored in repo-frontier shard metadata. Without that contract, later planner/setup work would either reopen raw submission input or invent ad hoc metadata packing during registration.

This task should define the Git payload contract only: what one repo-frontier shard stores in `connector_extra`, how those bytes are encoded and decoded deterministically, and how later stages recover the target-local Git state from the shard alone. The scope boundary is important:

- one normalized repo target = one payload
- payload/metadata contract only
- no planner fan-out
- no `create_run(...)` / `register_shards(...)`
- no synthetic-ref lowering for explicit commits
- no mirror-management or execution wiring

## Current State

The filesystem control-plane already has the payload stage we want to mirror for Git, but the Git side stops at normalized request types and runtime config shapes.

- `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/payload.rs` is filesystem-only today. It defines `FilesystemShardPayload`, deterministic encode/decode, and redacted `Debug`.
- `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/planner.rs` already treats payload construction as a distinct stage after request normalization and geometry planning.
- `crates/gossip-frontier/src/hint.rs` provides the generic shard-metadata envelope. `connector_extra` is explicitly connector-private and already has framing helpers.
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs` makes the source-of-truth split explicit: key-range bounds live in the shard spec, while opaque connector metadata is separate and capped at `MAX_METADATA_SIZE = 16_384`.
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` already has the Git-family nouns the payload should reuse: `RepoLocator`, `GitSelection`, and `GitRepoTarget`.
- `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` shows the runtime Git input shape. `scan_git_with_runtime(...)` expects a fully hydrated `GitScanConfig` up front.
- There is no `GitShardPayload` type or Git-specific payload module at `HEAD`, and no Git metadata decode helper analogous to the filesystem payload path.

```rust
// crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/payload.rs:40-66 — existing filesystem payload contract
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FilesystemShardPayload {
    mode: FilesystemSourceMode,
    canonical_root: PathBuf,
}

impl fmt::Debug for FilesystemShardPayload {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("FilesystemShardPayload")
            .field("mode", &self.mode)
            .field("canonical_root", &"<redacted>")
            .finish()
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/planner.rs:95-102 — payload construction is already a distinct stage
#[must_use]
pub fn shard_payload(&self) -> FilesystemShardPayload {
    FilesystemShardPayload::from_normalized_request(&self.request)
}
```


- stable `repo_id`
- canonical repo identity (`RepoKey`)
- canonical locator (`RepoLocator`) or the exact target-local path encoding chosen by the request-normalization seam
- optional diagnostic display metadata if later stages need it
- Git selection state for this target
- any additional Git-specific execution knobs that are truly shard-local

The task must also make an explicit source-of-truth split:

- shard-spec bounds remain the authority for repo-frontier range geometry
- payload bytes remain the authority for repo identity, locator, selection, and other target-local Git settings
- generic run-level settings that already live elsewhere should not be duplicated into the payload unless decode cannot remain self-contained without them

- `GitShardPayload` lands in `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/git_payload.rs`, matching the module layout Ticket 5 already plans to consume.

### Files to Modify

- Mirror the structure and testing style of `FilesystemShardPayload` in `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/payload.rs`.
- Keep payload encode/decode in one module. Other crates should call named helpers instead of hand-parsing bytes.
- Reuse the existing `ShardMetadata` envelope and `connector_extra` transport instead of creating a second metadata channel.
- Reuse the Git contract types already in `gossip-contracts`; do not create payload-local copies of repo identity or selection types.
- Keep the payload deterministic and byte-stable. Field ordering for variable-length collections must be canonical.
- If the payload needs to represent explicit-commit selection prior to Ticket 6, preserve that typed request-side state rather than inventing provisional synthetic-ref naming here.

- Ticket 5 will encode this payload into shard registration paths. If the payload contract is vague now, setup code will hard-code metadata packing details in a second place.

- `MAX_METADATA_SIZE` makes multi-target packing the wrong shape for MVP. This task should lock the single-target invariant so later setup code does not grow a manifest format accidentally.

## Design Notes

### Payload Scope

This task owns the bytes and the decode contract, not shard registration or execution. The filesystem Epic 2 payload task also wired runtime hydration because that runtime seam already existed. For Git, the distributed runtime seam is not ready yet, so this task should stop at:

- the typed payload
- the metadata-envelope packing helper
- the decode helper(s) that reconstruct target-local Git state from payload bytes
- tests that prove later runtime hydration will not need external lookup

### Target-Local vs Run-Level Settings

The task should explicitly document which settings belong inside the payload and which remain run-level. As a default:

- repo identity, locator, selection, and stable `repo_id` are payload-local
- global rule paths, budgets, and worker-local runtime toggles should stay outside the payload unless there is a concrete reason they must be per-shard

If you choose a different split, make the choice explicit in the task implementation docs and tests.

### Redaction

Payload `Debug` must follow the same privacy posture as `RepoLocator` and `GitSelection`: no raw repo paths, display names, refs, or commit bytes in logs. Use digests or `<redacted>` placeholders where appropriate.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Payload duplicates too much run-level config | Medium | Medium | Require an explicit target-local vs run-level split in the module docs and tests. |
| Payload omits fields later tickets need | Medium | High | Reconstruct target-local Git state directly from payload bytes and validate against the `GitScanConfig` target shape. |

| Payload decode fails late during execution instead of at boundary | Medium | High | Add malformed/truncated/unknown-tag tests and fail before any execution helper is called. |
| Payload grows into multi-target manifest | Low | Medium | Keep one normalized repo target per payload and enforce it in constructors/tests. |
| Metadata framing exceeds `MAX_METADATA_SIZE` | Medium | Medium | Preflight encoded length and reject oversize payloads during encode. |

## Performance Considerations

- Payload hydration should remain `O(1)` per shard.
- Use a fixed, deterministic wire format with simple decode steps instead of `serde` or schema negotiation.
- Avoid control-plane lookups after shard acquisition; the shard metadata itself should be sufficient for target-local Git state reconstruction.
- Keep encoded payload size bounded and comfortably within `MAX_METADATA_SIZE`.

## Testing Strategy

- Add round-trip tests proving the same `GitShardPayload` always encodes to the same bytes and decodes back identically.
- Add envelope tests proving Git payload bytes survive `ShardMetadata` packing and recovery through `decode_connector_extra(...)`.
- Add malformed-payload regressions for empty/truncated input, unknown discriminants, required-field omissions, and oversize metadata.

Implement explicit commit lowering via stable synthetic refs
description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 6 bridges request-side explicit commit intent into the ref-based execution model that `scanner-git` already understands. Ticket 3 (`gossip-9426`) keeps single-repo explicit commit input normalized on the request side, and Ticket 5 (`gossip-9429`) preserves that intent through shard registration. This task owns the deterministic lowering step that turns one explicit commit into one stable synthetic ref name so later runtime code can execute through the existing explicit-ref path.

This task should implement that lowering seam only. It owns synthetic-ref naming, mirror-local ref materialization, validation that the requested commit exists in the prepared mirror, and mapping from the request-side explicit-commit selection into a ref-based runtime selection. It does not own the broader mirror lifecycle from Ticket 7, the `scanner-git` adapter from Ticket 9, or the distributed worker loop from Ticket 11.

## Current State

`GitRefSelection` is ref-based today and has no explicit-commit variant.

`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:178-207`

`StartSetConfig::ExplicitRefs` already has stable identity semantics because canonical encoding sorts and dedupes refs before hashing `StartSetId`.

`crates/scanner-git/src/start_set.rs:108-156`

`RefWatermarkStore` keys persistence by `(repo_id, policy_hash, start_set_id, ref_name)`, so the synthetic ref name directly affects replay and watermark stability.

`crates/scanner-git/src/repo_open.rs:247-271`

`NativeRefResolver` already treats explicit refs strictly: missing refs are fatal, and the configured ref name is preserved in the resolved start set.

`crates/scanner-git/src/native_ref_resolver.rs:179-218`

`GitMirrorManager` only syncs a local mirror; `LocalMirror` is just a path plus sync metadata.

`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:427-475`

`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:668-672`

The runtime seam still initializes Git scans with `StartSetConfig::DefaultBranchOnly`.

`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:198-208`

`scanner-git` already exposes typed OID parsing helpers, so the lowering seam should reuse typed commit identity instead of re-parsing raw strings.

`crates/scanner-git/src/commit_parse.rs:324-331`

## Desired State

Introduce an explicit-commit lowering helper that takes one normalized Git target carrying typed explicit-commit intent and returns a ref-based execution selection backed by a deterministic synthetic ref that exists only inside the managed local mirror.

At minimum:
- define one private mirror namespace for explicit-commit lowering, for example `refs/gossip/scan-targets/commits/<object-format>/<hex-oid>` or an equivalent stable, non-user-facing prefix;
- derive the synthetic ref name deterministically from the object format plus commit identity so the same explicit commit always maps to the same ref name;
- validate that the requested commit exists in the prepared mirror object database before treating the selection as runnable;
- materialize or update the synthetic ref inside the mirror without mutating the source repository;
- map the request-side explicit-commit selection into the existing ref-based runtime shape: `GitRefSelection::ExplicitRefs { refs: [synthetic_ref] }` and the matching `StartSetConfig::ExplicitRefs`;
- preserve the rest of the selection tuple, including `scan_mode` and `merge_strategy`, while rewriting only the ref selection;
- keep reruns idempotent: rewriting the same synthetic ref to the same target commit must be safe and produce the same effective execution identity.

## Design Notes

### Lower To Refs, Not To A New Execution Mode

Reuse the ref-based start-set model that already drives watermark identity and explicit-ref resolution. Do not add a commit-only execution path in runtime or `scanner-git`.

### Synthetic Ref Names Are Part Of Persistence Identity

The synthetic ref name is persistence-affecting behavior. Keep the namespace stable and non-user-facing, but do not introduce a version suffix in the ref layout.

### Mirror Isolation Must Stay Absolute

This task may mutate refs only inside the prepared local mirror. The source repo remains read-only input.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Synthetic ref names are derived from unstable inputs such as temp paths or display names | Medium | High | Define the name only from a stable namespace plus canonical typed OID bytes. |
| Lowering invents a commit-only execution path instead of reusing explicit refs | Medium | High | Require `GitRefSelection::ExplicitRefs` / `StartSetConfig::ExplicitRefs` as the only post-lowering shape. |
| Missing commits are treated as retryable mirror noise | Medium | High | Classify missing commit selection as fatal input/config error. |
| Ref writes leak into the source repository instead of the managed mirror | Low | High | Keep helper inputs mirror-local and add tests that the source repo never mutates. |
| Future mirror-layout changes accidentally change synthetic ref names | Medium | Medium | Keep the namespace independent from mirror storage path layout. |

## Performance Considerations

- Synthetic-ref lowering sits on the repo-startup path, so it should be one commit-existence check plus one ref-store update in the mirror, not a broad fetch or secondary repository scan.
- Reusing the same stable synthetic ref on rerun is the main performance win here: it preserves watermark identity and avoids extra start-set churn.
- Keep the helper idempotent. Rewriting the same ref to the same OID should be cheap and should not force unnecessary mirror-side cleanup work.

## Testing Strategy

- Add naming tests proving the same typed explicit commit always yields the same synthetic ref name and different commits yield different names.
- Add object-format coverage if both SHA-1 and SHA-256 repos are supported in the relevant seam; synthetic ref names should remain deterministic for each format.
- Add mirror-local ref-write tests proving the synthetic ref is created or updated only in the managed mirror and never in the source repo.
- Add missing-commit tests proving unknown commits fail as fatal input/config errors before runtime execution proceeds.
- Add idempotency tests proving rerunning the lowering helper with the same mirror and commit leaves the same effective ref target and selection bytes.
- Add resolver/start-set tests proving the lowered output runs through `ExplicitRefs` semantics and preserves stable `StartSetId` / watermark naming.

## Recommended Skills

When implementing this task, explicitly leverage the following project skills so testing and documentation stay strong and maintainable:

- `/test-strategy` (`/Users/ahrav/Projects/Gossip-rs/.codex/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`) to choose the right mix of unit, `rstest`, property, fuzz, Kani, or simulation coverage for the code touched by this task.
- `/invariant-test-review` (`/Users/ahrav/Projects/Gossip-rs/.codex/skills/invariant-test-review/SKILL.md`) to verify that new regression, state-machine, or simulation tests actually isolate the claimed invariant and include the smallest discriminating boundary or negative-path twins where needed.
- `/test-consolidate` (`/Users/ahrav/Projects/Gossip-rs/.codex/skills/test-consolidate/SKILL.md`) after drafting coverage to collapse repetitive case-by-case tests into `rstest`, proptest, or fuzz targets when behaviors scale better than individual examples.
- `/doc-rigor` (`/Users/ahrav/.codex/skills/doc-rigor/SKILL.md`) after Rust code or comments change so module docs, item docs, and inline reasoning stay accurate and are verified against code reality.

## Related Work

|---------|-------|-------------|
| `gossip-9429` | Implement the Git control-plane planner and run setup path | Blocked-by |
| `gossip-9426` | Add typed Git submission request models and normalization | Relates-to |

title: Implement deterministic local mirror management
design:
# Task Forge Enrichment — gossip-9431

**Quality**: STRONG | **Conflicts resolved**: 5 | **Agents**: Testing, Implementation, Documentation, Interface Design, Security

## Conflicts Resolved

| # | Conflict | Resolution | Precedence |
|---|----------|------------|------------|
| 1 | `finalize_32` vs `finalize_64` for mirror path digest | Use `finalize_32`. Mirror paths are long-lived filesystem artifacts where collision is data loss. 256-bit provides ample margin. | Correctness/safety wins |
| 2 | tmp+rename vs sentinel file for atomic first-create | Use `.initializing` sentinel via `create_new(true)`. Directory rename is not atomic on all filesystems. Matches `spill_path.rs:48-60` pattern. Canonicalize+starts_with for symlink defense. | Correctness + codebase consistency |
| 3 | LocalPath clone-to-mirror vs validate-in-place | For `RepoLocator::LocalPath`, validate the existing path and return `LocalMirror` pointing at it (no clone). Cloning local-to-local wastes disk and time. Clone reserved for future URL variants. | Interface design agent wins on correctness |
| 4 | Cache key type | `[u8; 32]` digest key + test double for downstream are complementary, not conflicting. Both kept. | No conflict |
| 5 | Byte extraction for hashing | Match-exhaustive on `RepoLocator`, then `path.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes()` for `LocalPath` arm. All agents agree. | All compatible |

---

## Testing Strategy

**Test placement**: All tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` inside `git_mirror.rs`.

**Dependencies**: Add `proptest = "1.10"` to `gossip-scanner-runtime` `[dev-dependencies]`. `rstest` and `tempfile` already present.

### Required Tests (MUST)

1. **`test_mirror_path_determinism_from_locator`** — Unit. Same `RepoLocator` always produces the same cache path.
```rust
#[test]
fn mirror_path_determinism_from_locator() {
    let base = PathBuf::from("/tmp/mirrors");
    let locator = RepoLocator::local_path("/repos/acme/widgets.git");
    let mgr = LocalGitMirrorManager::new(base.clone());
    let path_a = mgr.derive_mirror_path(&locator);
    let path_b = mgr.derive_mirror_path(&locator);
    assert_eq!(path_a, path_b);
    assert!(path_a.starts_with(&base));
}
```

2. **`test_mirror_path_non_collision_distinct_locators`** — Proptest. Distinct locators produce distinct paths.
```rust
proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn distinct_locators_produce_distinct_mirror_paths(
        a in "[a-z]{1,20}/[a-z]{1,20}\\.git",
        b in "[a-z]{1,20}/[a-z]{1,20}\\.git",
    ) {
        prop_assume!(a != b);
        let base = PathBuf::from("/tmp/mirrors");
        let mgr = LocalGitMirrorManager::new(base);
        let pa = mgr.derive_mirror_path(&RepoLocator::local_path(&a));
        let pb = mgr.derive_mirror_path(&RepoLocator::local_path(&b));
        prop_assert_ne!(pa, pb);
    }
}
```

3. **`test_mirror_path_golden_value`** — Unit. Pins exact hex output to prevent silent digest drift.

4. **`test_first_create_atomicity_via_sentinel`** — Unit with `tempfile::TempDir`. After successful `sync_mirror`, no `.initializing` sentinel remains. Authoritative directory exists.

5. **`test_repeated_sync_reuses_authoritative_path`** — Unit. Same path returned on second call. `last_synced_at_ms` populated.

6. **`test_invalid_repo_produces_permanent_error`** — `rstest` with cases: nonexistent path, plain file. Assert `GitRunError` is permanent.
```rust
#[rstest]
#[case::nonexistent("/nonexistent/path/repo.git")]
#[case::plain_file("/dev/null")]
fn invalid_repo_produces_permanent_error(#[case] path: &str) {
    let base = tempdir().expect("tempdir");
    let locator = RepoLocator::local_path(path);
    let mut mgr = LocalGitMirrorManager::new(base.path().to_path_buf());
    let err = mgr.sync_mirror(&locator).expect_err("should fail");
    assert_eq!(err.class(), ErrorClass::Permanent);
}
```

7. **`test_mirror_path_domain_constant_in_registry`** — Covered by adding `GIT_MIRROR_PATH_V1` to `domain::ALL`. Existing `no_duplicate_values` test validates uniqueness automatically.

8. **`test_mirror_debug_output_redacts_base_path`** — Unit. `{:?}` output uses `ToxicDigest`, does NOT contain raw path.

### Recommended Tests (SHOULD)

9. **`test_concurrent_maintenance_produces_retryable_error`** — Create `.lock` file, assert retryable error.

10. **`test_interrupted_first_create_cleanup`** — Pre-create stale `.initializing` sentinel, assert cleanup on next sync.

### Do NOT Test (Already Covered)

| Behavior | Covered By | Location |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| `LocalMirror` debug redaction | `local_mirror_debug_redacts_path_and_preserves_freshness_metadata` | `git.rs:1011` |
| `GitRunError` constructors | `git_run_error_constructors_and_display_work` | `git.rs:1039` |
| `GitMirrorManager` Send + object-safety | `git_family_traits_require_send_and_are_object_safe` | `git.rs:1064` |
| `derive_repo_id` determinism | proptest suite | `repo_identity.rs:390` |
| BLAKE3 domain separation | proptest suite | `hashing.rs:224-287` |
| Lock file detection | integration suite | `git_preflight.rs:132` |

---

## Implementation Guidance Addendum

### Domain-Separated Hashing

1. Add `GIT_MIRROR_PATH_V1` constant to `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/domain.rs`:
   - Value: `"gossip/git/v1/mirror-path"` (distinct from `GIT_REPO_ID_V1`)
   - Add to `ALL` array (bump length from 17 to 18)

2. Add `MIRROR_PATH_HASHER` to `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/hashing.rs`:
   ```rust
   pub static MIRROR_PATH_HASHER: LazyLock<Hasher> =
       LazyLock::new(|| Hasher::new_derive_key(domain::GIT_MIRROR_PATH_V1));
   ```

3. Use `finalize_32` (not `finalize_64`) for collision resistance.

### Digest-Based Path Derivation

- Feed `RepoLocator` bytes via exhaustive `match`:
  ```rust
  match locator {
      RepoLocator::LocalPath(path) => path.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes(),
  }
  ```
- Hex-encode via `gossip_stdx::hex_encode` (at `gossip-stdx/src/lib.rs:149`).
- Layout: `mirror_root/local/<hex[..2]>/<full-64-hex>.git` — 2-char prefix avoids flat dirs with thousands of entries.

### LocalPath Optimization

For `RepoLocator::LocalPath`, do NOT `git clone --mirror`. Instead:
- Validate the path exists and is a Git repository.
- Return `LocalMirror` pointing directly at the validated path.
- Compute digest for cache keying but skip clone. Clone reserved for future URL variants.

### Cache Structure

- Key: `HashMap<[u8; 32], LocalMirror>` — `[u8; 32]` is Copy + Hash, no allocation on lookup.
- Trait has `&mut self`, so plain `HashMap` suffices — no Mutex/RefCell needed.

### Atomic First-Create (Future URL Variants)

- `.initializing` sentinel via `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true)` (matches `spill_path.rs:48-60`).
- Sentinel path: `<authoritative-path>.initializing`
- On success: remove sentinel. On failure: remove sentinel + partial directory.
- On startup: scan for stale sentinels and clean up.

### Lock Protocol

- Per-mirror `.lock` file with `create_new(true)` for atomic acquisition.
- No `flock`/`fs2` dependency — file-existence-based locking suffices for single-process model.
- Embed `std::process::id()` in lock content for stale-lock recovery (check PID liveness).

### Error Classification

- Reuse `GitRunError::retryable()`, `permanent()`, `concurrent_maintenance()` from `git.rs:749-761`.
- Bridge `io::Error` using same classification as `is_permanent_io_error` in `gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:210-220`. Replicate the match pattern locally (6 `ErrorKind` arms).
- `ENOSPC` → retryable (correct default).

### Redacted Debug

- `ToxicDigest::of_bytes` for all path fields, matching `LocalMirror::Debug` at `git.rs:602-611`.
- Never embed raw paths in `GitRunError` messages.

### Reusable Utilities

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `MIRROR_PATH_HASHER` (new) | `hashing.rs` | Cached hasher for mirror path derivation |
| `GIT_MIRROR_PATH_V1` (new) | `domain.rs` | Domain separation constant |
| `finalize_32` | `hashing.rs:149` | 256-bit digest finalization |
| `gossip_stdx::hex_encode` | `gossip-stdx/src/lib.rs:149` | Hex path components |
| `ToxicDigest::of_bytes` | `connector/types.rs:98` | Redacted debug output |
| `GitRunError::retryable/permanent/concurrent_maintenance` | `git.rs:749-761` | Error classification |
| `LocalMirror::new().with_last_synced_at_ms()` | `git.rs:572-585` | Return value builder |
| `create_new(true)` pattern | `spill_path.rs:48-60` | Atomic reservation |

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

| Anti-Pattern | Do Instead |
|---|---|
| `to_string_lossy().as_bytes()` for hashing | `as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes()` |
| New error enum alongside `GitRunError` | Map to existing constructors |
| `finalize_64` for mirror paths | `finalize_32` — 256-bit for filesystem collision resistance |
| Adding `fs2`/flock dependency | `.lock` file with `create_new(true)` |
| `Mutex<HashMap>` for cache | Plain `HashMap` — trait has `&mut self` |
| Reusing `GIT_REPO_ID_V1` domain | New `GIT_MIRROR_PATH_V1` domain constant |
| `git clone --mirror` for `LocalPath` | Validate + return `LocalMirror` at existing path |
| Raw paths in error messages | Redact via `ToxicDigest::of_bytes` |

---

## Documentation Requirements

### New File: `git_mirror.rs` Module Docs

Module-level documentation covering:
- Lifecycle overview: validate (LocalPath) or create/refresh (future URL variants)
- Digest-based path derivation and determinism guarantee
- Locking strategy and concurrency model
- Error classification bridge between `io::Error` and `GitRunError`
- Redaction policy (ADR invariant 7)
- Allocation tier: COLD

Pattern: `ordered_content.rs:1-67`.

### Struct Documentation

- Purpose and relationship to `GitMirrorManager` trait
- Invariants: digest cache consistency, sentinel cleanup
- Field semantics
- Thread safety: `&mut self` means single-owner

Pattern: `ordered_content.rs:100-117`.

### Function Documentation

- `sync_mirror` impl: algorithm overview, `# Errors` section, edge cases. Pattern: `git_repo.rs:81-96`.
- Digest path helper: algorithm, determinism, directory layout rationale. Pattern: `git_repo.rs:167-174`.

### Module Declaration

One-line comment above `pub mod git_mirror;` in `lib.rs`. Pattern: existing declarations at `lib.rs:103-104`.

### Trait Doc Enhancement

Expand `GitMirrorManager` trait doc at `git.rs:804-808`: postcondition, error contract, `last_synced_at_ms` requirement.

### Design Docs to Update

| Doc | Section | Change |
|-----|---------|--------|
| `docs/gossip-scanner-runtime.md:39` | Source File Map | Add `git_mirror.rs` |
| `docs/gossip-scanner-runtime.md:85` | Architecture | Mention mirror management stage |
| `docs/source-families.md:155` | Source file inventory | Add new file |
| `docs/adr/0001-git-mvp-execution-model.md:229` | Decision 4 / Mirror lifecycle | Reference concrete implementation |

---

## Security Hardening

### Critical

1. **Subprocess command injection** — When git subprocess calls are added for future URL variants, pass repo paths after `--` in all `Command::new("git")` invocations. Test that `--upload-pack=...` injection does not execute.

2. **Symlink defense** — After creating sentinel/lock files, `canonicalize()` parent and assert `starts_with(mirror_root)`. Pattern: `normalize_within` in `request.rs:163-185`.

### High

3. **Stale lock recovery** — Embed PID + timestamp in lock file. Check PID liveness on acquisition failure. Max lock age backstop (e.g., 30 min).

4. **Git env hygiene** — For future URL variants: `Command::env_remove()` for `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`. Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

5. **Subprocess timeout** — Future URL variants must enforce configurable timeout. Kill on timeout, classify as retryable.

### Medium

6. **Git stderr redaction** — Do not log subprocess stderr verbatim. Redact paths via `ToxicDigest`.

7. **TOCTOU lock atomicity** — `create_new(true)` makes create+check atomic. Tolerate mirror disappearance (retryable, not permanent).

8. **Orphaned sentinel cleanup** — On construction, scan mirror_root for stale `.initializing` sentinels.

9. **Disk exhaustion** — Mirror eviction is out of scope. File follow-up task.

---

## Performance Considerations

| File | Tier | Constraints |
|------|------|-------------|
| `git_mirror.rs` (NEW) | COLD | Scan-setup code. Allocations fine. Optimize for clarity. |
| `git_repo.rs` | COLD | Setup orchestration. No hot-path constraints. |
| `hashing.rs` | HOT (reuse only) | Add only `LazyLock<Hasher>` static. `clone()` is stack-only (~1.8 KB BLAKE3 state). |
| `domain.rs` | COLD | Compile-time constant addition only. |

Key: mirror management runs once per repo at scan setup, not per-shard/per-claim. All operations are I/O-bound. No micro-optimization justified.

title: Implement a minimal GitRepoDiscoverySource for static targets
description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 8 is the minimal discovery seam that lets repo-frontier workers consume the Git shards created by Ticket 5 (`gossip-9429`) without overbuilding hosted discovery or multi-target pagination. For MVP, every initial shard carries exactly one normalized repo target, but the runtime still needs a concrete `GitRepoDiscoverySource` that obeys the same paging/resume contracts as the rest of the frontier model: ordered by `RepoKey`, bounded to the shard, key-authoritative resume, and safe completion even when resume tokens are stale or absent.

This task should implement that minimal static discovery source only. It owns `discover_page()` behavior for one payload-backed target, optional trivial split-hint behavior, and page-validation tests. It does **not** own mirror sync, explicit-commit lowering, `scanner-git` execution, or distributed worker orchestration.

## Current State

The Git family contract already defines a repo discovery stage, but there is no concrete static discovery implementation in tree today.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:637-666 — discovery trait exists but has no static implementation
pub trait GitRepoDiscoverySource: Send {
    fn capabilities(&self) -> GitDiscoveryCapabilities;

    fn discover_page(
        &mut self,
        shard: &ShardSpec,
        cursor: &Cursor,
        budgets: Budgets,
    ) -> Result<Option<PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>>, EnumerateError>;

    fn choose_split_point(
        &mut self,
        _shard: &ShardSpec,
        _cursor: &Cursor,
        _budgets: Budgets,
    ) -> Result<Option<ItemKey>, EnumerateError> {
        Ok(None)
    }
}
```

The runtime crate likewise exposes only a placeholder discovery entrypoint. It still errors because connector-level repository enumeration is not wired in.

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:50-62 — Git repo discovery runtime path is still a placeholder
pub fn execute_discovery<D: GitRepoDiscoverySource>(
    _discovery: &mut D,
) -> Result<ScanReport, ScanRuntimeError> {
    Err(ScanRuntimeError::Driver(anyhow!(
        "git-repo discovery runtime path for source '{}' is not implemented yet",
        std::any::type_name::<D>()
    )))
}
```

The shared paging vocabulary already gives the exact validation boundary this task should use. `PageBuf::try_new_validated()` combines non-empty page construction with ordering, uniqueness, and shard-bound checks.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs:41-76 — validated page construction already exists
pub fn try_new_validated(
    items: Vec<T>,
    state: PageState,
    shard_start: &[u8],
    shard_end: &[u8],
) -> Result<Self, PageShapeError>
where
    T: KeyedPageItem,
{
    validate_filled_page(&items, shard_start, shard_end)?;
    Self::try_new(items, state)
}
```

The sequence-level invariants are also already spelled out. Page emission must advance strictly past the prior cursor boundary, and a `HasMore` cursor must carry the actual last emitted key.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs:326-380 — page-sequence validation for resume semantics
pub fn validate_page_sequence<T: KeyedPageItem>(
    items: &[T],
    page_state: &PageState,
    previous_last_key: Option<&ItemKey>,
    shard_start: &[u8],
    shard_end: &[u8],
) -> Result<(), PageSequenceViolation> {
    validate_filled_page(items, shard_start, shard_end)?;

    let first_key = items
        .first()
        .expect("validate_filled_page guarantees non-empty")
        .item_key();
    if let Some(prev) = previous_last_key
        && first_key <= prev
    {
        return Err(PageSequenceViolation::CursorDidNotAdvance {
            previous_last: prev.as_bytes().to_vec(),
            first_key: first_key.as_bytes().to_vec(),
        });
    }
```

`GitRepoTarget` is already the right emitted item shape. Ordering and pagination are defined entirely by `RepoKey`; `display_name` is diagnostic-only and already redacted in debug output.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:348-413 — Git repo discovery items already implement KeyedPageItem
pub struct GitRepoTarget {
    repo_key: RepoKey,
    locator: RepoLocator,
    display_name: Option<String>,
}

impl KeyedPageItem for GitRepoTarget {
    #[inline]
    fn item_key(&self) -> &ItemKey {
        self.repo_key.as_item_key()
    }
```

The generic conformance helpers also make one important resume requirement explicit: token loss or token corruption must not block key-authoritative resume when the last emitted key is available. Ticket 8 should preserve that contract even if the static source does not need tokens at all.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/conformance.rs:533-552 — stale/corrupt tokens must not change key-authoritative resume
let clean = drain_from_cursor(
    &mut clean_source,
    shard,
    Cursor::with_last_key(resume_key.clone()),
    drain_budgets,
    DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES,
)?;

let corrupt = drain_from_cursor(
    &mut corrupt_source,
    shard,
    Cursor::with_token(resume_key, corrupt_token),
    drain_budgets,
    DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES,
)?;
```

Finally, the documented Git family flow already calls out that discovery is its own stage, separate from mirror sync and repo execution. Ticket 8 should keep that seam narrow and not backfill later stages.

```text
// docs/source-families.md:94-99 — documented Git family pipeline
1. GitRepoDiscoverySource::discover_page(shard, cursor, budgets)
   -> Result<Option<PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>>, EnumerateError>
      Ok(None) => terminal completion (shard fully enumerated)
2. GitMirrorManager::sync_mirror(locator)
   -> Result<LocalMirror, GitRunError>
3. GitRepoExecutor::run_repo(mirror, selection, limits)
```

## Desired State

Introduce a minimal `StaticGitRepoDiscoverySource` or `SingleTargetGitRepoDiscoverySource` that emits the one normalized Git target carried in shard payload and obeys repo-frontier paging semantics without requiring an external control-plane lookup.

At minimum:
- hold exactly one `GitRepoTarget` plus any lightweight state needed to ensure it emits at most once,
- implement `discover_page()` so the first in-range call returns a one-item `PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>`,
- make resume key-authoritative: if the cursor’s last key is at or past the carried target’s `RepoKey`, the source must return `Ok(None)` regardless of token state,
- ignore missing/stale/corrupt tokens when `last_key` already proves the target is complete,
- guarantee out-of-range targets are never emitted when the shard bounds do not include the carried `RepoKey`,
- either leave `choose_split_point()` as `Ok(None)` for MVP or return only a trivial midpoint hint that cannot violate one-target-per-shard geometry.

Important semantic requirements:
- logs/debug output must continue to redact raw repo paths and display metadata,
- discovery must remain deterministic for the same payload and cursor state,
- completion must be explicit and replay-safe: the source may emit the target once, but it must never re-emit it after a cursor proving completion.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_discovery.rs` | **NEW** — define the static/single-target discovery source, paging logic, and focused unit tests. | The runtime crate is where family-specific frontier hydration and execution seams live. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs` | Wire the new discovery source into the Git runtime boundary or expose a narrow constructor/helper for later Ticket 11 runtime use. | `git_repo.rs` already owns the Git runtime placeholder entrypoints. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Export the discovery module if later runtime paths need it directly. | Keeps the source reusable by the eventual worker loop. |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` | Touch only if a tiny helper/accessor on `GitRepoTarget` or discovery capabilities is genuinely needed. | The contract already has the right nouns; avoid parallel discovery types. |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs` or tests | Reuse as-is unless a tiny generic helper is needed for validated Git page construction. | Page validation already lives here. |

### Patterns to Follow

- Use `PageBuf::try_new_validated()` for one-item page emission instead of hand-rolling order/bounds checks.
- Treat `cursor.last_key()` as authoritative for resume. Tokens are optional and must not be required for correct replay.
- Emit at most one target per source instance / shard payload.
- Keep discovery bounded and deterministic. This source should not do filesystem scans, directory walks, or mirror checks; it should only expose the already-normalized target carried by the shard.
- Default `choose_split_point()` to `Ok(None)` unless there is a compelling trivial hint that preserves exact one-target geometry.
- Preserve existing redaction semantics through `GitRepoTarget`, `RepoLocator`, and `display_name` debug behavior.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `GitRepoDiscoverySource` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:637-666` | Implement the existing discovery trait directly. |
| `GitRepoTarget` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:348-413` | Emit the payload-carried target through the existing keyed page item type. |
| `PageBuf::try_new_validated` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs:47-76` | Construct valid one-item discovery pages without duplicating bounds/order checks. |
| `validate_page_sequence` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs:326-380` | Use in tests to prove resume/cursor correctness. |
| `Cursor::with_last_key` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:700-723` | Build key-authoritative resume fixtures in tests. |
| token-fallback conformance pattern | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/conformance.rs:533-552` | Mirror the same stale-token resume requirement in Git discovery tests. |

### Blast Radius

- Ticket 11’s runtime loop will use this discovery source to turn a Git shard payload into a frontier completion step before mirror sync and repo execution.
- If this source re-emits the carried target after resume, later runtime tickets can violate no-overlap/no-gap semantics immediately even with only one target per shard.
- If it requires tokens for resume, crash/restart behavior will drift from the connector family’s key-authoritative contract.


### Allocation Tier & Approach (Task Forge Enrichment)

**Allocation tier:** ALL COLD. Discovery runs once per shard claim lifecycle. Optimize for clarity. `.clone()` on `GitRepoTarget` is acceptable (single call per shard). No deadline/budget checking needed (sub-microsecond execution).

**State tracking:** Use a `bool` field (`emitted: bool`) rather than `Option<GitRepoTarget>.take()`. The `take()` pattern loses the target for debug inspection and logging. The `bool` flag keeps the target accessible while preventing double-emission.

**Shard bounds guard sequence — follow `fill_page_single_file` exactly** (`crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:510-521`):

```rust
// Guard 1: target below shard start
if !shard.key_range_start().is_empty()
    && self.target.item_key().as_bytes() < shard.key_range_start()
{
    return Ok(None);
}
// Guard 2: cursor already at or past target (key-authoritative resume)
if cursor
    .last_key()
    .is_some_and(|last_key| self.target.item_key().as_bytes() <= last_key.as_bytes())
{
    return Ok(None);
}
// Guard 3: target at or past shard end (exclusive upper bound)
if !shard.key_range_end().is_empty()
    && self.target.item_key().as_bytes() >= shard.key_range_end()
{
    return Ok(None);
}
```

**Page construction — use `PageBuf::try_new_validated`** (not `try_new`). Error wrapping pattern from `filesystem.rs:567-574`:

```rust
PageBuf::try_new_validated(
    vec![self.target.clone()],
    PageState::Complete,
    shard.key_range_start(),
    shard.key_range_end(),
)
.map(Some)
.map_err(|error| EnumerateError::permanent(format!("invalid git discovery page: {error}")))
```

**Return `PageState::Complete`** not `HasMore`. Single-item source has no continuation.

**Capabilities:** Construct explicitly:
```rust
GitDiscoveryCapabilities {
    paging: PagingCapabilities {
        ordered_keys: true,
        resumable: false,
        split_hints: false,
    },
}
```

**Constructor:** Simple `fn new(target: GitRepoTarget) -> Self`.

**Module placement:** `git_discovery.rs` as a sibling to `git_repo.rs`. Add `pub mod git_discovery;` to `lib.rs`.

### Key Pattern References (Task Forge Enrichment)

| Pattern | Location | Role |
|---------|----------|------|
| `fill_page_single_file` | `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:502-575` | THE primary reference for single-item enumeration with three-guard pattern |
| `StubDiscovery` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:842-857` | Trait implementation shape |
| Page construction + error wrapping | `crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:567-574` | Error wrapping pattern |
| Test helper factories | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:826-839` | `repo_key()`, `repo_locator()`, `repo_target()` |

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid (Task Forge Enrichment)

| Anti-Pattern | Why | Do Instead |
|-------------|-----|------------|
| `Option<T>.take()` for emit-once | Loses re-inspection capability | `bool emitted` flag |
| `PageState::HasMore` for single-item | Unnecessary round-trip | `PageState::Complete` |
| Inspecting `cursor.token()` | Violates key-authoritative contract | Only inspect `cursor.last_key()` |
| `PageBuf::try_new()` without validation | Skips shard-bounds checking | `PageBuf::try_new_validated()` |
| Putting impl in gossip-contracts | Belongs in runtime crate | `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_discovery.rs` |
| Tests in separate file | Project convention: inline | `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in same file |

## Code References

## Design Notes

### One-Target Discovery Still Needs Real Paging Semantics

Even though MVP shards carry only one repo target, the discovery step still needs to honor the repo-frontier contract so later shard-splitting or multi-target work composes without replacing the interface.

### Resume Is Driven By `last_key`, Not By Tokens

The static source should treat tokens as optional transport noise. If `cursor.last_key()` is already at or beyond the carried `RepoKey`, the source is done.

### Discovery Stops Before Mirror Work

This task should not couple discovery to repo existence checks beyond what earlier normalization already guaranteed. Mirror sync, ref lowering, and repo execution belong to later tickets.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Source re-emits the carried target after restart because it ignores `last_key` | Medium | High | Require key-authoritative resume tests and sequence validation. |
| Discovery requires tokens and fails when token state is missing or stale | Medium | High | Explicitly test token-loss and corrupt-token resume behavior. |
| Out-of-range target leaks past shard bounds | Low | High | Always construct pages through `try_new_validated()` using shard bounds. |
| Task expands into mirror or executor logic because the pipeline stages are adjacent | Medium | Medium | Keep ownership limited to `discover_page()` and optional trivial split hints. |
| Debug/log output leaks raw repo metadata | Low | Medium | Reuse `GitRepoTarget` / `RepoLocator` redaction behavior rather than new debug structs. |

## Performance Considerations

**Allocation tier:** ALL COLD — discovery runs once per shard claim lifecycle. No allocation-silence requirements.

- O(1) execution: one key comparison against shard bounds, one against cursor state, at most one one-item page allocation.
- `.clone()` on `GitRepoTarget` is acceptable (once per `discover_page` call that emits).
- `Vec` allocation for the single-item page is fine (no pooling needed).
- No deadline/budget checking required (sub-microsecond execution).
- `choose_split_point()` remains `Ok(None)` — no computation.
- Avoid external control-plane lookups or filesystem checks; the payload already contains the normalized target.

## Testing Strategy
