title: Build the scanner-git execution adapter
description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 9 is the adapter seam between the Git family runtime contracts and `scanner-git`’s existing `run_git_scan(...)` engine. Tickets 6-8 define the inputs that adapter should consume: explicit commits lower into stable explicit refs (`gossip-9430`), mirrors become deterministic local repo roots (`gossip-9431`), and static repo discovery yields one payload-backed `GitRepoTarget` per shard (`gossip-9432`). What is still missing is the concrete runtime executor that takes a prepared `LocalMirror`, a contract-level `GitSelection`, and `GitExecutionLimits`, translates them into `scanner_git::GitScanConfig`, and classifies execution outcomes on the existing runtime error boundary.

This task should implement that adapter only. It owns selection-to-start-set mapping, mirror-path execution, execution-limit translation, and retryable-vs-fatal outcome mapping. It does **not** own inner persistence adapters, repo-family durable receipts, or the distributed lease loop.

## Current State

The Git family contract already expects a repo executor, but there is no concrete adapter implementation today.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:674-683 — Git repo execution is still a trait boundary
pub trait GitRepoExecutor: Send {
    /// Execute a repo-native Git scan.
    fn run_repo(
        &mut self,
        mirror: &LocalMirror,
        selection: &GitSelection,
        limits: GitExecutionLimits,
    ) -> Result<GitRunOutcome, GitRunError>;
}
```

`gossip-scanner-runtime` already contains most of the low-level plumbing for direct local Git scans: it builds the engine, constructs a `scanner_git::GitScanConfig`, creates a native ref resolver, calls `run_git_scan`, and translates the report back into the crate-level `ScanReport`.

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:94-147 — direct local scan path already calls run_git_scan
let git_sink: Arc<dyn scanner_git::EventSink> =
    Arc::new(ChannelEventOutput::new(event_tx.clone()));
let git_cfg = build_git_scan_config(config)?;
let resolver = NativeRefResolver::new(git_cfg.start_set.clone());
let watermarks = EmptyWatermarkStore;
let seen = NeverSeenStore;

let result = run_git_scan(
    &canonical_repo,
    engine,
    &resolver,
    &seen,
    &watermarks,
    None,
    &git_cfg,
    git_sink,
)
```

The critical gap is in `build_git_scan_config()`: it maps a subset of runtime settings, but it hardcodes `StartSetConfig::DefaultBranchOnly` and therefore ignores contract-level `GitSelection` entirely.

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:166-215 — current config mapper ignores selection
let mut git_cfg = RuntimeGitScanConfig {
    repo_id: config.repo_id,
    scan_mode: config.scan_mode,
    merge_diff_mode: config.merge_mode,
    pack_exec_workers: config.workers.max(1),
    enrich_identities: config.enrich_identities,
    start_set: StartSetConfig::DefaultBranchOnly,
    ..RuntimeGitScanConfig::default()
};
git_cfg.engine_adapter.scan_binary = config.scan_binary;
```

The contract-level selection type already carries everything the adapter needs to map into a `scanner-git` start set and merge mode without reopening raw request input.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:286-334 — GitSelection is the runtime-facing tuple
pub struct GitSelection {
    refs: GitRefSelection,
    scan_mode: GitScanMode,
    merge_strategy: GitMergeStrategy,
}

impl GitSelection {
    pub fn refs(&self) -> &GitRefSelection {
        &self.refs
    }

    pub fn scan_mode(&self) -> GitScanMode {
        self.scan_mode
    }

    pub fn merge_strategy(&self) -> GitMergeStrategy {
        self.merge_strategy
    }
}
```

`scanner-git` already exposes the corresponding runtime start-set config shape, including `ExplicitRefs`, and already treats that shape as the durable start-set identity boundary.

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/runner.rs:132-141 — scanner-git config already expects a StartSetConfig
pub struct GitScanConfig {
    pub scan_mode: GitScanMode,
    pub repo_id: u64,
    pub policy_hash: [u8; 32],
    pub start_set: StartSetConfig,
    pub merge_diff_mode: MergeDiffMode,
    pub repo_open: RepoOpenLimits,
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/start_set.rs:49-75 — start-set variants match the contract-level ref-selection intent
pub enum StartSetConfig {
    DefaultBranchOnly,
    AllRemoteBranches {
        remote: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    },
    BranchesAndTags {
        include_remote_branches: bool,
        remote: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    },
    ExplicitRefs {
        refs: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    },
}
```

The `LocalMirror` contract result already exposes the repo root that the adapter should run against. Ticket 9 should use the prepared mirror path, not reopen the original source repo path.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:434-456 — LocalMirror exposes the prepared local repo root
impl LocalMirror {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: path.into(),
            last_synced_at_ms: None,
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    #[must_use]
    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        self.path.as_path()
    }
}
```

Finally, the current Git runtime docs already describe the family split correctly: `git_repo` is supposed to cover repository discovery and repository execution paths. Ticket 9 should complete that path, not invent a parallel executor outside the runtime module.

```text
// docs/gossip-scanner-runtime.md:174-182 — git_repo family owns repository execution paths
- `ordered_content` covers sources that behave like forward-only item streams
- `git_repo` covers repository discovery and repository execution paths
- `distributed` exposes the worker-loop nouns for distributed shard execution
```

## Desired State

Introduce a concrete runtime Git executor adapter that implements `GitRepoExecutor` by reusing the existing `run_git_scan(...)` plumbing against a prepared `LocalMirror`.

At minimum:
- map `GitSelection::refs()` into the matching `StartSetConfig` variant without losing ref names or widening selection,
- preserve `scan_mode` and `merge_strategy` semantics when constructing `scanner_git::GitScanConfig`,
- execute against `mirror.path()` rather than the original source repo path,
- map `GitExecutionLimits` into the existing runtime config knobs and `scanner_git::GitScanConfig` fields,
- support the explicit-commit-lowered path from Ticket 6 by treating it as ordinary `ExplicitRefs`,
- classify outcomes on the existing error boundary:
  - retryable mirror/execution failures stay retryable `GitRunError`,
  - invalid refs or invalid explicit-commit-lowered selections become fatal input/config errors,
  - concurrent maintenance remains retryable.

Important semantic requirements:
- the adapter must preserve stable ref names so watermark and `StartSetId` behavior stays consistent with Tickets 6 and `scanner-git`,
- it must not introduce a commit-only execution mode,
- it must not flatten or bypass inner `scanner-git` semantics just to fit the outer runtime shape.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs` | **NEW** or equivalent — define the concrete `GitRepoExecutor` adapter and focused tests. | A dedicated module keeps the adapter distinct from discovery and from the direct local-scan entrypoint. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs` | Refactor/reuse existing `scan_local_repo()` and `build_git_scan_config()` helpers so the new adapter shares one runtime path rather than duplicating runner setup. | Most of the needed plumbing already exists here. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Export any new adapter surface that later distributed/runtime tickets need. | Keeps the executor seam reusable. |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` | Touch only if a tiny helper is needed on `GitSelection`, `GitExecutionLimits`, or `GitRunOutcome`. | The contract surface already has the right execution nouns. |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/start_set.rs` | Reuse as-is unless a tiny helper is needed for explicit `GitRefSelection` -> `StartSetConfig` mapping tests. | The adapter should consume the existing runtime start-set seam. |

### Patterns to Follow

- Reuse the existing `scan_local_repo()` / `build_git_scan_config()` path rather than writing a second `run_git_scan()` wrapper from scratch.
- Convert contract-level `GitRefSelection` into `StartSetConfig` 1:1:
  - `DefaultBranchOnly` -> `DefaultBranchOnly`
  - `AllRemoteBranches { remote }` -> `AllRemoteBranches { remote }`
  - `BranchesAndTags { include_remote_branches, remote }` -> matching `BranchesAndTags`
  - `ExplicitRefs { refs }` -> `ExplicitRefs { refs }`
- Preserve explicit ref names exactly. Do not sort, canonicalize, or rewrite them in the adapter; Ticket 6 and `StartSetConfig` identity logic already own that.
- Treat the prepared mirror as the repo root. The adapter should not reach back to raw source locators once it has `LocalMirror`.
- Keep error classification on the `GitRunError` / `ScanRuntimeError` boundaries already used by the runtime instead of introducing new ad hoc enums.
- Keep persistence out of scope here. Ticket 9 may produce `GitRunOutcome`, but Ticket 10 owns inner persistence adapters and durable receipts.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `scan_local_repo()` | `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:94-160` | Refactor or generalize the existing direct local-scan path into a reusable mirror-backed executor path. |
| `build_git_scan_config()` | `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_repo.rs:166-215` | Extend the existing config mapper to consume `GitSelection` instead of hardcoding the default branch. |
| `GitSelection` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:286-334` | Drive start-set, scan-mode, and merge-strategy mapping from the existing contract tuple. |
| `GitExecutionLimits` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:496-585` | Map runtime limit knobs from the contract type instead of inventing executor-local settings. |
| `StartSetConfig` | `crates/scanner-git/src/start_set.rs:49-75` | Use the existing runtime start-set boundary and identity semantics. |
| `GitRunError::concurrent_maintenance()` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:618-623` | Preserve retryable classification for artifact/mirror maintenance invalidation. |

### Blast Radius

- Ticket 10’s persistence/durable-receipt work will sit directly below this adapter and needs it to preserve `scanner-git` semantics rather than flattening them.
- Ticket 11’s distributed runtime loop will call this adapter after discovery and mirror sync; any ambiguity about retryable vs fatal classification here becomes lease-loop behavior later.
- If the adapter rewrites explicit refs or changes selection identity, Ticket 6’s synthetic-ref stability guarantee is lost.


### Implementation Guidance Addendum (Enriched)

**Allocation tier**: ALL COLD. All code in `git_executor.rs` runs at per-call dispatch boundary, not inner loops. Optimize for clarity.

**Struct design**:
- `ScannerGitExecutor` holds a pre-built `Arc<scanner_engine::Engine>` and an `Arc<dyn scanner_git::EventSink>`. Both injected at construction time because `run_repo` does not accept them.
- Engine construction is expensive (regex compilation); amortize across repos.

**Conversion helpers** (place in `git_executor.rs`, NOT in contracts crate):
- `fn map_scan_mode(mode: gossip_contracts::connector::git::GitScanMode) -> scanner_git::GitScanMode` — exhaustive match, 2 arms.
- `fn map_merge_strategy(strategy: GitMergeStrategy) -> MergeDiffMode` — exhaustive match, 2 arms.
- Do NOT implement `From` traits across the crate boundary (contracts must not depend on scanner-git).

**`GitExecutionLimits` to `RuntimeGitScanConfig` mapping**:
- `pack_exec_workers`: `limits.pack_exec_workers().unwrap_or_else(available_workers).max(1)`
- `scan_binary` -> `git_cfg.engine_adapter.scan_binary`
- `enrich_identities` -> `git_cfg.enrich_identities`
- `tree_delta_cache_mb`: when `Some`, pass through `mebibytes_to_u32_bytes` (reuse from `git_repo.rs`, now `pub(crate)`)
- `engine_chunk_mb`: when `Some`, pass through `mebibytes_to_usize_bytes` (reuse from `git_repo.rs`, now `pub(crate)`)
- `debug_level`: post-scan formatting only; does not enter `RuntimeGitScanConfig`

**Reusable utilities** (promote to `pub(crate)`, do not duplicate):
- `start_set_from_ref_selection` (git_repo.rs:248)
- `mebibytes_to_u32_bytes` / `mebibytes_to_usize_bytes` (git_repo.rs:187-211) — extract from nested fn to module-level `pub(crate) fn`
- `format_git_debug_output` (git_repo.rs:315)
- `digest_repo_path` (git_repo.rs:174)
- `build_runtime_engine` (lib.rs:901)
- `forward_git_events` + `ChannelEventOutput` (lib.rs)
- `available_workers` (lib.rs:877)
- `EmptyWatermarkStore` / `NeverSeenStore` (scanner_git)
- `NativeRefResolver` (scanner_git)

**Error classification** (`classify_scan_error` function):
```rust
fn classify_scan_error(err: GitScanError, mirror_path: &Path) -> GitRunError {
    match err {
        GitScanError::ConcurrentMaintenance => GitRunError::concurrent_maintenance(),
        GitScanError::ArtifactAcquire(ArtifactAcquireError::ConcurrentMaintenance) => {
            GitRunError::concurrent_maintenance()
        }
        GitScanError::RepoOpen(_) => GitRunError::permanent(format!(...)),
        GitScanError::UnsupportedMode(_) => GitRunError::permanent(format!(...)),
        GitScanError::ResourceLimit(_) => GitRunError::permanent(format!(...)),
        // All other pipeline-stage errors are retryable (transient I/O,
        // corrupt pack state that may be resolved by re-mirror).
        other => GitRunError::retryable(format!(...)),
    }
}
```
Note: `ArtifactAcquireError::ConcurrentMaintenance` is nested inside `GitScanError::ArtifactAcquire` — the match arm must destructure it to classify correctly.

**`GitRunOutcome` construction from `GitScanReport`**:
- `commit_count`: `u64::try_from(report.commit_count).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` — saturating conversion from `usize`.
- Metric fields from `report.common_metrics`: `objects_scanned`, `bytes_scanned`, `chunks_scanned`, `findings_emitted`, `errors`.
- `scan_ns`: prefer `stage_nanos.scan` when > 0, else wall-clock elapsed.
- `persist_ns: 0` — persistence is out of scope.

**Edge cases**:
- Reject empty `mirror.path()` with permanent `GitRunError` before attempting `run_git_scan`.
- Empty `ExplicitRefs { refs: vec![] }` means "scan no refs" — let it pass through, do not treat as error.
- ExplicitRefs lowering is the caller's responsibility — do NOT call `materialize_synthetic_commit_ref` inside `run_repo`.

**Anti-patterns to avoid**:
- Do not create a shared "build config" function with 15+ parameters for both the existing `GitScanConfig` and the new `GitSelection + GitExecutionLimits` input shapes.
- Do not add `From<GitScanMode>` or `From<GitMergeStrategy>` impls in gossip-contracts (boundary violation).
- Do not wildcard re-export from `git_executor` (`pub use git_executor::*`). Use explicit named exports.
- Do not add new error types. Use `GitRunError` (from `define_connector_error!`) as-is.
- Do not map all `GitScanError` variants to permanent — most pipeline failures are transient and must remain retryable.

## Code References

```rust
    fn run_repo(
        &mut self,

```

```rust
let result = run_git_scan(

```


## Design Notes

### Extend The Existing Runtime Path, Do Not Fork It

The direct local Git scan path in `gossip-scanner-runtime` already knows how to run `scanner-git`. Ticket 9 should generalize or reuse that path for mirror-backed execution instead of creating an unrelated executor wrapper with separate behavior.

### Selection Identity Must Survive Translation

The adapter’s job is translation, not reinterpretation. If the contract-level selection says “these explicit refs with this scan mode and merge strategy,” the `scanner-git` config should reflect that exactly.

### Mirror Path Is The Only Repo Root Here

Once Ticket 7 hands the adapter a `LocalMirror`, execution should be fully mirror-backed. The adapter should not need raw source repo paths or control-plane lookups.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Adapter duplicates `scan_local_repo()` logic instead of reusing it | Medium | High | Require refactor/reuse of the existing runtime wrapper and config mapper. |
| Selection mapping silently drops `scan_mode` or `merge_strategy` | Medium | High | Add explicit mapping tests for all `GitSelection` fields. |
| Explicit-commit-lowered refs are rewritten again, changing start-set identity | Low | High | Preserve explicit ref names exactly and treat Ticket 6 output as authoritative. |
| Fatal selection errors are surfaced as retryable runtime failures | Medium | High | Pin error classification rules in acceptance criteria and tests. |
| Task drifts into persistence or receipt logic | Medium | Medium | Keep durable receipt work explicitly deferred to Ticket 10. |

## Performance Considerations

All code in `git_executor.rs` is **COLD tier** (per-call dispatch boundary, not inner loops). No allocation-silence constraints apply.

- **Engine pre-construction**: `Arc<Engine>` is built once at `ScannerGitExecutor` construction, not per `run_repo` call. Regex compilation in engine construction is the dominant cost; amortizing it across runs is essential.
- **Event forwarding**: Same bounded `sync_channel(EVENT_CHANNEL_CAP)` + scoped-thread pattern as `scan_local_repo`. The channel capacity is tuned to absorb finding bursts without blocking the scan thread.
- **`commit_count: usize -> u64`**: Use `u64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` rather than bare `as u64`, which silently truncates on 32-bit platforms.
- **MiB overflow checks**: Reuse the existing `mebibytes_to_u32_bytes` / `mebibytes_to_usize_bytes` helpers. The `NonZeroU32` / `NonZeroUsize` types in `GitExecutionLimits` guarantee zero is unrepresentable, so only overflow needs checking.
- The adapter should stay thin. Most cost belongs to `scanner-git`; this task adds translation overhead only.

## Testing Strategy

**Framework**: rstest (already in dev-dependencies). No new dependencies needed.

All tests in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:

4. **`test_execution_limits_mapping`** — unit test. Construct `GitExecutionLimits` with all 6 fields set to non-default values. Verify the resulting `RuntimeGitScanConfig` has: `pack_exec_workers` from the NonZeroUsize value, `scan_binary` propagated, `enrich_identities` propagated, `tree_delta_cache_mb` converted via `mebibytes_to_u32_bytes`, `engine_chunk_mb` converted via `mebibytes_to_usize_bytes`, `debug_level` stored for post-scan formatting.

5. **`test_executor_uses_mirror_path`** — unit test. Verify the adapter passes `mirror.path()` to `run_git_scan`, not any other path. Validate structurally by checking the `PathBuf` argument passed to the scan function.

6. **`test_error_classification_retryable_vs_fatal`** — rstest parameterized over `GitScanError` variants. Classification rules:
   - `ConcurrentMaintenance` -> retryable (`GitRunError::concurrent_maintenance()`)
   - `ArtifactAcquire(ArtifactAcquireError::ConcurrentMaintenance)` -> retryable
   - `RepoOpen` -> permanent
   - `UnsupportedMode` -> permanent

7. **`test_explicit_commit_lowered_path`** — unit test. Construct `ExplicitRefs { refs: vec![b"refs/synth/abc".to_vec()] }`, verify it passes through as `StartSetConfig::ExplicitRefs` without special-casing.

| `GitExecutionLimits::default()` accessor values | Unit test | `gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` |

title: Add real-backend end-to-end launch proof for Git
description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 14 is the real-backend launch proof for Git. Earlier tickets provide the control-plane planner/setup, distributed runtime loop, production worker config, and durability integration, but the repository currently only has a filesystem real-backend proof. There is no Git equivalent proving that a real etcd + PostgreSQL worker launch can submit Git work, claim shards, complete them durably, and restart safely.

This task should add that Git launch proof only. It owns the real-backend integration test harness and matrix. It does **not** own the underlying Git runtime features or the general Git-specific contract/property tests from Ticket 13.

## Current State

The existing launch proof is explicitly filesystem-centric. It submits a `FilesystemRequest`, plans one initial shard, registers it through `setup_filesystem_run(...)`, and verifies that submission stops after registration rather than implicitly claiming the shard.

```rust
// crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs:213-265 — current submission helper is filesystem-only
fn submit_filesystem_request(
    coordinator: &mut EtcdCoordinator,
    scan_root: &Path,
    lease_duration_ms: u64,
) -> ShardKey {
    let request = FilesystemRequest::directory_root(scan_root, test_run_config(lease_duration_ms))
        .normalize()
        .expect("test filesystem request should normalize");
    let plan = plan_filesystem_initial_shards(request.clone());
    let payload = plan.shard_payload();
    let outcome = setup_filesystem_run(
        coordinator,
        now(1),
        tenant_id(),
        run_id(),
        FilesystemRunSetupInput::new(&request, plan.initial_shard(), &payload),
        OpId::from_raw(1),
    )
    .expect("test filesystem run setup should succeed");
    …
}
```

The worker-process launcher is likewise hardcoded to `--mode=connector fs`, which means the real-backend proof currently exercises only the filesystem distributed path.

```rust
// crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs:359-376 — worker launch is still wired to filesystem mode
command
    .arg("--mode=connector")
    .arg("fs")
    .arg(scan_root)
    .stdout(Stdio::piped())
    .stderr(Stdio::piped())
    .env(ENV_ETCD_ENDPOINTS, etcd_config.endpoints().join(","))
    .env(ENV_ETCD_NAMESPACE, etcd_config.namespace_prefix())
    .env(ENV_DONE_LEDGER_POSTGRES_DSN, done_ledger_dsn)
    .env(ENV_FINDINGS_POSTGRES_DSN, findings_dsn)
    .env(ENV_TENANT_ID, hex_encode(&TENANT_ID_BYTES))
    .env(ENV_RUN_ID, run_id().as_raw().to_string())
    .env(ENV_WORKER_ID, worker_id().as_raw().to_string())
    .env(ENV_POLICY_HASH, hex_encode(&POLICY_HASH_BYTES))
    .env(ENV_TENANT_SECRET_KEY, hex_encode(&TENANT_SECRET_KEY_BYTES))
    .env(ENV_WORKER_RULES_FILE, rules_path)
    .env(ENV_STARTUP_SCHEMA_MODE, "validate")
    .env("RUST_LOG", "info");
```

The current filesystem proof asserts the key integration properties Git will also need: worker launch succeeds, durable state is written, shard completion is visible in etcd, and restart is idempotent.

```rust
// crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs:480-506 — current proof validates durable completion
#[test]
fn worker_binary_happy_path_commits_to_real_backends_and_completes_the_shard() {
    let proof = SeededLaunchProof::new();

    let output = proof.run_worker_binary();
    assert_worker_success(&output, "real-backend worker happy path");

    let done_ledger_rows = proof.done_ledger_row_count();
    let observation_rows = proof.observation_row_count();
    assert_eq!(done_ledger_rows, 2);
    assert_eq!(observation_rows, 1);
    assert_completed_shard_state(&proof.coordinator, proof.shard_key);
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs:508-541 — restart is already proven idempotent for filesystem
#[test]
fn worker_binary_restart_is_idempotent_after_completed_shard() {
    let proof = SeededLaunchProof::new();

    let first = proof.run_worker_binary();
    assert_worker_success(&first, "first real-backend worker launch");
    let done_rows_after_first = proof.done_ledger_row_count();
    let observation_rows_after_first = proof.observation_row_count();

    let second = proof.run_worker_binary();
    assert_worker_success(&second, "worker restart after completed shard");

    assert_eq!(proof.done_ledger_row_count(), done_rows_after_first);
    assert_eq!(proof.observation_row_count(), observation_rows_after_first);
    assert_completed_shard_state(&proof.coordinator, proof.shard_key);
}
```

What does not exist is the Git equivalent: no Git repo generator, no Git request submission helper, no distributed Git worker launch, and no matrix covering default selection, explicit refs, explicit commits, or repo lists.

## Desired State

Add a Git real-backend launch proof that exercises the actual production-shaped stack:

- submit Git work through the orchestrator control plane,
- verify etcd run + shard state after submission,
- launch the worker binary in distributed Git mode against real etcd/PostgreSQL backends,
- assert durable completion and expected persisted state,
- rerun safely to prove idempotent replay.

Cover, at minimum, this matrix:

- single repo, default selection,
- single repo with explicit refs,
- single repo with explicit commit,
- explicit repo list.

The proof should stay local/static only. No provider discovery or hosted Git setup belongs here.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs` | Add Git fixture builders, Git submission helpers, worker launch variants, and Git assertions. | This is the existing real-backend proof harness. |
| `crates/gossip-orchestrator` Git setup helpers from Tickets 3-5 | Use the real Git control-plane surface rather than bypassing orchestrator setup. | The proof should validate the real submission path. |
| `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs` / `main.rs` only if the test needs stable CLI/env hooks | Keep the proof aligned with the user-visible distributed Git launch path. | Avoid hidden test-only launch modes. |

### Patterns to Follow

- Mirror the current filesystem proof's two-phase shape:
  - submission registers active shards but does not claim them,
  - worker launch performs the actual claim/execute/complete path.
- Mirror the restart idempotency assertion pattern already used for filesystem.
- Keep live-backend assertions grounded in persisted state and coordinator snapshots, not in implementation internals.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `submit_filesystem_request(...)` shape | `crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs` | Use it as the model for a Git submission helper that stops after shard registration. |
| `run_worker_process(...)` | `crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs` | Extend it for distributed Git launches instead of creating a parallel process harness. |
| `assert_completed_shard_state(...)` | `crates/gossip-worker/tests/real_backend_launch_proof.rs` | Reuse or generalize the etcd completion assertions for Git repo-frontier shards. |
| `contention_namespace` | `gossip-coordination-etcd::test_support` | Already used by FS proof for etcd namespace isolation. |
| `create_test_db` | `gossip-pg-common::test_support` | Already used by FS proof for PostgreSQL database provisioning. |
| `setup_git_run` | `gossip-orchestrator::git_setup` | Re-exported from `gossip-orchestrator` lib.rs. |
| `plan_git_initial_shards` | `gossip-orchestrator::git_planner` | Re-exported from `gossip-orchestrator` lib.rs. Requires `GitExecutionLimits` as second arg (unlike FS planner). |
| `GitRequest::single_repo` / `::repo_list` / `::repo_with_explicit_refs` / `::repo_with_explicit_commit` | `gossip-orchestrator::git_request` | Four constructors covering the entire test matrix. |

### Prerequisite: Unblock connector-mode Git support

Three sites must change before any Git launch proof test can pass:

| Location | Current State | Required Change |
|----------|--------------|-----------------|
| `config.rs` ~line 1312-1316 | `source=git` rejected with `UnsupportedCombination` | Remove the guard. Allow Git source with connector mode and production backend. |
| `config.rs` `DistributedWorkerConfig` ~line 723 | Hardcoded to `FsSourceSettings` | Generalize source settings field to support both FS and Git source settings. |
| `distributed.rs` `build_lease_from_acquire` | Calls `hydrate_filesystem_source_from_spec` unconditionally | Add Git-aware hydration path that reads Git source settings from the shard spec payload. |

**Note:** The existing test `connector_mode_rejects_git_source_for_local_git_scans` must be deleted or inverted once the guard is removed.

### Implementation Steps

**Step 0 — Unblock Git connector mode** (prerequisite to all tests): Apply the three changes above.

**Step 1 — Git fixture creation:** Reuse existing helpers where possible. Check `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/test_support.rs` for `init_git_repo`/`run_git_in` (pub(crate)) and `crates/gossip-worker/src/main.rs` tests for `create_git_repo`/`run_git`. Do NOT create a third copy. The fixture must: configure `user.name`/`user.email`, write an evidence file containing `SAFE_TOKEN`, and commit. For explicit-commit variants, capture the SHA via `git rev-parse HEAD`.

**Step 2 — `GitSeededLaunchProof` struct:** Pattern after existing `SeededLaunchProof`. Fields: coordinator client, DSNs, `GitScanFixture` (temp dir + repo path + HEAD OID). Submission flow: `GitRequest::single_repo` (or `::repo_list`) -> `plan_git_initial_shards` (requires `GitExecutionLimits`) -> `setup_git_run`.

**Step 3 — Worker process invocation:** Git proof passes `--mode=connector git <repo_path>` instead of `fs <scan_root>`. Parameterize the existing `run_worker_process` helper to accept source kind and path, or create a `run_git_worker_process` wrapper.

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

| Anti-Pattern | Why | What to Do Instead |
|--------------|-----|-------------------|
| Adding tests without unblocking Git connector mode | Worker binary rejects `--mode=connector git` at config resolution. Tests fail at process exit code. | First remove the `source != Fs` guard and generalize distributed payload hydration. |
| Creating a bare `git init` without commits | `scanner_git` operates on commit history; empty repos produce zero scan results. | Always create at least one commit with trackable content. |
| Hardcoding done-ledger row counts | Git scans enumerate blobs from commit diffs, not filesystem entries. Counts differ from FS. | Use `assert!(count > 0)` initially; tighten after empirical verification. |
| Duplicating `init_git_repo` helpers | Already exists in `gossip-orchestrator/src/test_support.rs` and `gossip-worker/src/main.rs` tests. | Search for and reuse existing implementations. |
| Setting `ENV_FS_SKIP_ARCHIVES` for Git runs | FS-specific env var, meaningless for Git. | Omit it from Git worker process invocations. |

### Blast Radius

- Depends on Ticket 11 and Ticket 12 being complete enough to submit and execute Git distributed work.
- Will likely need fixture helpers that create deterministic local Git repos with stable commits/refs for the matrix cases.
- Ticket 15 may later add more telemetry assertions; keep the proof focused on launch/completion/idempotency, not observability detail.

title: Add Git-specific contract, property, and failure tests
description:
## Context

Epic 3 Ticket 13 is the Git-family verification pass for the repo-frontier runtime. Tickets 2-12 add RepoKey normalization, Git payloads, mirror handling, execution, durability, runtime loop, and worker composition, but the current test surface does not yet prove Git-specific no-gap/no-overlap behavior, crash/retry safety, or replay-safe mirror/executor semantics at the repo-frontier boundary.

This task should add the missing contract, property, and failure tests for Git MVP. It owns test coverage only. It does **not** own the underlying Git runtime features themselves or the real-backend end-to-end launch proof.

## Current State

The project already documents a layered testing strategy: unit tests, conformance tests, scenario tests, and simulation all build toward protocol safety and liveness. The Git family should match that bar instead of relying on happy-path unit tests alone.

```text
// docs/gossip-coordination/coordination-testing.md:15-19 — runtime integration is expected to reuse family entrypoints
A family-oriented execution seam in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/` and
`gossip_contracts::connector` bridges coordination and scan execution.
Coordination tests continue to validate protocol invariants independently of
scan execution internals, while runtime integration tests exercise the same
family entrypoints used by the CLI and worker binaries.
```

The coordination test docs explicitly call out property-based testing and simulation as required tools for protocol behavior, not optional extras.

```text
// docs/gossip-coordination/coordination-testing.md:131-134 — property testing is already part of the project bar
The module also includes **property-based tests** (proptest) that fuzz
random operation sequences against the coordinator and assert structural
invariants (record consistency, fence monotonicity, cursor monotonicity,
idempotent replay) after every step.
```

The coordination simulation harness is designed around deterministic fault injection and invariant checking, including lease expiry and replay behavior. Git repo-frontier work should align with that philosophy.

```text
// docs/gossip-coordination/simulation-harness.md:123-139 — simulation verifies safety first, then convergence
### Stage 1: Safety

Runs `safety_ops` random operations under fault injection.

**Goal:** Verify that no invariant (S1-S9) is ever violated regardless of
operation ordering, timing, or fault injection.

### Stage 2: Liveness

Runs `liveness_ops` operations biased toward acquire and complete. No faults
are injected.

**Goal:** Verify that the system converges -- all shards reach a terminal
state (Done, Split, or Parked).
```

`scanner-git` already has its own deterministic simulation harness, including explicit invariants for watermark gating and schedule stability.

```text
// docs/scanner-git/git_simulation_harness_guide.md:31-46 — scanner-git already has deterministic invariants
- Determinism: identical inputs and seeds yield identical trace + outputs.
- Stability: changing only the schedule seed yields identical normalized output.
- Watermark gating: any skipped candidate yields `Partial` and suppresses
  watermark advancement.
- Ordering: refs are processed in lexicographic order by raw refname bytes.
- Output sets: scanned and skipped OIDs are sorted, unique, and disjoint.
```

The runtime durability suite already proves the core outer invariant Git must preserve: no durable receipt means no checkpoint progress, and retries after crashes must remain safe.

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs:678-717 — no receipt means no checkpoint progress
let mut aggregator = PrefixCheckpointAggregator::new(context, unit.sequence_no(), 4);
assert!(
    aggregator
        .prepare_checkpoint()
        .expect("checkpoint preparation should succeed")
        .is_none(),
    "without a receipt, the runtime must not fabricate checkpoint progress"
);
assert_eq!(aggregator.buffered_receipt_count(), 0);
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs:829-835 — crash-before-durability also yields no progress
assert!(
    aggregator
        .prepare_checkpoint()
        .expect("checkpoint preparation should succeed")
        .is_none(),
    "no receipt means no checkpoint progress"
);
```

What is missing is the Git-specific suite that composes these ideas at the repo-frontier layer: there are no repo-frontier property tests for token loss, lease loss mid-execution, durable-finalize vs outer-checkpoint crash windows, or redaction-safe Git telemetry/log assertions.

## Desired State

Add a Git-family test suite that proves the MVP runtime honors the same invariants the rest of the project already enforces:

- same request inputs normalize to the same ordered repo targets,
- repo-frontier resume is key-authoritative even when tokens are stale or missing,
- crash/retry does not let outer repo progress outrun inner durable finalize,
- lease loss stops execution without overlapping authoritative progress,
- mirror and executor replay remain idempotent,
- logs/telemetry stay redacted.

The suite should combine:

- unit tests for RepoKey / request normalization / payload / synthetic refs / classification,
- runtime integration tests for repo-frontier claim/execute/checkpoint behavior,
- property or simulation coverage for crash/retry and reassignment scenarios,
- targeted redaction assertions for Git-specific operational fields.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

**IMPORTANT: Orchestrator files corrected.** The Git-specific orchestrator types live in `git_request.rs`, `git_planner.rs`, `git_payload.rs` — NOT in the generic `request.rs`/`planner.rs`/`payload.rs` which are filesystem-only.

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` | Extend the existing Git contract tests for `RepoKey` ordering, `GitRunError` classification, and redaction behavior. | This file already owns the contract-level Git types and tests. |
| `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/git_request.rs` | Add request-normalization tests for the Git submission model introduced in earlier tickets. | The Git task should mirror the normalization discipline already used for filesystem requests. |
| `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/git_planner.rs` | Add planner tests for one-target-per-shard geometry and deterministic shard shape. | This is where the submission geometry becomes stable. |
| `crates/gossip-orchestrator/src/git_payload.rs` | Add payload codec tests for Git shard metadata. | The payload round-trip is what later runtime hydration consumes. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` | Add crash/retry and outer-checkpoint assertions for repo-frontier Git receipts. | This file already proves receipt-driven checkpoint behavior. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Add Git repo-frontier claim/execute/checkpoint integration tests around the new lease loop. **BLOCKED: `run_git_repo_frontier_lease` does not exist yet.** Defer to after gossip-9434/9437. | This is where runtime separation from ordered-content must be proven. |
| `crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/property/git_engine_adapter.rs` and `crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/property/git_commit_walk.rs` | Add deterministic property coverage for adapter and traversal edge cases. | These are the existing Git property-test surfaces in the repo. |
| `crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/simulation/git_scan_random.rs` and `crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/simulation/git_scan_corpus.rs` | Add deterministic failure/corpus/simulation coverage for finalize/watermark/replay edge cases. | These are the existing Git simulation entrypoints in the repo. |
| `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs` / `crates/gossip-worker/src/recorder.rs` tests | Add configuration and redaction assertions for distributed Git surfaces. | Git-specific logs and telemetry should be proven safe, not assumed safe. |

**Note:** `git_scan_shallow_limits.rs` is NOT a true simulation test — it shells out to `git` via `Command::new` and creates real tempdirs. Do NOT add DST-style sim tests to this file.

### Patterns to Follow

- Follow the layering in `docs/gossip-coordination/coordination-testing.md`: unit first, then conformance/runtime integration, then simulation/property sweeps.
- Reuse the scanner-git simulation harness when the failure mode is inside Git execution/finalize semantics.
- Reuse runtime durability tests for crash-before/after durable-proof behavior instead of building ad hoc assertions from scratch.

### Utilities to Reuse

|---------|----------|-------------|
| `PrefixCheckpointAggregator` durability helpers/tests | `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/runtime_durability_tests.rs` | Use them as the oracle for "outer checkpoint advances only from durable proof." |
| Git simulation harness | `docs/scanner-git/git_simulation_harness_guide.md` and `scanner-git` sim code | Use it for deterministic finalize/watermark/retry fault injection. |
| Coordination simulation patterns | `docs/gossip-coordination/simulation-harness.md` | Follow its lease-loss/reassignment mindset for repo-frontier runtime tests. |

### Blast Radius

- This task should add or tighten tests around almost every earlier Epic 3 seam, but it should avoid re-implementing production code just to test it.
- Ticket 14 will build on this by adding the real-backend proof; keep that separate from in-memory/property/simulation coverage here.
- Ticket 15 may add additional telemetry fields; tests written here should assert redaction behavior broadly enough to survive those additions.

### Implementation Guidance Addendum (Task Forge Enrichment)

**Proptest placement:**

- `gossip-orchestrator`: NO proptest dev-dep — proptest tests for orchestrator types go in `scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/property/` under `property-tests` feature gate
- `scanner-engine-integration-tests`: proptest available as direct dev-dep

**Phase 4 blocker:** `distributed.rs` only has `run_filesystem_lease`. There is no `run_git_repo_frontier_lease`. Distributed end-to-end Git tests are BLOCKED until gossip-9434 or gossip-9437 lands. Unit-level tests against `PrefixCheckpointAggregator` in repo-frontier mode ARE possible now.

**OnceLock reuse:** `scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/property/git_engine_adapter.rs` line 13 defines `static ENGINE: OnceLock<Engine>`. New property test files that need an engine instance must share this via a common module or re-export, NOT create a second OnceLock.

**Test infrastructure to reuse:**

| Utility | Location | Use For |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `write_context_with_epoch()`, `completed_unit()`, `scanned_translation()` | `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/test_fixtures` | Runtime durability tests |
| `InMemoryFindingsSink`, `InMemoryDoneLedger` | `gossip-persistence-inmemory` | Runtime durability tests |
| `GitSimRunner`, `GitFaultPlan`, `generate_scenario()` | `scanner-git/src/sim_git_scan/` | Simulation tests |
| `test_engine()` OnceLock | `scanner-engine-integration-tests/.../git_engine_adapter.rs` | Property tests |
| `TestCommitGraph`, `dag_strategy()` | `git_commit_walk.rs` | Property tests |
| `TestEnv`, `production_env()` | `config.rs` tests | Worker tests |
| `canary_raw_events()`, `full_coverage_records()` | `recorder.rs` tests | Redaction tests |
| `run_config()`, `init_git_repo()`, `run_git_in()` | `gossip-orchestrator/src/test_support.rs` | Orchestrator tests |
| `StubDiscovery`, `StubMirrorManager`, `StubExecutor` | `gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` tests | Contract tests |

**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

## Design Notes

### Prove The Boundary, Not Just The Happy Path

Git MVP's risk is not that a default-branch scan works once. The risk is that lease loss, retries, partial finalize, or cursor replay produce subtle no-gap/no-overlap violations. The tests should center those cases.

### Keep Real Backends Separate

Ticket 13 is the deterministic/conformance/property layer. The real etcd/PostgreSQL worker proof belongs in Ticket 14 so this task can stay fast, focused, and reproducible.

## Risk Analysis

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Git tests stop at unit coverage and miss lease-loss or crash windows | High | High | Require runtime integration plus property/simulation coverage. |
| Tests re-encode implementation details instead of asserting invariants | Medium | Medium | Reuse existing receipt/durability/simulation oracles. |
| Redaction gaps go untested because they are treated as "logging only" | Medium | High | Add explicit log/telemetry redaction assertions. |
| Test task expands into real-backend harness work | Medium | Medium | Keep full etcd/PostgreSQL launch proof deferred to Ticket 14. |
| Distributed runtime Git path does not yet exist | High | High | Phase 4 (distributed.rs) is explicitly blocked on gossip-9434/9437. Write unit-level tests against PrefixCheckpointAggregator repo-frontier mode instead. |

All code in this task is COLD tier (test-only). No benchmark-gated performance constraints apply to the test code itself.

- Property tests sharing an `Engine` via `OnceLock` amortize expensive engine construction. New property test files must follow this pattern rather than constructing engines per-test-case.

```rust
    let findings_sink = InMemoryFindingsSink::new();
    let done_ledger = InMemoryDoneLedger::new();
    let committer = ResultCommitter::new(findings_sink.clone(), done_ledger.clone());
    let context = write_context_with_epoch(700);

    let translation = scanned_translation(context, 0xA1, 1);
    let receipt = committer.commit_translation(context, &unit, &translation)
        .expect("inner finalize succeeds");
    // Simulate crash: do NOT record receipt to aggregator.

    assert!(aggregator.prepare_checkpoint().unwrap().is_none(),
        "outer checkpoint must not advance without explicit receipt");
    // Retry: re-derive and re-commit.
    let retry_receipt = committer.commit_translation(context, &unit, &translation)
        .expect("idempotent retry succeeds");
    let input = CheckpointAggregatorInput::new(

    assert_eq!(aggregator.record_receipt(input).unwrap(), ReceiptRecordOutcome::Buffered);
}
```

Add detection rules for 5 missing secret providers: Razorpay, Klaviyo, Braze, Kakao, LeanPlum
description:
## Context

The SecretLoc paper (arXiv:2510.18601, "Evaluating Large Language Models in
detecting Secrets in Android Apps", Alecci et al., Oct 2025) systematically
evaluated secret detection across 5135+ Android apps and discovered 10+ secret
types that all existing regex-based, static-analysis, and ML-based tools missed.
Cross-referencing the paper's findings against our 223 default rules identified
5 providers with zero coverage: Razorpay, Klaviyo, Braze, Kakao, and LeanPlum.

Deep research across official documentation, TruffleHog/Gitleaks rule sets, and
SDK source code confirmed the exact key formats and FP reduction strategies for
each provider.

## Current State

The scanner has 223 rules in `default_rules.yaml`. None of the following
providers are covered:

```yaml
# crates/scanner-engine/default_rules.yaml — no matches for:
# razorpay, klaviyo, braze, kakao, leanplum
```

The test at `crates/scanner-engine/src/rules/yaml_unit_tests.rs:636-638`
asserts the rule count:

```rust
// crates/scanner-engine/src/rules/yaml_unit_tests.rs:636-638
fn builtin_rules_count() {
    // ...
    assert_eq!(rules.len(), 223);
}
```

The doc at `docs/scanner-engine/detection-rules.md:17` states:

```
Built-in rules: 223
```

## Desired State

Add 5 new detection rules (one per provider, 6 total — Razorpay gets 2 rules
for key ID + key secret), bringing the total to 228-229. Each rule must follow
established patterns, minimize false positives, and pass all existing validation
tests.

## Implementation Guidance

### Rule Specifications

#### 1. Razorpay Key ID (prefix-structured, lowest FP risk)

**Pattern**: Follows `stripe-access-token` template (line 4259).

- **Format**: `rzp_test_` or `rzp_live_` prefix + 14 alphanumeric chars
- **Total length**: 23 characters
- **Charset**: `[A-Za-z0-9]`
- **Evidence**: TruffleHog detector (`trufflehog/pkg/detectors/razorpay/razorpay.go`),
  test data confirms `rzp_live_oE9IEkoNYnmwkG` (14-char payload).
  Official docs at `razorpay.com/docs/api/authentication/`.
- **Approach**: Prefix-structured rule. No `value_suppressors_any` needed (prefix
  constrains matches). Both `rzp_test_` and `rzp_live_` as anchors and keywords.

```yaml
- name: razorpay-key-id
  regex: \b(rzp_(?:test|live)_[A-Za-z0-9]{14})(?:[\x60'"\s;]|\\[nr]|$)
  anchors:
  - rzp_test
  - rzp_live
  radius: 256
  must_contain: null
  keywords_any:
  - rzp_test
  - rzp_live
  entropy:
    min_bits_per_byte: 3.0
    min_len: 10
    max_len: 256
    min_entropy_bits_per_byte: 2.0
  two_phase: null
  local_context: null
  secret_group: null
```

#### 2. Razorpay Key Secret (keyword-context, medium FP risk)

**Pattern**: Follows `launchdarkly-access-token` template (line 2756).

- **Format**: 24-character alphanumeric string, no prefix
- **Charset**: `[A-Za-z0-9]`
- **Evidence**: TruffleHog test data `u5FJFQ0KuTe4hD8iwza076e2`.
- **Approach**: Since the secret has no prefix, it must be gated by `razorpay`
  keyword context. Use keyword-context regex template with `value_suppressors_any`.

```yaml
- name: razorpay-key-secret
  regex: '(?i)[\w.-]{0,50}?(?:razorpay)(?:[ \t\w.-]{0,20})[\s''"]{0,3}(?:=|>|:{1,3}=|\|\||:|=>|\?=|,)[\x60''"\s=]{0,5}([A-Za-z0-9]{24})(?:[\x60''"\s;]|\\[nr]|$)'
  anchors:
  - razorpay
  - RAZORPAY
  radius: 256
  must_contain: null
  keywords_any:
  - razorpay
  - RAZORPAY
  value_suppressors_any:
  - "example"
  - "EXAMPLE"
  - "sample"
  - "SAMPLE"
  - "placeholder"
  - "PLACEHOLDER"
  - "changeme"
  - "CHANGE_ME"
  - "change_me"
  - "xxxxxx"
  - "XXXXXX"
  - "000000"
  - "abcdef"
  - "123456"
  - "dummy"
  - "DUMMY"
  - "redacted"
  - "REDACTED"
  - "YOUR_"
  - "your_"
  - "INSERT_"
  - "insert_"
  - "REPLACE_"
  - "replace_"
  - "fake_"
  - "FAKE_"
  - "test_"
  - "TEST_"
  entropy:
    min_bits_per_byte: 3.0
    min_len: 16
    max_len: 256
    min_entropy_bits_per_byte: 2.0
  two_phase: null
  local_context: null
  secret_group: null
```

#### 3. Klaviyo Private API Key (prefix-structured, low FP risk)

**Pattern**: Follows `stripe-access-token` / `huggingface-access-token` template.

- **Format**: `pk_` prefix + 34 alphanumeric characters
- **Total length**: 37 characters
- **Charset**: `[a-zA-Z0-9]`
- **Evidence**: TruffleHog detector (`trufflehog/pkg/detectors/klaviyo/klaviyo.go`)
  regex `\b(pk_[[:alnum:]]{34})\b`, test data `pk_1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx`.
  Official Klaviyo docs confirm "Private keys will have the prefix pk_".
- **FP discrimination**: Stripe also uses `pk_` but always followed by `live_`
  or `test_` (e.g., `pk_live_...`, `pk_test_...`). Klaviyo keys are `pk_` directly
  followed by 34 alphanumeric chars with no intermediate underscore segment.
  The regex `pk_[A-Za-z0-9]{34}` will NOT match Stripe keys because Stripe keys
  are `pk_live_` or `pk_test_` (the `_` after `live`/`test` extends beyond 34 chars).
- **Important**: Do NOT detect the public API key (6-char site ID) — it is
  explicitly not a secret per Klaviyo docs.

```yaml
- name: klaviyo-api-key
  regex: \b(pk_[A-Za-z0-9]{34})(?:[\x60'"\s;]|\\[nr]|$)
  anchors:
  - pk_
  radius: 256
  must_contain: null
  keywords_any:
  - pk_
  entropy:
    min_bits_per_byte: 3.0
    min_len: 16
    max_len: 256
    min_entropy_bits_per_byte: 2.0
  two_phase: null
  local_context: null
  secret_group: null
```

**Validation note**: Confirm the regex does NOT match Stripe `pk_live_` / `pk_test_`
keys. The Stripe rule (`stripe-access-token`) matches `sk_` and `rk_` prefixed
keys but not `pk_` — so Stripe publishable keys (`pk_live_...`) are NOT covered
by the existing Stripe rule. If needed, add a negative lookahead `pk_(?!(?:test|live)_)`
to explicitly exclude Stripe-patterned keys. However, since Stripe `pk_live_` +
payload is typically 24+ chars after `pk_live_`, and Klaviyo is exactly `pk_` +
34 chars, the length difference may naturally separate them. Test this.

#### 4. Braze REST API Key (UUID-format, keyword-context, medium-high FP risk)

**Pattern**: Follows `heroku-api-key` / `hubspot-api-key` template (line 2424/2490).

- **Format**: UUID v4 (`8-4-4-4-12` hex with hyphens, 36 chars total)
- **Charset**: `[0-9a-f]` + hyphens
- **Evidence**: Official Braze docs at `braze.com/docs/api/basics/` confirm UUID
  format. Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer {API_KEY}`. REST endpoints are
  instance-specific: `rest.iad-01.braze.com`, `rest.fra-01.braze.eu`, etc.
  The old product name was "Appboy" — include as keyword for legacy code.
- **FP strategy**: UUID format is generic. MUST use `uuid_format_secret: true`,
  `keywords_any` (braze/appboy), and full `value_suppressors_any` list.
  No Gitleaks or TruffleHog rule exists for Braze.

```yaml

  - APPBOY

  - "changeme"

  - "INSERT_"

  two_phase: null
  local_context: null
```

#### 5. Kakao REST API Key (keyword-context, 32-char hex)

**Pattern**: Follows `launchdarkly-access-token` template.

- **Format**: 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string
- **Charset**: `[a-f0-9]`
- **Evidence**: Official Kakao Developers docs at
  `developers.kakao.com/docs/latest/en/app-setting/app`. Auth header uses
  distinctive `KakaoAK` prefix: `Authorization: KakaoAK {REST_API_KEY}`.
  All 4 key types (REST API, Native App, JavaScript, Admin) are 32-char hex.
- **FP risk**: 32-char hex overlaps with MD5 hashes. MUST require `kakao` keyword
  context. Include `KakaoAK` as an anchor for the auth header pattern.
- **No existing rules** in Gitleaks or TruffleHog.

```yaml

  regex: (?i)[\w.-]{0,50}?(?:kakao)(?:[ \t\w.-]{0,20})[\s'"]{0,3}(?:=|>|:{1,3}=|\|\||:|=>|\?=|,)[\x60'"\s=]{0,5}([a-f0-9]{32})(?:[\x60'"\s;]|\\[nr]|$)
  anchors:
  - kakao
  - KAKAO
  - KakaoAK
  radius: 256
  must_contain: null
  keywords_any:
  - kakao
  - KAKAO
  - KakaoAK
  value_suppressors_any:
  - "example"
  - "EXAMPLE"
  - "sample"
```

Note: `digit_penalty: true` subtracts from Shannon entropy for all-digit

description:
## Context

For enterprise customers scanning monorepos with 10M+ objects and multi-hour scan times, the current all-or-nothing Git scan pipeline wastes all progress when a worker dies mid-scan. Watermarks only advance on complete runs (`FinalizeOutcome::Complete` in `finalize.rs:128-132`), and there is no mechanism to persist partial progress within a single scan invocation. As the system becomes stateful for enterprises scanning a wide variety of repositories — from millions of small repos to massive monorepos — mid-scan resumption becomes critical for operational reliability.

This epic originated from a deep-research evaluation of three external articles proposing Git commit-graph position-based frontiers, MIDX + Roaring bitmap visited sets, and frontier + bitset + pack-offset checkpointing. The research (5 parallel agents, synthesizer, integrator) found that:

1. **The durable layer (OID watermarks + RoaringSeenBitmap + MIDX) is already built and solid.** Two of the three articles largely describe infrastructure that already exists in `scanner-git`.
2. **The missing 40% is the session-durable mid-scan checkpoint layer** — the ability to persist progress between pipeline stages so that worker death doesn't waste hours of pack decompression.
3. **Position-based frontiers are unsound** for our architecture (ephemeral `CommitGraphMem`, HashMap O(1) lookup, positions shift on any commit set change).
4. **Pack-plan-level checkpointing is the highest-leverage addition** — each completed pack plan in `execute_pack_plans_with_scheduler()` is an independent unit of work that can be durably recorded.

## Current State

The Git scan pipeline runs as a single atomic unit with no mid-scan progress persistence:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/finalize.rs:117-132 — all-or-nothing watermark gating
pub enum FinalizeOutcome {
    Complete,
    Partial,
}
// Partial runs produce empty watermark_ops — no progress saved.
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/roaring_seen.rs:256-260 — seen-bitmap only persisted at finalize
pub struct RoaringSeenBitmap {
    oid_len: u8,
    oids: Vec<OidBytes>,   // sorted OID index
    seen: RoaringBitmap,    // bit i set iff oids[i] has been seen
}
// SeenBitmapDelta written only via FinalizeOutput — not incrementally during scan.
```

The pipeline has natural checkpoint boundaries but no mechanism to use them:
```
repo_open → commit_plan → tree_diff/blob_intro → spill/dedup → mapping_bridge
→ pack_planning → pack_exec(plan₀) → pack_exec(plan₁) → ... → loose_scan → finalize → persist
```

The coordination layer already has `CheckpointBoundaryKind::RepoFrontier` for Git scans and `PrefixCheckpointAggregator` supports incremental flush cycles.

## Desired State

A Git scan pipeline that persists progress at natural stage boundaries, enabling resumption after worker death without re-doing completed work:

1. **Incremental seen-bitmap persistence** — `SeenBitmapDelta` written after spiller flush batches, not just at finalize.
2. **Pack-plan completion tracking** — Roaring bitmap of completed `pack_id` values persisted after each pack plan executes.
3. **Stage-gated mid-scan checkpoints** — Progress checkpointed at post-spill, between pack plans, and pre-finalize boundaries.
4. **Generation-augmented watermarks** — `(oid, generation)` pairs for O(1) force-push detection without ancestry DFS.
5. **On-disk commit-graph reading** — For large repos, read `gix_commitgraph::Graph` instead of BFS-loading `CommitGraphMem` to reduce startup cost.

## Implementation Guidance

### Sub-tasks (ordered by dependency and impact)

| # | Task | Impact | Complexity | Dependencies |
|---|------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | Incremental seen-bitmap persistence | High | S | None |
| 2 | Pack-plan completion tracking | High | S | Task 1 |
| 3 | Stage-gated mid-scan checkpoints in runner.rs | High | M | Tasks 1, 2; gossip-9434, gossip-9437 |
| 4 | Generation-augmented watermarks | Low-Med | S | None |
| 5 | On-disk commit-graph reading for large repos | Medium | M | None |

### Key Architectural Constraints

- **Allocation policy**: HOT paths (per-pack-plan checkpoint writes) must avoid heap allocation. Use existing `ByteSlab`, `InlineVec`, or pre-allocated scratch buffers.
- **Atomicity**: Seen-bitmap deltas and pack-completion bitmaps must be crash-safe. Partial writes must not corrupt the durable state.
- **Compatibility**: Must integrate with existing `PrefixCheckpointAggregator` and `RepoFrontier` checkpoint boundary kind.
- **ConcurrentMaintenance**: Existing two-phase artifact stability checks (`runner.rs:943, 1012`) remain the correctness backstop for concurrent `git gc`.

## Code References

title: Add incremental seen-bitmap persistence during Git scan spiller flush
description:
## Context

For enterprise monorepo scans processing millions of blobs, worker death before finalize currently discards ALL blob dedup progress. The `SeenBitmapDelta` is only assembled and persisted at finalize time via `build_finalize_ops()` in `finalize.rs:392-501`. This means a multi-hour scan that crashes at 95% completion must re-examine every blob from scratch. By persisting the seen-bitmap incrementally after each spiller `flush_batch()`, the system can resume from the last durable checkpoint rather than starting over.

This is sub-task #1 of the mid-scan resumption epic (gossip-9483) and has no dependencies on other sub-tasks. The existing `merge_delta()` infrastructure already supports incremental merging — only the write path needs to call it during the spill stage.

## Current State

The spiller's `flush_batch()` queries the seen store and emits unseen blobs, but never writes back which OIDs it just processed:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:427-456 — flush_batch only reads, never writes
fn flush_batch<S: SeenBlobStore + ?Sized, B: UniqueBlobSink>(
    &self,
    batch: &BatchBuffer,
    stats: &mut SpillStats,
    seen_store: &S,
    sink: &mut B,
) -> Result<(), SpillError> {
    // ...
    let seen_flags = seen_store.batch_check_seen(batch.oids())?;
    // Emits unseen blobs to sink, but never persists the batch's OIDs
    // as newly-seen. Progress is lost if the worker dies.
}
```

The `SeenBitmapDelta` is built only at finalize time, collecting all scanned OIDs in a single pass:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/finalize.rs:491-501 — delta constructed at finalize, not incrementally
if !seen_oids.is_empty() {
    let delta = SeenBitmapDelta::from_canonical_oids(seen_oids)
        .expect("scanned blobs always use a single object format");
    ops_seen.push(WriteOp {
        key: build_seen_scope_key(input.repo_id, &input.policy_hash),
        value: delta.serialize(),
    });
}
```

The `SeenBlobStore` trait is read-only by design — it has no write method:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/seen_store.rs:20-23 — no persist_delta or write method
pub trait SeenBlobStore {
    fn batch_check_seen(&self, oids: &[OidBytes]) -> Result<Vec<bool>, SpillError>;
}
```

Meanwhile, the `RoaringSeenBitmap` already supports incremental merging:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/roaring_seen.rs:386-391 — merge_delta does O(n+m) sorted merge
fn merge_delta(&mut self, delta: &SeenBitmapDelta) -> Result<(), SeenBitmapError> {
    if self.oid_len != delta.oid_len {
        return Err(SeenBitmapError::MixedOidLengths);
    }
    self.merge_positions(delta.oids(), |_| true)
}
```

And RocksDB `WriteBatch` already provides atomic writes in `commit_finalize`:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/persist_rocksdb.rs:170-248 — WriteBatch for atomic commit
let mut batch = WriteBatch::default();
// ... collect ops ...
self.db.write(batch).map_err(|err| PersistError::backend(err.to_string()))?;
```

## Desired State

After `flush_batch()` emits unseen blobs to the `UniqueBlobSink`, the batch's OIDs are also persisted as a `SeenBitmapDelta` to durable storage via a new `SeenBitmapPersister` trait. The spiller calls `persist_seen_delta()` after each successful `flush_batch()`, writing the batch's OIDs atomically to the seen-bitmap scope key. This keeps the in-memory `RoaringSeenStore` and the on-disk bitmap in sync incrementally.

Key behavioral requirements:
- The incremental write persists ONLY the seen-bitmap. It does NOT advance ref watermarks — that remains exclusively a finalize-time operation gated by `FinalizeOutcome::Complete`.
- The batch OIDs fed to `persist_seen_delta()` are already sorted (guaranteed by the spiller's sorted-merge pipeline), so `SeenBitmapDelta::from_canonical_oids()` can be used to avoid re-sorting.
- Finalize still produces its own `SeenBitmapDelta` for completeness, but the on-disk bitmap is already warm from incremental writes, so the finalize merge is near-zero-cost for OIDs already present.
- On crash recovery, a resumed scan loads the partially-warm seen-bitmap from RocksDB and skips already-seen OIDs, saving hours of re-work.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs` | Add `SeenBitmapPersister` parameter to `flush_batch()`, `push_unique()`, `process_chunk_only()`, `process_with_merge()`, and `finalize()`. Call `persist_seen_delta()` after each successful `flush_batch()`. |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/seen_store.rs` | Add a new `SeenBitmapPersister` trait with `fn persist_seen_delta(&self, oids: &[OidBytes]) -> Result<(), SpillError>`. Keep `SeenBlobStore` read-only. |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/persist_rocksdb.rs` | Implement `SeenBitmapPersister` for `RocksDbStore`. The implementation builds a `SeenBitmapDelta::from_canonical_oids()`, merges into the in-memory `RoaringSeenStore`, serializes, and writes via `db.put()` (single-key atomic). |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/persist.rs` | Implement `SeenBitmapPersister` for `InMemoryPersistenceStore` (test double). |

### Patterns to Follow

- **Trait separation**: Keep read (`SeenBlobStore`) and write (`SeenBitmapPersister`) as separate traits. The spiller already takes `S: SeenBlobStore` — add `P: SeenBitmapPersister` as a second generic parameter.
- **No-op persister for tests**: Provide a `NullSeenBitmapPersister` that discards deltas, mirroring the `NeverSeenStore` pattern for tests that don't need persistence.
- **Sorted-OID fast path**: The `BatchBuffer.oids()` returns sorted OIDs (invariant enforced by debug_assert at `spiller.rs:591-594`). Use `SeenBitmapDelta::from_canonical_oids()` to avoid the O(n log n) sort in `from_oids()`.
- **Single-key atomic write**: Each `persist_seen_delta()` call writes one key (`sb\0` + repo_id + policy_hash) via `db.put()`. This is already atomic in RocksDB without needing `WriteBatch`.
- **Watermark isolation**: The `persist_seen_delta()` path must NEVER write to the `rw` (ref watermark) namespace. Only `commit_finalize()` writes watermarks.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `SeenBitmapDelta::from_canonical_oids()` | `roaring_seen.rs:136-152` | Build delta from pre-sorted OIDs without re-sorting |
| `RoaringSeenBitmap::merge_delta()` | `roaring_seen.rs:386-391` | O(n+m) merge of delta into persisted bitmap |
| `RoaringSeenStore::bitmap_mut()` | `roaring_seen.rs:611-613` | Mutable access for in-memory merge |
| `build_seen_scope_key()` | `finalize.rs:248-255` | Consistent scope key construction |
| `RoaringSeenBitmap::serialize()` | `roaring_seen.rs:473-506` | Serialize for RocksDB put |

### Blast Radius

- **Spiller signature change**: `flush_batch()` gains a `persister` parameter. All callers in `process_chunk_only()` and `process_with_merge()` must be updated.
- **`finalize()` signature change**: Adds `P: SeenBitmapPersister` generic parameter alongside existing `S: SeenBlobStore`.
- **Test updates**: All spiller tests must supply a `NullSeenBitmapPersister` (or `InMemoryPersistenceStore`).
- **No wire format changes**: The on-disk `RoaringSeenBitmap` format is unchanged. The delta is the same `SeenBitmapDelta` already used at finalize time.
- **No coordination layer changes**: This is purely within `scanner-git`. The coordination layer's checkpoint infrastructure is not touched.

## Code References

- `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:427-456` — `flush_batch()` where persistence call should be added
- `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:394-418` — `push_unique()` that calls `flush_batch()`
- `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:247-303` — `process_chunk_only()` finalize path
- `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:309-384` — `process_with_merge()` finalize path
- `crates/scanner-git/src/spiller.rs:213-240` — `finalize()` entry point
- `crates/scanner-git/src/roaring_seen.rs:136-152` — `from_canonical_oids()` sorted fast path
- `crates/scanner-git/src/roaring_seen.rs:386-391` — `merge_delta()` incremental merge
- `crates/scanner-git/src/roaring_seen.rs:592-621` — `RoaringSeenStore` wrapping `SeenBlobStore`
- `crates/scanner-git/src/persist_rocksdb.rs:170-248` — `commit_finalize()` WriteBatch pattern
- `crates/scanner-git/src/persist_rocksdb.rs:260-288` — `batch_check_seen()` on RocksDbStore
- `crates/scanner-git/src/finalize.rs:491-501` — current finalize-only delta construction
- `crates/scanner-git/src/finalize.rs:248-255` — `build_seen_scope_key()` key builder
- `crates/scanner-git/src/seen_store.rs:20-23` — `SeenBlobStore` trait (read-only)
- `crates/scanner-git/src/spill_limits.rs:22-23` — `seen_batch_max_oids: 8_192` default batch size

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9483 | Git scan mid-scan resumption and checkpoint recovery | parent epic — this is sub-task #1 |
| gossip-9456 | Migrate seen-blob store from per-OID RocksDB keys to single serialized Roaring bitmap | predecessor — established the Roaring bitmap infrastructure this task extends |
| gossip-9437 | Implement inner Git persistence adapters and a repo-family durable receipt | sibling — extends the same persistence seam; coordinate trait placement |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New `SeenBitmapPersister` trait defined in `seen_store.rs` with `fn persist_seen_delta(&self, oids: &[OidBytes]) -> Result<(), SpillError>`
- [ ] `NullSeenBitmapPersister` provided for tests (discards deltas, no I/O)
- [ ] `RocksDbStore` implements `SeenBitmapPersister` — merges delta into in-memory bitmap and persists via `db.put()`
- [ ] `InMemoryPersistenceStore` implements `SeenBitmapPersister` for test doubles
- [ ] `Spiller::flush_batch()` calls `persist_seen_delta()` after emitting unseen blobs

- [ ] Unit test: spiller with `InMemoryPersistenceStore` verifies bitmap grows incrementally across flush batches
- [ ] Unit test: seen-bitmap persisted after flush_batch is queryable by `batch_check_seen()` on next batch
- [ ] Integration test (rocksdb feature): `RocksDbStore` incremental persist survives reopen — OIDs written mid-spill are still seen after store reload
- [ ] Finalize still produces correct results — incremental persistence is additive, not replacing finalize delta
