title: FindingsCaptureSink refactor: perf, safety, capacity
description:
## Context

Step 4 of the done-ledger Bloom filter epic (gossip-9550). With the `DoneLedgerBloomFilter` wrapper (gossip-9550.2) and `list_done_hashes` method (gossip-9550.3) in place, this task wires filter construction into the shard claim lifecycle. The filter is built once (COLD-tier) after the scan engine is constructed and before the page loop begins.

The done-ledger is a monotonic lattice, so a filter built at claim time may miss items committed by other workers after construction. This is safe — it only causes extra database lookups, never incorrect results. The filter is represented as `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` for transparent degradation when construction is skipped (below threshold) or fails.

## Current State

`scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine()` at `distributed.rs:1823-1831` takes a done-ledger reference and passes it to the page loop. The page loop calls `prefilter_done_ledger()` at `distributed.rs:1954` which issues `batch_get()` on every page. No filter exists.

```rust
// distributed.rs:1823-1831 — current function signature
fn scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine<D>(
    lease: &ShardLease,
    config: &FsScanConfig,
    done_ledger: &D,
    engine: Arc<scanner_engine::Engine>,
    out: &dyn EventOutput,
    commit: &ReceiptCommitSink,
    cancel: &CancellationToken,
) -> Result<OrderedSourceAssignmentOutcome, ScanRuntimeError>
```

## Desired State

After engine construction in the shard scan setup path, call `list_done_hashes()` to bulk-load OvidHash keys and construct a `DoneLedgerBloomFilter`. Pass the resulting `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` through to the page loop function.

```rust
// After engine build, before entering the page loop:
let bloom_filter = {
    let hashes = done_ledger
        .list_done_hashes(
            lease.write_context().tenant_id(),
            lease.write_context().policy_hash(),
        )
        .map_err(|e| ScanRuntimeError::Driver(
            anyhow::Error::new(e).context("bloom filter key enumeration failed")
        ))?;
    match DoneLedgerBloomFilter::new(hashes.len()) {
        Some(mut filter) => {
            for h in &hashes {
                filter.insert(h);
            }
            tracing::info!(
                shard_id = %lease.shard_id(),
                items = hashes.len(),
                memory_bytes = filter.memory_bytes(),
                "done-ledger bloom filter constructed",
            );
            Some(filter)
        }
        None => {
            tracing::debug!(
                shard_id = %lease.shard_id(),
                done_ledger_size = hashes.len(),
                "done-ledger bloom filter skipped (below threshold or exceeds memory cap)",
            );
            None
        }
    }
};
```

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Add filter construction after engine build; add `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` parameter to `scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine` | Wire filter into scan lifecycle |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Pass `bloom_filter.as_ref()` to prefilter call sites | Thread filter to page loop |

### Patterns to Follow

| Pattern | Reference | Apply to |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Structured logging at lifecycle boundaries | `distributed.rs` tracing calls at shard claim/complete | Filter construction logging |
| Error context wrapping | `distributed.rs:368-372` (anyhow context) | list_done_hashes error wrapping |
| Option-based feature gating | Common Rust pattern | `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` |

### Allocation Tier Classification

- `list_done_hashes()` call: COLD (once per shard claim)
- `DoneLedgerBloomFilter::new()`: COLD (single heap allocation)
- `filter.insert()` in construction loop: COLD (bit-flipping, no allocation)
- Filter storage: COLD (lives for shard lifetime)

## Code References

```rust

    lease: &ShardLease,
    config: &FsScanConfig,
    done_ledger: &D,

    out: &dyn EventOutput,

// persistence/write_context.rs:24-29 — WriteContext carries scope

    tenant_id: TenantId,
    policy_hash: PolicyHash,

}
```

| gossip-9550 | In-memory Bloom filter acceleration layer | Parent epic |
| gossip-9550.2 | DoneLedgerBloomFilter wrapper | Blocked by — provides the filter type |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Filter is `None` when below threshold, above memory cap, or on enumeration error
- [ ] Structured tracing: `info` when filter is constructed (with item count and memory), `debug` when skipped
- [ ] `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` passed to page loop function

description:
## Context

Step 6 of the done-ledger Bloom filter epic (gossip-9550). After Step 5 integrates the filter into `prefilter_done_ledger()`, the filter only contains keys loaded at shard claim time. Items committed during the current scan (page N marks item X as done) are not in the filter, so if item X reappears in a later page (e.g., re-enumerated due to cursor mechanics), the filter cannot catch it and a redundant `batch_get()` occurs.

This task closes that gap by feeding newly-committed OvidHash keys back into the filter between page iterations. Since the page loop is single-threaded and processes pages sequentially, committed keys from page N can be inserted into the filter before page N+1 is prefiltered.

## Current State

The page loop in `scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine()` (`distributed.rs:1823-2047`) processes pages sequentially:
1. `source.enumerate_page()` → get items
2. `page.prefilter_done_ledger()` → classify against done-ledger
3. Execute scan misses → produce findings + done-ledger records
4. Commit via `ReceiptCommitSink` → durably write done-ledger records
5. Loop to next page

The commit pipeline (`commit_pipeline.rs`) runs on a dedicated thread and produces `ItemCommitReceipt` values that flow back through a channel. The page loop drains committed receipts after each page.

No mechanism currently feeds committed OvidHash keys back to any in-memory structure.

## Desired State

After draining the commit outcome channel for the previous page's results (between pages), insert the committed items' OvidHash keys into the Bloom filter:

```rust
// In the page loop, after processing commit outcomes from previous page:
if let Some(ref mut bloom) = bloom_filter {
    for committed_ovid in &newly_committed_ovid_hashes {
        bloom.insert(committed_ovid);
    }
}
```

The `insert()` call is allocation-free (HOT-tier safe) — it only flips bits in the existing filter array.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | After commit drain, insert committed OvidHashes into bloom filter | Close the feedback loop |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs` | Expose committed OvidHash keys from commit receipts (if not already exposed) | Provide the data to insert |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_pipeline.rs` | Ensure committed OvidHash keys are available in the drain result (if not already) | Pipeline output for feedback |

### Design Considerations

The committed OvidHash keys must be available at the point where the page loop drains commit outcomes. Two approaches:

1. **Capture at commit submission**: When the `ReceiptCommitSink` submits done-ledger records, save the OvidHash keys in a side buffer. After drain, use the buffer to update the filter.

2. **Extract from commit receipts**: If `ItemCommitReceipt` or `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt` carries the committed OvidHash, extract during drain.

Approach 1 is simpler because the OvidHash is already available at submission time (derived in the scan miss execution path).

### Allocation Tier

- `bloom.insert()`: HOT-tier safe (allocation-free bit-flipping)
- Collecting committed OvidHash keys: WARM-tier (temporary Vec per page, freed after insertion)
- This happens between pages, not per-item, so the temporary collection is acceptable

## Code References

```rust
// The page loop processes pages sequentially and drains commits:
// distributed.rs — simplified page loop structure:
loop {
    let page = source.enumerate_page(..)?;
    let filtered = page.prefilter_done_ledger(write_context, done_ledger, bloom.as_ref())?;
    let scan_result = execute_scan_misses(..)?;
    commit.submit(scan_result)?;
    // ... drain commit outcomes here ...
    // NEW: insert committed OvidHashes into bloom filter
}

// DoneLedgerBloomFilter::insert is allocation-free
pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, hash: &OvidHash) { .. }
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|--------------|
| gossip-9550 | In-memory Bloom filter acceleration layer | Parent epic |
| gossip-9550.2 | DoneLedgerBloomFilter wrapper | Blocked by — provides insert() method |
| gossip-9550.5 | Integrate filter into prefilter_done_ledger | Blocked by — filter must be wired into prefilter first |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Committed OvidHash keys are inserted into the Bloom filter between page iterations
- [ ] Items committed in page N are caught by the filter in page N+1 (no redundant DB lookup)
- [ ] `bloom.insert()` calls are allocation-free (no heap allocation per insert)
- [ ] When bloom is None, the feedback path is a no-op (zero overhead)
- [ ] New test: commit item in page 1 → verify filter catches it in page 2 without DB call
- [ ] Existing distributed runtime tests pass unchanged
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- Page loop: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` (scan_ordered_filesystem_lease_with_engine)
- Commit pipeline: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_pipeline.rs`
- Result committer: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs`
- DoneLedgerBloomFilter::insert: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/done_ledger_bloom.rs`

## Implementation Guidance Addendum

### fastbloom API (MUST — 98%)

Use raw-hash API directly — no custom `BuildHasher` needed:
```rust
#[inline]
fn ovid_to_u64(hash: &OvidHash) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes(hash.as_bytes()[..8].try_into().expect("8 bytes from 32"))
}
// In maybe_contains: self.inner.contains_hash(ovid_to_u64(hash))
// In insert: self.inner.insert_hash(ovid_to_u64(hash))
```

### Construction (MUST — 95%)

Use builder: `BloomFilter::with_false_pos(0.01).expected_items(n)` — computes optimal bits and hash count automatically. Do NOT hardcode "10 bits/key" or calculate manually.

### Memory cap (MUST — 95%)

After construction, check `filter.as_slice().len() * 8 > MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` and return `None` if exceeded. Alternatively, pre-compute: `optimal_size(n, 0.01) / 8 <= 32 * 1024 * 1024`. At 1% FPR, ~26.8M items = ~30.7 MB.

### `is_terminal()` (MUST — 99%)

Use exhaustive match (not negation) so the const exhaustiveness guard catches new variants:
```rust
#[inline]
#[must_use]
pub const fn is_terminal(self) -> bool {
    match self {
        Self::FailedPermanent | Self::Skipped
        | Self::ScannedClean | Self::ScannedWithFindings => true,
        Self::FailedRetryable => false,
    }
}
```
Document distinction from `ShardStatus::is_terminal()` in coordination crate — both use "terminal" but with different semantics (done-ledger = "no rescan needed"; shard = "no further transitions").

- Rename `item_count()` to `len()` per Rust conventions

## Implementation Guidance Addendum

### Chunk Partitioning (MUST — 95%)

Drop the `Vec<bool>` is_positive approach. Instead, compute bloom negatives inline:
```rust
// For each chunk, reuse the already-computed ovid_hashes Vec
let mut positive_hashes: Vec<OvidHash> = Vec::new();
let mut positive_indices: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
for (i, ovid) in ovid_hashes.iter().enumerate() {
    if bloom.as_ref().is_none_or(|b| b.maybe_contains(ovid)) {
        positive_indices.push(i);
        positive_hashes.push(*ovid);
    }
}
// batch_get only positives (skip entirely if empty)
let batch = if positive_hashes.is_empty() {
    Vec::new()
} else {
    done_ledger.batch_get(tenant_id, policy_hash, &positive_hashes)?
};
// Walk original chunk order
let mut batch_idx = 0;
for (i, (item, ovid)) in chunk.into_iter().zip(ovid_hashes.iter()).enumerate() {
    let disposition = if positive_indices.get(batch_idx) == Some(&i) {
        let d = classify_record(batch[batch_idx]);
        batch_idx += 1;
        d
    } else {
        OrderedContentPrefilterDisposition::ScanMiss
    };
    classified.push(OrderedContentClassifiedItem::new(item, disposition));
}
```

### Reuse `ovid_hashes` (MUST — 99%)

The existing code at `ordered_content.rs:357-365` already computes `ovid_hashes: Vec<_>` per chunk. The bloom check MUST operate on these already-derived hashes — do NOT call `derive_ovid_hash` a second time (each call clones a cached Hasher and runs `write_canonical` + `finalize`).

### Filter Placement (MUST — 95%)

Construct `Option<DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` inside `run_filesystem_lease` (distributed.rs ~line 2587), between engine build and the scan call. Pass `bloom.as_mut()` as `Option<&mut DoneLedgerBloomFilter>` into the page loop chain so the feedback insertions can mutate it. The bloom lives on the stack frame for the shard lifetime.

### Committed-key Feedback (SHOULD — 85%)

The page loop is single-threaded per shard (verified: `workers = 1` enforced). `&mut` access to the bloom within the loop scope is safe. Feed back committed OvidHash keys between pages using `bloom.insert()` — bit-flipping only, allocation-free.

### bloom=None Passthrough (MUST — 95%)

When `bloom` is `None`, the method MUST behave identically to the current implementation — all items go to `batch_get`. Use `bloom.as_ref().is_none_or(|b| b.maybe_contains(ovid))` which evaluates to `true` when bloom is None, sending all items through.

---

## Testing Strategy

### Existing Tests (must pass unchanged)

All 8 prefilter tests at `ordered_content.rs:3408-3731` must pass after signature change. They serve as "no-filter equivalence" regression anchors. Update call sites to pass `None` for bloom parameter.

### New Tests

**Unit tests (ordered_content.rs mod tests)**:

7. `prefilter_bloom_chunking_with_filter` — SHOULD, 85%

8. `prefilter_bloom_none_matches_original_behavior` — MUST, 95%

Add norm_hash to FindingEvent and OwnedCoreEvent::Finding for Git finding persistence
description:
## Context

The Git distributed worker path captures finding events during scan execution via `FindingsCaptureSink`, but the `FindingEvent` and `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` types omit `norm_hash` — the BLAKE3 digest of the normalized secret content. This is the root of the entire 3-tier persistence identity chain (`NormHash → SecretHash → FindingId → OccurrenceId → ObservationId`). Without it, Git findings cannot be translated into durable persistence records and are permanently lost.

The filesystem path correctly carries `norm_hash` through `FsFindingRecord` (which has a `norm_hash: NormHash` field). The Git path routes through `FindingEvent → OwnedCoreEvent::Finding`, which was designed as a telemetry-oriented type and intentionally omits `norm_hash`. The hash IS computed at scan time and IS available at the emission site — it is simply not forwarded.

## Current State

`FindingEvent<'a>` (events.rs:26-37) has no `norm_hash` field:

```rust
// crates/scanner-scheduler/src/events.rs:26-37
pub struct FindingEvent<'a> {
    pub source: SourceKind,
    pub object_path: &'a [u8],
    pub start: u64,
    pub end: u64,
    pub rule_id: u32,
    pub rule_name: &'a str,
    pub commit_id: Option<u32>,
    pub change_kind: Option<&'a str>,
    pub confidence_score: i8,
}
```

`OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` (lib.rs:1620-1636) mirrors the same field set with no `norm_hash`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:1620-1636
pub enum OwnedCoreEvent {
    Finding {
        source: SourceKind,
        object_path: Vec<u8>,
        start: u64,
        end: u64,
        rule_id: u32,
        rule_name: String,
        commit_id: Option<u32>,
        change_kind: Option<String>,
        confidence_score: i8,
    },
    // ...
}
```

The `norm_hash` exists in `ScoredFinding.key.norm_hash` at the emission point but is dropped:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/engine_adapter.rs:553-564
for f in &self.findings_buf {
    self.event_sink.emit(ScanEvent::Finding(FindingEvent {
        source: SourceKind::Git,
        object_path: path,
        start: u64::from(f.key.start),
        end: u64::from(f.key.end),
        rule_id: f.key.rule_id,
        rule_name: self.engine.rule_name(f.key.rule_id),
        commit_id: Some(commit_id),
        change_kind: Some(change_kind),
        confidence_score: f.confidence_score,
        // f.key.norm_hash is available here but NOT forwarded
    }));
}
```

## Desired State

`FindingEvent<'a>` and `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` carry `norm_hash: Option<[u8; 32]>`. The Git emission path populates this field from `ScoredFinding.key.norm_hash`. The generic FS emission path (`scan_helpers::emit_findings`) sets it to `None` (the `FindingRecord` trait has no `norm_hash()` method). The ordered-content FS path (`distributed.rs`) sets it to `Some(finding.norm_hash)` since `FsFindingRecord` carries the hash. `FindingsCaptureSink` captures the hash along with the other finding fields for downstream translation.

## Implementation Guidance

### Type Decision

Use `pub norm_hash: Option<[u8; 32]>` on both `FindingEvent` and `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding`. Do not import `NormHash` from `gossip-contracts` or `scanner-engine` — the scanner-engine `NormHash` is a bare type alias (no type safety), and `gossip-contracts::NormHash` would create cross-crate coupling that does not exist today. Redacted Debug is handled via manual `Debug` impl, not via the newtype.

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/events.rs` | Add `pub norm_hash: Option<[u8; 32]>` to `FindingEvent<'a>` | Core struct change |
| `crates/scanner-git/src/engine_adapter.rs` | Populate `norm_hash: Some(f.key.norm_hash)` at ~line 558 in `stream_findings` | Bridge from arena-stored finding identity to event pipeline |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Add `norm_hash: Option<[u8; 32]>` to `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` variant, update `from_core`, `emit_into`, and manual `PartialEq` impl | Owned conversion must propagate the new field through all paths |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Set `norm_hash: Some(finding.norm_hash)` in `emit_ordered_item_findings` (~line 1429) | `FsFindingRecord` carries `norm_hash` — do not discard available data |
| `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/scheduler/scan_helpers.rs` | Set `norm_hash: None` in `emit_findings` | Generic `FindingRecord` trait has no `norm_hash()` method; persistence captures it separately |
| `crates/gossip-worker/src/recorder.rs` | Bind and drop `norm_hash` in `from_core_event` destructure (use `_norm_hash` or `..`) | Do NOT add to `SanitizedCoordinationRecord` — secret-derived digest must not appear in telemetry |

### Construction Site Inventory (17 sites)

**FindingEvent construction (14 sites):**

| Site | File | Value |
|------|------|-------|
| Git HOT path | `engine_adapter.rs:~553` | `Some(f.key.norm_hash)` |
| Ordered-content FS | `distributed.rs:~1429` | `Some(finding.norm_hash)` |
| Generic FS emit | `scan_helpers.rs:~140` | `None` |
| Test: VecEventOutput | `events.rs:~338` | `None` |
| Test: finding_event() | `coordination_sink.rs:~268` | `Some([0xAA; 32])` or `None` |
| Test: round-trip | `lib_tests.rs:~1080` | `Some(...)` and `None` |
| Tests: event_sink.rs | 7 sites (~589-756) | `None` |

**OwnedCoreEvent::Finding construction (3 sites):**

| Site | File |
|------|------|
| Variant definition | `lib.rs:~1641` |
| `from_core` | `lib.rs:~1682` |
| Test constructors | `recorder.rs:~841, ~1197` |

**Destructuring sites (4):**

| Site | File | Action |
|------|------|--------|
| `from_core` | `lib.rs:~1680` | Extract `norm_hash` from `FindingEvent` |
| `emit_into` | `lib.rs:~1721` | Pass through to emitted `FindingEvent` |
| `PartialEq` | `lib.rs:~1781` | Include in equality comparison |
| `from_core_event` | `recorder.rs:~584` | Bind and drop — do NOT forward |

### JSON Serialization — Three Paths, All Skip norm_hash

Do NOT serialize `norm_hash` in any JSON/JSONL output. It is a cryptographic digest of secret content — writing it to event logs creates a lookup oracle.

1. **`VecEventOutput`** in `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/events.rs:153-187` — skip
2. **`VecEventSink`** in `crates/scanner-git/src/events.rs:131-166` — skip
3. **`encode_core_event`** in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/event_sink.rs:314-354` — skip

At each path, add an inline comment: `// norm_hash intentionally omitted — secret-derived digest must not appear in event logs.`

### Debug Redaction

Add a manual `Debug` impl for `FindingEvent` that prints `norm_hash: [redacted]` when `Some`, `norm_hash: None` when `None`. Follow the pattern in `commit_sink.rs:48-57`.

For `OwnedCoreEvent`, ensure the existing `Debug` derive or manual impl handles `norm_hash` with redaction. The `#[derive(Debug)]` on `OwnedCoreEvent` will print raw bytes — replace with manual impl for the `Finding` variant.

### Patterns to Follow

- `FsFindingRecord.norm_hash` field (scanner-scheduler/src/store.rs:41-56) — exemplary per-field documentation
- `commit_sink::FindingRecord` Debug impl (commit_sink.rs:48-57) — redacted Debug pattern
- `NormHash::from_digest([u8; 32])` at result_translation.rs:385 — conversion at the persistence boundary (downstream task)
- `commit_id: Option<u32>`, `change_kind: Option<&str>` on FindingEvent — existing source-conditional Option pattern

### Anti-Patterns — Do NOT

- Import `NormHash` from `gossip-contracts` or `scanner-engine` into these crates
- Serialize `norm_hash` to any JSON/JSONL output
- Add `norm_hash` to `SanitizedCoordinationRecord` in any form (not even `RedactedDigest`)
- Set `norm_hash: None` in `distributed.rs` ordered-content path (data IS available)
- Create an `emit_findings_with_hash` variant in scan_helpers
- Use `[0u8; 32]` as a sentinel for "absent" — zero hash is a valid BLAKE3 output

### Blast Radius

All construction sites of `FindingEvent` and `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` listed above. The compiler will catch missing fields — non-exhaustive struct patterns ensure compile-time safety.

### Security Note

`norm_hash` is a BLAKE3 digest of the normalized secret — it does NOT contain the raw secret but is still security-sensitive (reversible with brute force for low-entropy secrets). Ensure:
- Manual `Debug` impl redacts `norm_hash` (do not use `#[derive(Debug)]`)
- All 3 JSONL encoders skip `norm_hash` entirely
- `SanitizedCoordinationRecord::from_core_event` drops the field silently
- `TextEventSink` verbose output does not include `norm_hash`

## Code References

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/engine_adapter.rs:140-152 — FindingKey with norm_hash
pub struct FindingKey {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
    pub rule_id: u32,
    pub norm_hash: NormHash,
}
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-scheduler/src/store.rs:41-53 — FsFindingRecord with norm_hash
pub struct FsFindingRecord {
    pub rule_id: u32,
    pub root_hint_start: u64,
    pub root_hint_end: u64,
    pub span_start: u64,
    pub span_end: u64,
    pub norm_hash: NormHash,
    pub confidence_score: i8,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_translation.rs:385 — NormHash conversion
let norm_hash = NormHash::from_digest(finding.norm_hash);
let secret_hash = key_secret_hash(tenant_secret_key, &norm_hash);
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:48-57 — Redacted Debug pattern
impl fmt::Debug for FindingRecord {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("FindingRecord")
            // ... fields ...
            .field("norm_hash", &"[redacted]")
            .finish()
    }
}
```

## Testing Strategy

### MUST Tests (6)

**1. `test_finding_event_norm_hash_round_trips_through_owned`** (unit)
Location: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs`
Property: `norm_hash: Some([0xAB; 32])` survives `from_core → OwnedCoreEvent → emit_into → FindingEvent`.
```rust
let event = FindingEvent { norm_hash: Some([0xAB; 32]), ..base_finding() };
let owned = OwnedCoreEvent::from_core(CoreEvent::Finding(event));
// emit_into and assert norm_hash == Some([0xAB; 32])
```

**2. `test_finding_event_norm_hash_none_round_trips`** (unit)
Location: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs`
Property: `norm_hash: None` preserved through round-trip. FS findings must not fabricate a hash.

**3. `test_git_finding_emits_norm_hash_from_scored_finding`** (unit)
Location: `crates/scanner-git/src/engine_adapter_tests.rs`
Property: Emitted `FindingEvent.norm_hash` equals `ScoredFinding.key.norm_hash`. Critical data-flow link.

**4. `test_vec_event_output_omits_norm_hash_in_json`** (unit)
Location: `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/events.rs:mod tests`
Property: JSON output from `VecEventOutput` does NOT contain `"norm_hash"` key, regardless of field value.

**5. `test_owned_core_event_partial_eq_includes_norm_hash`** (unit)
Location: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib_tests.rs`
Property: Two `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` values differing only in `norm_hash` are NOT equal.

**6. `test_sanitized_record_drops_norm_hash`** (unit)
Location: `crates/gossip-worker/src/recorder.rs`
Property: `SanitizedCoordinationRecord::from_core_event` produces a record with no norm_hash field and Debug output contains no hash bytes.

### SHOULD Tests (3)

**7. `test_findings_capture_sink_forwards_norm_hash`** (unit)

**8. `test_fs_emit_findings_sets_norm_hash_none`** (unit)

**9. `test_jsonl_sink_norm_hash_omitted`** (rstest, parameterized over Some/None)

### Do NOT Test (Already Covered)

title: Capture commit_id to commit_oid mapping in FindingsCaptureSink for Git finding identity
description:
## Context

The Git finding translation pipeline (see gossip-9579) needs to derive `ObjectVersionId` for each finding's `OccurrenceRecord`. The `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` carries `commit_id: Option<u32>`, which is a commit-graph ordinal (positional index from traversal order), NOT a stable identifier. The actual commit OID lives in `CommitMetaEvent.commit_oid` events emitted alongside findings.

To resolve ordinals to stable OIDs, the capture layer must build a lookup table from `CommitMetaEvent` events during the scan. Without this mapping, Git findings cannot derive deterministic `ObjectVersionId` values, and the identity chain breaks on re-scan (ordinals change when the commit graph changes).

## Current State

`FindingsCaptureSink` (coordination_sink.rs:175-197) only counts `Finding` events via `AtomicU64`. It receives `GitEvent` via its `GitEventOutput` impl but forwards them directly to the inner sink without capturing any data:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/coordination_sink.rs:216-219
impl GitEventOutput for FindingsCaptureSink {
    fn emit_git(&self, event: GitEvent<'_>) {
        self.inner.emit_git(event);
    }
}
```

`CommitMetaEvent` (scanner-git/src/events.rs:13-23) carries the actual commit OID:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/events.rs:13-23
pub struct CommitMetaEvent {
    pub commit_id: u32,           // ordinal (same as FindingEvent::commit_id)
    pub commit_oid: OidBytes,     // actual SHA-1 or SHA-256
    pub timestamp: u64,
    pub identity: Option<CommitIdentityIds>,
}
```

The ordinal-to-OID relationship is established in `engine_adapter.rs:533-543` where `CommitMetaEvent` is emitted before its associated findings:

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/engine_adapter.rs:533-543
if self.commit_meta_seen.test_and_set(commit_id as usize) {
    let oid = self.commit_graph.commit_oid(Position(commit_id));
    self.event_sink.emit(ScanEvent::CommitMeta(CommitMetaEvent {
        commit_id,
        commit_oid: oid,
        // ...
    }));
}
```

## Desired State

`FindingsCaptureSink` intercepts `GitEvent::CommitMeta` events to build a `commit_id → OidBytes` lookup table. After scan completion, callers retrieve this map alongside captured findings via a new accessor. The map is used by the downstream translation function (separate task) to resolve `commit_id` ordinals to stable commit OIDs for `ObjectVersionId` derivation.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/coordination_sink.rs` | Add `commit_oid_map: Mutex<HashMap<u32, OidBytes>>` field to `FindingsCaptureSink`; intercept `CommitMeta` in `emit_git`; add `drain_commit_oid_map()` accessor | Captures ordinal-to-OID mapping for downstream translation. |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Call `drain_commit_oid_map()` alongside `detected_finding_count()` at ~line 3038; pass map to the persistence function | Wires the captured map into the translation path. |

### Patterns to Follow

Follow the existing `detected_finding_count` pattern (coordination_sink.rs:189-196):
- `Mutex<HashMap<u32, OidBytes>>` with poisoning recovery via `unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())`
- `drain_commit_oid_map` takes `&self`, returns the map via `std::mem::take`
- Matches the `VecEventSink::take` pattern at `scanner-git/src/events.rs:122-124`

### Utilities to Reuse

- `OidBytes` type from `scanner-git/src/events.rs` (re-exported at `scanner-git/src/lib.rs:264`) — the commit OID representation
- `GitEvent` enum from `scanner-git/src/events.rs` — for matching `CommitMeta` variant
- Mutex poisoning recovery pattern established at `distributed.rs:861,875`

### Blast Radius

- `FindingsCaptureSink::new` needs an updated constructor (no new parameters — the map is initialized empty)
- `run_git_repo_lease` in distributed.rs calls `detected_finding_count()` — needs updated to also call `drain_commit_oid_map()`
- Test helpers constructing `FindingsCaptureSink` are unaffected (new field is initialized internally)

### Design Note

`CommitMetaEvent` is emitted at most once per commit (guarded by `commit_meta_seen` bitset in engine_adapter.rs:533). The map will contain at most one entry per unique commit in the scan, bounded by `max_items` (configured scan budget). Memory overhead is small: ~36 bytes per entry (4 bytes key + 32 bytes OID).

### Allocation Tier & Data Structure (WARM)

`FindingsCaptureSink` is a per-repo-lease wrapper created once per claimed shard (`distributed.rs:2954`), NOT an inner-loop component. The drain point at ~line 3038 is post-scan, single-threaded after `thread::scope` join. **WARM-tier policy applies: optimize for simplicity.**

- **`HashMap<u32, OidBytes>`** is correct. A `Vec<Option<OidBytes>>` indexed by `commit_id` is rejected — it would require allocating for the full commit-graph size (potentially millions of entries) while only a fraction of commits have findings. Map cardinality equals the number of distinct commits with findings, typically well under 1,000 per scan.
- **`std::sync::Mutex`** (not `DashMap` or `parking_lot::Mutex`). The crate uses `std::sync::Mutex` throughout. `CommitMeta` events are gated by `AtomicBitSet::test_and_set` upstream, so contention is near-zero.
- **No `with_capacity`** — cardinality is unknown at construction time. WARM-tier: simplicity first.

### `emit_git` Interception Pattern

Extract Copy fields (`commit_id: u32`, `commit_oid: OidBytes`) via `ref meta` before forwarding. **Critical: drop Mutex guard before `inner.emit_git(event)` to minimize hold time and avoid holding the lock across a potentially blocking downstream call.**

```rust
impl GitEventOutput for FindingsCaptureSink {
    fn emit_git(&self, event: GitEvent<'_>) {
        if let GitEvent::CommitMeta(ref meta) = event {
            self.commit_oid_map
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
                .insert(meta.commit_id, meta.commit_oid);
        }
        // Guard dropped here before forwarding.
        self.inner.emit_git(event);
    }
}
```

### `drain_commit_oid_map` Accessor

Return owned `HashMap<u32, OidBytes>` via `std::mem::take`. The caller invokes this after worker join, so no concurrent access.

```rust
pub(crate) fn drain_commit_oid_map(&self) -> HashMap<u32, OidBytes> {
    std::mem::take(
        &mut *self
            .commit_oid_map
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()),
    )
}
```

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

| Anti-Pattern | Why | What to Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| `Vec<Option<OidBytes>>` indexed by `commit_id` | Wastes memory for full commit-graph size; only finding-bearing commits matter | `HashMap<u32, OidBytes>` — sparse, sized to actual cardinality |
| `DashMap` or `RwLock` | Overkill for WARM tier with near-zero contention | `std::sync::Mutex` — simpler, consistent with crate |
| Holding Mutex guard across `inner.emit_git()` | Risks deadlock or unnecessary blocking | Drop guard before forwarding |
| `parking_lot::Mutex` | Inconsistent with crate convention | `std::sync::Mutex` |

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/coordination_sink.rs:175-197 — FindingsCaptureSink struct
pub(crate) struct FindingsCaptureSink {
    inner: Arc<CoordinationEventSink>,
    finding_count: AtomicU64,
}
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/events.rs:1-11 — GitEvent enum
pub enum GitEvent<'a> {
    CommitMeta(CommitMetaEvent),
    // ...
}
```

## Testing Strategy

**10 tests. All reuse existing `make_sink_and_recorder()` infrastructure. No new dependencies required.**

### MUST Tests (6)

1. **`test_commit_oid_map_captures_commit_meta_events`** — Unit. Emit one `GitEvent::CommitMeta`, drain map, assert single entry with correct key/value.
```rust
#[test]
fn commit_oid_map_captures_commit_meta_events() {
    let (sink, _recorder) = make_sink_and_recorder();
    let oid = scanner_git::OidBytes::sha1([0xab; 20]);
    sink.emit_git(GitEvent::CommitMeta(scanner_git::CommitMetaEvent {
        commit_id: 42, commit_oid: oid, timestamp: 1_700_000_000, identity: None,
    }));
    let map = sink.drain_commit_oid_map();
    assert_eq!(map.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(map[&42], oid);
}
```

2. **`test_commit_oid_map_multiple_distinct_commits`** — Unit. Emit 5 distinct `CommitMeta` events, drain, assert `map.len() == 5` and all entries correct.

3. **`test_commit_oid_map_ignores_non_commit_meta_events`** — Unit. Emit `IdentityDictionary` and `Finding` events only. Drain map, assert empty.

4. **`test_commit_oid_map_still_forwards_to_inner`** — Unit. Emit `CommitMeta`, verify both map populated AND inner sink received the event. Capture is additive.

5. **`test_drain_commit_oid_map_clears_map`** — Unit. Populate map, drain once (assert non-empty), drain again (assert empty). Validates `std::mem::take` semantics.

6. **`test_commit_oid_map_interleaved_with_finding_count`** — Unit. Interleave `CommitMeta` and `Finding` events. Assert both `detected_finding_count()` and `drain_commit_oid_map()` return correct independent results.

### SHOULD Tests (4)

7. **`test_commit_oid_map_last_write_wins_for_duplicate_commit_id`** — Unit. Defensive: emit two `CommitMeta` with same `commit_id` but different OIDs. Assert second OID wins. Documents HashMap insert semantics.

8. **`test_commit_oid_map_with_sha256_oids`** — Unit. Use 32-byte OID. Assert stored correctly. Format-agnostic validation.

9. **`test_commit_oid_map_empty_when_no_commit_meta_events`** — Unit. Emit only `Finding` events. Drain, assert empty. Baseline sanity.

10. **`proptest: commit_oid_map_preserves_all_unique_commit_ids`** — Property. Generate unique `(commit_id, OidBytes)` pairs, emit as `CommitMeta`, drain, assert `map.len() == input.len()`.

### Do NOT Test (Already Covered Upstream)

| Behavior | Covered By | Location |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| CommitMeta emitted at-most-once per commit_id | engine_adapter_tests | scanner-git/src/engine_adapter_tests.rs:1086 |
| CommitMeta carries correct OID and timestamp | engine_adapter_tests | scanner-git/src/engine_adapter_tests.rs:1175 |
| Finding counter increment logic | existing coordination_sink tests | coordination_sink.rs:298-354 |
| CommitMeta-to-StoredGitEvent transformation | existing coordination_sink tests | coordination_sink.rs:356-375 |

## Documentation Requirements

### MUST (5 items)

1. **`FindingsCaptureSink` type-level doc update** (coordination_sink.rs:164-174) — Rewrite to describe dual capture role: finding count via `AtomicU64` AND commit-OID map via `Mutex<HashMap>`. State the invariant that both captures are additive (events always forwarded to inner sink). Mention the call-after-join contract. Pattern: extend existing doc at lines 164-174.

2. **`commit_oid_map` field doc** — Document purpose (maps commit-graph ordinals to stable OID bytes), population source (`GitEvent::CommitMeta`), and sync strategy (`std::sync::Mutex`; low contention due to upstream `AtomicBitSet` dedup).

3. **`drain_commit_oid_map()` function doc** — Document: returns owned map and leaves internal map empty (`std::mem::take`); must be called after worker join (single-threaded context); uses poisoning recovery; return type `HashMap<u32, OidBytes>`. Pattern: `detected_finding_count` doc at lines 189-196.

4. **`emit_git` inline comment** — Explain why only `CommitMeta` is intercepted and that the guard is dropped before forwarding. Keep to 2-3 lines. Pattern: `emit_core` inline comment at lines 200-208.

5. **Call-site doc in `distributed.rs`** (~line 3038) — Comment explaining why OID map is drained here, where it flows downstream. Update the TODO at lines 2782-2785 since OID map is now available.

### SHOULD (1 item)

6. **Module-level doc update** (coordination_sink.rs:1-7) — Add one sentence mentioning that the capture layer also builds a commit-OID lookup for finding translation.

### Doc Quality Checklist

- [ ] `FindingsCaptureSink` type doc covers dual capture role
- [ ] `commit_oid_map` field has inline doc
- [ ] `drain_commit_oid_map()` has full function doc with call-after-join contract
- [ ] `emit_git` has inline comment explaining interception logic
- [ ] Module-level doc updated
- [ ] Call site in distributed.rs has inline comment
- [ ] TODO at distributed.rs:2782-2785 updated
- [ ] All comments comply with comment policy (no tracking IDs, no temporal narration)

## Performance Considerations

**Allocation tier: WARM.** Per-repo-lease wrapper, not inner loop. Drain point is post-scan, single-threaded.

- **Mutex contention: negligible.** CommitMeta events deduplicated upstream via `AtomicBitSet::test_and_set`.
- **HashMap growth: bounded.** Cardinality = unique commits with findings (<<1,000 per scan). ~36 bytes per entry.
- **Lock hold time: minimal.** Drop guard before `inner.emit_git()` to avoid holding lock across downstream calls.
- **No false sharing risk.** `finding_count: AtomicU64` and `commit_oid_map: Mutex<HashMap>` written on different event kinds.
- **No benchmark gating required.** WARM-tier change with no hot-path impact.

## Related Work

title: Implement Git finding translation: OwnedCoreEvent::Finding to FindingRecord/OccurrenceRecord/ObservationRecord
description:
## Context

The distributed Git worker captures finding events via `FindingsCaptureSink` and drains them after scan completion, but `persist_git_repo_findings_and_done_ledger` currently submits an **empty** `FindingsUpsertBatch` — all Git scan findings are permanently lost. This is the most critical data-loss gap in the scanner: findings are detected, logged in telemetry, then discarded before reaching the persistence layer.

With gossip-9579 (norm_hash in events) and gossip-9580 (commit_id → commit_oid mapping) landed, all data needed for the 3-tier persistence identity chain will be available at the translation boundary. This task implements the actual translation logic and wires it into the distributed runtime.

## Current State

`persist_git_repo_findings_and_done_ledger` (distributed.rs:2758-2777) submits an empty batch:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:2780-2791
let batch = FindingsUpsertBatch::new(&[], &[], &[]);
let handle = persistence
    .findings_sink
    .upsert_batch(batch)
    .map_err(|error| { /* ... */ })?;
```

Captured findings are drained and counted but never translated (distributed.rs:3031-3049):

```rust
let captured_findings = capture_sink.drain_findings();
let detected_count = captured_findings.len();

if detected_count > 0 {
    tracing::warn!(
        shard_id = %lease.shard_id(),
        detected_count,
        "git repo scan detected findings but translation to durable persistence \
         records is not yet implemented; findings are captured in telemetry only"
    );
}
```

The filesystem path has a working translation in `translate_item_result` (result_translation.rs:281-348) and `translate_findings` (result_translation.rs:350-423). These produce `FindingRecord`, `OccurrenceRecord`, and `ObservationRecord` from `FsFindingRecord` inputs.

## Desired State

A new `translate_git_findings` function translates `Vec<OwnedCoreEvent>` (with `norm_hash`) plus the `commit_id → OidBytes` map into `Vec<FindingRecord>`, `Vec<OccurrenceRecord>`, and `Vec<ObservationRecord>`. The `persist_git_repo_findings_and_done_ledger` function accepts these captured findings and the commit_oid map, calls the translation, and submits a real `FindingsUpsertBatch`. The done-ledger entry reflects the actual finding count.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_translation.rs` (or new `git_result_translation.rs`) | Add `translate_git_findings` function | Core translation logic: map `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` → 3-tier persistence records |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | (1) Update `persist_git_repo_findings_and_done_ledger` signature to accept captured findings + commit_oid_map; (2) Call `translate_git_findings`; (3) Submit real batch; (4) Pass real `findings_count` to done-ledger; (5) Remove warning log about missing translation | Wire translation into the runtime |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Update `run_git_repo_lease` to pass `captured_findings` and `commit_oid_map` to persist function | Connect capture to translation |

### Critical Prerequisite — Resolve the norm_hash Data Gap

`OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` does not carry `norm_hash`, `key_secret_hash`, or other fields required for `FindingRecord` construction. The translation function cannot operate on raw captured events alone.

**Recommended approach**: Intercept finding data from `FinalizeOutput.data_ops` after the finalize builder commits findings to the persistence backend. The finalize builder already computes `norm_hash` and writes complete finding records at `NS_FINDING` keys. Extract these from the `data_ops` vec before (or instead of) writing to the backend, and feed them into the translation function. This keeps the change local to `gossip-scanner-runtime` with no cross-crate modifications.

**Alternative (not recommended)**: Extend `FindingEvent`/`OwnedCoreEvent` to carry `norm_hash` — requires cross-crate schema changes touching `scanner-scheduler`, `scanner-git`, and `gossip-scanner-runtime`.

### Identity Derivation Design

The 3-tier model requires these identifiers per finding:

**1. `StableItemId`** — represents "what item was scanned":
- For Git: derive from `(repo_id, object_path)` — the blob's location within the repo.
- Use `ItemIdentityKey` with `ConnectorTag("git")`, `ConnectorInstanceIdHash` from repo_id, and `locator = object_path`.
- Note: the done-ledger already uses repo_id zero-padded to 32 bytes for StableItemId (git_persistence.rs:820-826). Per-finding StableItemId should be more granular (per-blob, not per-repo). Do NOT use `StableItemId::from_bytes(zero_padded_repo_id)` — that is repo-level identity only.

**Exact contract:**
```
StableItemId = ItemIdentityKey {
    connector_tag: ConnectorTag("git"),
    connector_instance_id_hash: ConnectorInstanceIdHash(..),
    locator: CanonicalBytes(repo_id ++ object_path),
}.stable_id()
```

**2. `ObjectVersionId`** — represents "which version of that item":
- For Git: derive from `commit_oid + object_path` per the contracts documentation: `blake3(commit_sha ++ tree_sha_for_path)` (item.rs:498-499).
- Use `ObjectVersionId::from_version_bytes(&composite)` where `composite = commit_oid_bytes ++ object_path_bytes`.
- Resolve `commit_id` ordinal → `OidBytes` via the commit_oid_map from gossip-9580.
- `commit_id: None` and `commit_id` not in `oid_map` are both **hard errors** — Git findings require commit provenance. Do not silently skip.

**Exact contract:**
```
ObjectVersionId = ObjectVersionId::from_version_bytes(
    CanonicalBytes(commit_oid ++ object_path)
)
```

**3. `SecretHash`** — derived from `NormHash` + `TenantSecretKey`:
- `NormHash::from_digest(finding.norm_hash.unwrap())` — requires gossip-9579 landed.
- `key_secret_hash(&tenant_secret_key, &norm_hash)` — same as FS path (result_translation.rs:386).

**4. `RuleFingerprint`** — derived from rule name:
- `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` has `rule_name: String`.
- Derive via `RuleFingerprint::from_rule_name(&rule_name)` or the same `rule_fingerprint(rule_id)` callback pattern from `ReceiptCommitSink`.

**5. `OvidHash`** — derived from `(StableItemId, VersionId)`:
- Same as FS path: `derive_ovid_hash(&OvidHashInputs { stable_item_id, version: VersionId::Strong(object_version_id) })`.
- **Critical grouping requirement**: Findings must be grouped by `(object_path, commit_id)` before OvidHash derivation. A single captured array may contain findings across multiple objects and commits. Each unique `(object_path, commit_id)` pair gets its own OvidHash, ObservationRecord, and set of OccurrenceRecords.

### Translation Function Sketch

```rust
/// Context struct to reduce positional parameter count and prevent u64 mixups.
struct GitTranslationContext<'a> {
    repo_id: u64,
    connector_instance_id_hash: ConnectorInstanceIdHash,
    commit_oid_map: &'a HashMap<u32, OidBytes>,
    write_context: &'a WriteContext,
    tenant_secret_key: &'a TenantSecretKey,
    // ... other fields
}

fn translate_git_findings(
    ctx: &GitTranslationContext<'_>,
    captured: &[OwnedCoreEvent],
    rule_fingerprint: &dyn Fn(u32) -> RuleFingerprint,
    seen_at: LogicalTime,
) -> Result<FindingsLayers> {
    // Group findings by (object_path, commit_id)
    // For each group:
    //   1. Derive StableItemId from (repo_id, object_path) via ItemIdentityKey
    //   2. Derive ObjectVersionId from (commit_oid, object_path)
    //   3. Derive OvidHash from (StableItemId, VersionId)
    //   4. For each finding in group:
    //      a. Derive SecretHash from (norm_hash, tenant_secret_key)
    //      b. Derive RuleFingerprint from rule_id
    //      c. Construct FindingRecord, OccurrenceRecord, ObservationRecord
    //   5. Deduplicate via three HashSets (same pattern as FS translate_findings)
    // Validate: validate_referential_integrity + validate_observation_identity
}
```

### CommitMeta Capture

Add `Mutex<HashMap<u32, OidBytes>>` to `FindingsCaptureSink` to capture `GitEvent::CommitMeta` mappings. This is the only sink modification needed for commit_oid_map data. Finding data comes from `FinalizeOutput`, not from the capture sink.

### Patterns to Follow

Mirror `translate_findings` (result_translation.rs:350-423):
- Validate span: `end > start`, derive `byte_offset = start`, `byte_length = end - start`
- Use `NormHash::from_digest` → `key_secret_hash` → `FindingRecord::new`
- Use `OccurrenceRecord::try_new` (validates `byte_length > 0`)
- Use `ObservationRecord::from_write_context`
- Derive `OvidHash` for each finding
- Three-`HashSet` dedup loop (by FindingId, OccurrenceId, ObservationId)
- Return type: use existing `FindingsLayers` alias (result_translation.rs:36-40)
- Call `validate_observation_identity` + `validate_referential_integrity` before returning

Consider extracting the shared dedup+record-construction loop into a helper parameterized by data source if the FS and Git paths share >60% logic. Assess after initial implementation.

### Utilities to Reuse

- `NormHash::from_digest` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/finding.rs)
- `key_secret_hash` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/finding.rs)
- `derive_finding_id` / `FindingRecord::new` (persistence/findings.rs:79-98)
- `OccurrenceRecord::try_new` (persistence/findings.rs:186-200)
- `ObservationRecord::from_write_context` (persistence/findings.rs:362-377)
- `derive_ovid_hash` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs)
- `ObjectVersionId::from_version_bytes` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs:528-548)
- `ItemIdentityKey::stable_id()` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs:446-450)
- `domain_hasher` + `CanonicalBytes` (gossip-contracts/src/identity/canonical.rs)
- `ResultTranslationError` variants (result_translation.rs:244-263)

### Blast Radius

- Done-ledger `findings_count` changes from 0 to real count — affects `gossip-9570` fix

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- Do NOT use `commit_id` ordinal directly as version identity — ordinals are positional and unstable across re-scans
- Do NOT use `object_path` alone as `StableItemId` — must include connector/repo context to prevent cross-repo collision
- Do NOT use `StableItemId::from_bytes(zero_padded_repo_id)` for per-blob findings — that's repo-level only
- Do NOT carry raw secret bytes — use `NormHash` (BLAKE3 digest) only
- Do NOT duplicate `translate_findings` logic — extract shared helpers if >60% overlap
- Do NOT clone `OwnedCoreEvent` during translation — destructure by value/move
- Do NOT add `prefix_scan` to `GitPersistenceBackend` trait — intercept `FinalizeOutput` instead
- Do NOT extend `FindingEvent`/`OwnedCoreEvent` with `norm_hash` — cross-crate scope creep

## Design Notes

### StableItemId Granularity

The done-ledger uses a repo-level `StableItemId` (derived from `repo_id` alone). Per-finding `StableItemId` must be per-blob (derived from `repo_id + object_path`) because multiple findings in different files within the same repo must have distinct `FindingId` values. The `FindingId` derivation includes `StableItemId`, so repo-level granularity would conflate findings from different blobs.

### Handling Missing norm_hash

If `OwnedCoreEvent::Finding` has `norm_hash: None` (e.g., events captured before gossip-9579 lands, or events from non-Git sources), the translation should skip that finding with a warning log. This makes the translation forward-compatible.

### Capacity Overflow

`FindingsCaptureSink` drops findings beyond `capacity` (coordination_sink.rs:236). Dropped findings still reach telemetry but are NOT in the persistence batch. This is an accepted data loss vector bounded by scan budget configuration. Log the delta between detected_count (telemetry) and persisted_count (batch) if they differ.

|------|-----------|--------|-----------|
| Identity instability across re-scans (wrong ObjectVersionId) | Medium | High | Use commit_oid (stable) not commit_id ordinal (unstable); test with re-scan scenarios |
| Cross-repo StableItemId collision | Low | High | Include repo_id in StableItemId derivation; use domain-separated hasher |
| Finding count mismatch (telemetry vs persistence) | Medium | Low | Log delta between capture count and persisted count |
| Translation error leaves empty batch | Medium | High | Return error on translation failure; do not submit partial batch |

description:
## Context

The cooperative cancellation infrastructure is fully wired through the distributed
and local-CLI scan paths, but the `GitRepoExecutor` trait — the connector-mode
entry point — has no abort parameter. Its sole real implementation
(`ScannerGitExecutor::run_repo`) creates a local `AtomicBool::new(false)` that
nobody can ever set, making connector-mode scans uncancellable.

This gap was identified during review of the `feature/git-caller-owned-abort` branch
which added caller-owned abort signaling throughout scanner-git.

## Current State

The trait accepts no abort signal:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:818-826
pub trait GitRepoExecutor: Send {
    fn run_repo(
        &mut self,
        mirror: &LocalMirror,
        selection: &GitSelection,
        limits: GitExecutionLimits,
    ) -> Result<GitRunOutcome, GitRunError>;
}
```

The impl creates a dead abort flag:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs:221-224
let abort = AtomicBool::new(false);
self.execute_repo_with(mirror, selection, limits, [0; 32], &abort, run_scan)
    .map(git_run_outcome)
```

The distributed path correctly wires a real `CancellationToken`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs:238-246
pub(crate) fn run_repo_with_persistence<B>(
    &self,
    mirror: &LocalMirror,
    selection: &GitSelection,
    limits: GitExecutionLimits,
    policy_hash: [u8; 32],
    abort: &AtomicBool,               // caller-owned abort
    persistence: &GitPersistenceAdapter<B>,
) -> Result<GitRunExecution, GitRunError>
```

## Desired State

`GitRepoExecutor::run_repo` accepts `abort: &AtomicBool` so callers can cancel
connector-mode scans. The internal plumbing already accepts `&AtomicBool` — this
is pure parameter threading.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:820` | Add `abort: &AtomicBool` to `run_repo` signature | Trait method gains cancellation |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:877` | Update `StubExecutor::run_repo` test stub | Trait impl match |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs:1086` | Verify object-safety assertion still holds | `&AtomicBool` is object-safe |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs:274-291` | Forward `abort` through `impl GitRepoExecutor` | Wire real signal |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs:205-224` | `run_repo_with` accepts `abort: &AtomicBool` instead of creating local | Remove dead flag |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/git_executor.rs:672-686` | Update test call to pass `&AtomicBool::new(false)` | Test compilation |

### Patterns to Follow

The distributed path already demonstrates the pattern. `CancellationToken::as_atomic()`
(at `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:264-267`) bridges the runtime-level
token to scanner-git's `&AtomicBool` interface.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `CancellationToken::as_atomic()` | `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:264` | Callers pass `token.as_atomic()` to `run_repo` |

### Type Choice

Use `&AtomicBool` (not `CancellationToken`) because:
- `gossip-contracts` has zero runtime dependencies
- `scanner-git` uses `&AtomicBool` throughout
- `execute_repo_with` already accepts `&AtomicBool`
- `CancellationToken::as_atomic()` provides the bridge at call sites

### Blast Radius

Small. Only two `impl GitRepoExecutor` blocks exist (one real, one test stub),
and only one test calls `.run_repo()` directly. The distributed and local-CLI
paths bypass the trait and already have proper cancellation.

Add directory validation for Fs source in DistributedWorkerConfig::new
description:
## Context

DistributedWorkerConfig::new() validates directory-ness only for Git mirror_root (line 830), not for Fs source paths. An Fs source constructed directly (bypassing the resolution path) can hold a non-directory path and will fail deep in the scan loop rather than at config validation.

## Current State

The constructor at crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:829 only validates Git:

```rust
if let DistributedSourceSettings::Git(source) = &source {
    validate_directory_exists("mirror_root", source.mirror_root())?;
}
```

The Fs resolution path calls validate_path_exists (existence only, line 1529) but the constructor has no Fs validation at all.

## Desired State

The constructor should also validate that Fs source paths exist and are directories, matching the Git validation pattern. Distributed scanning always walks directory trees; a file path would fail inside the scan loop with a confusing error. Single-file Fs scanning is not intentional for distributed mode.

## Implementation Guidance

### Core Change

Replace the `if let` at config.rs:829-831 with an exhaustive `match` on `DistributedSourceSettings`:

```rust
match &source {
    DistributedSourceSettings::Git(source) => {
        validate_directory_exists("mirror_root", source.mirror_root())?;
    }
    DistributedSourceSettings::Fs(source) => {
        validate_directory_exists("path", source.path())?;
    }
}
```

### Key Decisions

- **Use `validate_directory_exists` (config.rs:1660), NOT `validate_path_exists`**: The former checks existence + directory-ness + dangling symlinks with clear errors. The latter only checks existence.
- **Use exhaustive `match` instead of `if let`**: Ensures future `DistributedSourceSettings` variants get a compiler error if validation is forgotten.
- **Fs field name is `"path"`**: Matches the field name used in `validate_path_exists` calls in the resolution pipeline (config.rs:1530).
- **Do NOT create new helper functions**: Reuse existing `validate_directory_exists` directly.

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- Using `validate_path_exists` for Fs (only checks existence, not directory-ness)
- Keeping `if let` (silently skips new enum variants)
- Adding a separate `validate_fs_path` helper (duplicates existing utility)

### Allocation Tier

COLD (constructor called once at startup). Optimize for clarity, no allocation constraints.

### Documentation Updates Required

1. **DistributedWorkerConfig::new doc comment** (config.rs:802-813): Add Fs source validation to the Errors section. Change to: "or when a distributed source (Git or filesystem) points at a path that is missing from the local host, is a dangling symlink, or is not a directory."
2. **DistributedSourceSettings enum doc** (config.rs:477-482): Add that Fs paths must also be existing directories, not just Git mirror_root.
3. **FsSourceSettings::new doc** (config.rs:211-216): No change needed — it correctly states "does not validate the path" since validation occurs at the DistributedWorkerConfig level.

## Code References

- Constructor to modify: `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:814-839`
- Git validation (pattern to match): `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:829-831`
- `validate_directory_exists` helper: `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:1660-1700`
- `validate_path_exists` helper (do NOT use): `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:1644-1658`
- `FsSourceSettings` type: `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:202-314`
- `DistributedSourceSettings` enum: `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:477-489`
- Existing Git test (pattern for new tests): `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:2353-2401`
- Existing dangling symlink test (pattern): `crates/gossip-worker/src/config.rs:2403-2453`

## Testing Strategy

### Existing Coverage

| Behavior | Test | Location |
|----------|------|----------|
| Git mirror_root non-directory | `distributed_config_rejects_git_mirror_root_that_is_not_a_directory` | config.rs:2353 |
| Git mirror_root dangling symlink | `distributed_config_rejects_dangling_symlink_mirror_root` | config.rs:2403 |

### Required Tests

**1. `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_that_is_not_a_directory`** (MUST)
- Create a tempdir, write a sentinel file, pass that file path as Fs source
- Assert `WorkerConfigError::InvalidValue { field: "path", reason containing "not a directory" }`
- Follow the exact pattern of the Git test at config.rs:2353-2401

```rust
#[test]
fn distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_that_is_not_a_directory() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
    let file_path = dir.path().join("not-a-directory");
    std::fs::write(&file_path, "sentinel").expect("write sentinel file");

    let backends = ProductionBackendConfig::new(
        EtcdCoordinatorConfig::localhost(),
        "host=127.0.0.1 dbname=done",
        "host=127.0.0.1 dbname=findings",
    )
    .expect("backend config should be valid");
    let identity = WorkerIdentityConfig::new(
        TenantId::from_bytes([0x11; 32]),
        RunId::from_raw(1),
        WorkerId::from_raw(1),
        PolicyHash::from_bytes([0x22; 32]),
        TenantSecretKey::from_bytes([0x33; 32]),
    )
    .expect("identity should be valid");
    let runtime = DistributedWorkerRuntimeSettings::new(
        ScanBudgets::default(),
        DistributedRuntimeConfig::default().commit_queue_capacity,
    );

    let err = DistributedWorkerConfig::new(
        backends,
        ProductionStartupSettings::validate_only(),
        identity,
        DistributedSourceSettings::Fs(FsSourceSettings::new(&file_path)),
        runtime,
    )
    .expect_err("non-directory Fs source path must be rejected");

    assert!(
        matches!(
            err,
            WorkerConfigError::InvalidValue {
                field: "path",
                ref reason,
                ..
            } if reason.contains("not a directory")
        ),
        "expected InvalidValue for path with not a directory reason, got: {err:?}"
    );
}
```

**2. `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_nonexistent_path`** (MUST)
- Pass a nonexistent path as Fs source
- Assert `WorkerConfigError::InvalidValue { field: "path", reason containing "does not exist" }`

**3. `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_dangling_symlink`** (SHOULD, #[cfg(unix)])
- Create a dangling symlink, pass as Fs source
- Assert error mentions "symlink" and "target does not exist"
- Follow pattern of config.rs:2403-2453

**4. `distributed_config_accepts_fs_source_directory`** (SHOULD)
- Create a real tempdir, pass as Fs source with valid backends/identity/runtime
- Assert Ok(config) is returned

### Do NOT Test (Already Covered)

| Behavior | Covered By |
|----------|-----------|
| Git mirror_root non-directory rejection | Existing test at config.rs:2353 |
| Git mirror_root dangling symlink rejection | Existing test at config.rs:2403 |
| Budget validation | Multiple existing tests in config.rs |

### Test Dependencies
No new dependencies. Tests use tempfile (already in dev-dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fs source paths validated with `validate_directory_exists` in `DistributedWorkerConfig::new`
- [ ] `if let` replaced with exhaustive `match` on `DistributedSourceSettings`
- [ ] `DistributedWorkerConfig::new` doc comment Errors section covers Fs validation
- [ ] `DistributedSourceSettings` doc comment mentions Fs directory requirement
- [ ] Test: `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_that_is_not_a_directory` passes
- [ ] Test: `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_nonexistent_path` passes
- [ ] Test: `distributed_config_rejects_fs_source_dangling_symlink` passes (unix)
- [ ] Test: `distributed_config_accepts_fs_source_directory` passes
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-worker` passes

## Recommended Skills

Invoke these skills during and after implementation for best results.

| Phase | Skill | When to Invoke | Why |
|-------|-------|---------------|-----|
| After | `/doc-rigor` | After all code and doc changes | Verify doc claims match new validation behavior |

## Pointers

- Check `FsScanConfig::new()` in the scanner-engine crate if questions arise about whether Fs paths can be files (they cannot — it walks directories)
- The resolution pipeline at config.rs:1528-1538 shows how Fs sources are built in the normal path

title: Consolidate workspace-wide git test helpers into single source of truth
description:
## Context

At least 11 independent `run_git`/`git_output`/`run_git_in`/`init_git_repo`/`git_available`/`decode_hex` helper functions exist across test files in 5 crates. Each copy reimplements the same Command::new("git") + assert-success pattern with minor variations in error formatting and invocation style (`-C dir` flag vs `current_dir()`). This duplication violates the single-source-of-truth principle and creates maintenance drift risk.

## Current State

### Canonical helpers (gossip-scanner-runtime::test_fixtures)

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/test_fixtures.rs:56-109
fn assert_git_output(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output { .. }
pub fn run_git_in(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) { .. }
pub fn run_git_in_stdout(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String { .. }
pub fn init_git_repo(dir: &Path, email: &str, name: &str) { .. }
```

Exported under `test-support` feature. Uses `-C dir` flag, provides detailed error messages with stdout/stderr dumps.

### Duplicate locations (11 total across 5 crates)

| # | Crate | File:Line | Functions | Style |
|---|-------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| 1 | gossip-connectors | `src/git_tests.rs:22-37` | `run_git` | `-C dir` |
| 2 | gossip-orchestrator | `src/test_support.rs:14-35` | `run_git_in`, `init_git_repo` | `-C dir` (identical to canonical) |
| 3 | scanner-git | `src/repo_identity.rs:200-238` | `run_git_in`, `run_git` (bare), `init_repo` | `-C dir` + bare args |
| 4 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_scan_validation.rs:45-63` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 5 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_tree_diff.rs:50-68` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 6 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_pack_exec.rs:53-61` | `run_git` | `-C dir` |
| 7 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_snapshot.rs:25-42` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 8 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_commit_walk.rs:31-48` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 9 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/integration/git_inmem_artifacts.rs:38-55` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 10 | scanner-engine-integration-tests | `tests/simulation/git_scan_shallow_limits.rs:26-43` | `run_git`, `git_output` | `current_dir()` |
| 11 | (canonical) gossip-scanner-runtime | `src/test_fixtures.rs:56-109` | See above | `-C dir` |

### Additional duplicated helpers

- `git_available()` — 5 copies across scanner-engine-integration-tests test files (git_scan_validation:40, git_tree_diff:34, git_snapshot:21, git_commit_walk:27, git_inmem_artifacts:34, git_scan_shallow_limits:22)
- `decode_hex()` — 5 copies across scanner-engine-integration-tests test files (git_tree_diff:71, git_scan_validation:66, git_snapshot:44, git_commit_walk:50, git_inmem_artifacts:57, git_scan_shallow_limits:45)

## Desired State

One canonical set of git test helpers shared across all 5 crates. Each duplicate replaced by an import from the canonical module. Zero local `fn run_git`-style helpers remaining in test files.

## Implementation Guidance

### Critical dependency constraint

```
gossip-scanner-runtime depends on:
  ├── gossip-connectors
  ├── gossip-orchestrator
  └── scanner-git
```

gossip-connectors, gossip-orchestrator, and scanner-git CANNOT depend on gossip-scanner-runtime (circular dependency). The helpers must be relocated to a crate lower in the dependency graph.

### Recommended approach: Move helpers to scanner-git behind test-support feature

**Why scanner-git:**
- Already depended on by gossip-connectors (Cargo.toml:19), gossip-orchestrator (Cargo.toml:14), and scanner-engine-integration-tests (Cargo.toml:42)
- Git CLI helpers are semantically related to the git scanning crate
- The helpers use only `std::process::Command` and `std::path::Path` — zero project-specific dependencies
- scanner-git already has a rich feature set in its Cargo.toml

**Step-by-step migration order:**

1. **Create `scanner-git/src/test_helpers.rs`** — Add a new module gated behind `test-support` feature:
   ```rust
   //! Shared git CLI helpers for test fixtures across the workspace.
   //!
   //! Provides fire-and-forget command execution, stdout capture, repository
   //! initialization, git-availability probing, and hex decoding. All functions
   //! panic on failure — appropriate for test setup, not production code.

   pub fn run_git_in(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) { .. }
   pub fn run_git_in_stdout(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String { .. }
   pub fn init_git_repo(dir: &Path, email: &str, name: &str) { .. }
   pub fn git_available() -> bool { .. }
   pub fn decode_hex(hex: &str) -> Vec<u8> { .. }
   ```
   Use the `-C dir` invocation style (more explicit, matches canonical). Keep detailed error messages from gossip-scanner-runtime version.

2. **Add `test-support` feature to `scanner-git/Cargo.toml`:**
   ```toml
   [features]
   test-support = []
   ```
   Gate the module: `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")] pub mod test_helpers;`

3. **Update gossip-scanner-runtime test_fixtures.rs** — Replace the git helper implementations with re-exports from scanner-git:
   ```rust
   pub use scanner_git::test_helpers::{run_git_in, run_git_in_stdout, init_git_repo};
   ```
   (gossip-scanner-runtime already depends on scanner-git)

4. **Update gossip-connectors** — Add `scanner-git = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }` to `[dev-dependencies]` (it already has scanner-git in [dependencies], just add test-support for dev). Replace `git_tests::run_git` with import.

5. **Update gossip-orchestrator** — Add `scanner-git = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }` to `[dev-dependencies]` (scanner-git is already in [dependencies]). Delete `test_support::run_git_in` and `init_git_repo`, replace with imports.

6. **Update scanner-engine-integration-tests** — Add `scanner-git = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }` to dev-deps (scanner-git already in dev-deps, just add feature). Create a shared `test_util` module in `tests/integration/` or `tests/common/` that re-exports from scanner-git. Replace all per-file `run_git`/`git_output`/`git_available`/`decode_hex` with imports.

7. **Update scanner-git internal tests** — `repo_identity.rs` tests can use `crate::test_helpers::*` directly (module is in the same crate).

8. **Delete all duplicate implementations** — Remove the old functions from every file listed in the duplicates table.

### Signature unification

The `current_dir()` variants (scanner-engine-integration-tests) pass args directly, while the `-C dir` variants pass dir separately. The canonical `-C dir` style is preferred because:
- More explicit about which directory the command targets
- Works correctly even if `current_dir()` changes between calls
- Matches how the canonical helpers already work

For callers that used `current_dir()` style, the migration is straightforward — the function signature is identical: `fn(dir: &Path, args: &[&str])`.

### Allocation tier

All helpers are COLD (test setup/teardown). No allocation constraints apply.

## Code References

```rust
// Canonical implementation — crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/test_fixtures.rs:56-78
fn assert_git_output(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {
    let output = Command::new("git")
        .arg("-C")
        .arg(dir)
        .args(args)
        .output()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            panic!("failed to spawn git -C {} {}: {e}", dir.display(), args.join(" "))
        });
    assert!(output.status.success(),
        "git command failed: git -C {} {}\nstdout:{}\nstderr:{}",
        dir.display(), args.join(" "),
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));
    output
}
```

```rust
// Typical duplicate — crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/integration/git_tree_diff.rs:50-57
fn run_git(repo: &Path, args: &[&str]) {
    let status = Command::new("git")
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(repo)
        .status()
        .expect("failed to run git");
    assert!(status.success(), "git command failed: {args:?}");
}
```

## Testing Strategy

No new tests needed — this is a pure refactoring task. Existing test suites validate correctness:

| Test suite | Command | What it validates |
|------------|---------|-------------------|
| scanner-git unit tests | `cargo test -p scanner-git` | repo_identity tests still pass with shared helpers |
| gossip-connectors tests | `cargo test -p gossip-connectors` | git_tests still create repos correctly |
| gossip-orchestrator tests | `cargo test -p gossip-orchestrator` | git_request tests still pass |
| Integration tests | `cargo test -p scanner-engine-integration-tests --features integration-tests --test integration` | All git_* integration tests pass |
| Simulation tests | `cargo test -p scanner-engine-integration-tests --features sim-harness --test simulation` | git_scan_shallow_limits passes |
| Runtime tests | `cargo test -p gossip-scanner-runtime` | Re-exported helpers work correctly |

**Do NOT test:** The helper functions themselves do not need unit tests — they are test infrastructure that panics on failure by design.

## Documentation Requirements

| Item | Scope | Must Cover |
|------|-------|------------|
| `scanner-git::test_helpers` module | Module-level doc | Purpose, what it provides, that it panics on failure |
| `run_git_in` | Function doc | What it does, panics if git command fails |
| `run_git_in_stdout` | Function doc | Returns trimmed stdout, panics on non-UTF-8 or failure |
| `init_git_repo` | Function doc | Creates repo with `-b main`, configures author identity |
| `git_available` | Function doc | Probes for git CLI on PATH |
| `decode_hex` | Function doc | Converts hex ASCII to bytes, panics on odd-length input |

Pattern to follow: the existing docs in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/test_fixtures.rs:54-55,80-81,85,100-104` are good examples.

## Performance Considerations

None. All code is COLD-tier test infrastructure. No allocation, latency, or throughput constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single `test_helpers` module in scanner-git behind `test-support` feature exports `run_git_in`, `run_git_in_stdout`, `init_git_repo`, `git_available`, `decode_hex`
- [ ] All 10 duplicate locations replaced with imports from scanner-git::test_helpers
- [ ] gossip-scanner-runtime::test_fixtures re-exports scanner-git helpers (backward compat for existing callers)
- [ ] Zero `fn run_git` / `fn git_output` / `fn run_git_in` local definitions remain in test files
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes
- [ ] `cargo check` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p scanner-git` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-connectors` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-orchestrator` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-scanner-runtime` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p scanner-engine-integration-tests --features integration-tests --test integration` passes
- [ ] No new crate dependencies introduced (only feature additions to existing deps)

## Recommended Skills

Invoke these skills during and after implementation:

| Phase | Skill | When to Invoke | Why |
|-------|-------|---------------|-----|
| After | `/dedup-audit` | After migration complete | Verify no remaining duplicates were missed |
| After | `/doc-rigor` | After writing test_helpers module | Verify documentation accuracy |

## Pointers

- Canonical implementation: `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/test_fixtures.rs:54-109`
- Dependency graph: `gossip-scanner-runtime` depends on scanner-git, gossip-connectors, gossip-orchestrator (so helpers must flow DOWN, not UP)
- Feature flag pattern: see `gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml` `test-support = ["dep:proptest"]` for prior art
- Integration test harness structure: `crates/scanner-engine-integration-tests/tests/integration/main.rs` lists all modules
